title: Medicine Hat College Student Awards
audience: Students starting or continuing at Medicine Hat College
notes: MHC's own award page says applications for the next round open March 1, 2027 and does not publish a closing date. Individual award amounts are not published.
description: Medicine Hat College hands out more than $400,000 a year in scholarships and bursaries to new, continuing and returning students. Some are marked on grades, some on financial need, and many on both. One online form enters you for every award you qualify for, so you do not apply to them individually.
metaDetail: One form enters you for every award you qualify for.

title: South Country Co-op Scholarship
audience: High school students in the South Country Co-op trading area
notes: The Co-op's page sets the deadline as July 31 of each year, so this repeats annually. Your family has to be a member in good standing and have bought at least $2,000 from the Co-op in the current fiscal year, so check with whoever holds the membership before you write the essay.
description: South Country Co-op gives $1,000 to a student from a member family graduating from a high school in its trading area. You need proof of acceptance and paid registration at a post-secondary institution, a 500 word essay on your community involvement, and two or more reference letters about it.
metaDetail: Needs a family Co-op membership.

title: Alberta Indigenous Careers Award
audience: Indigenous students enrolled full-time at an Alberta post-secondary school
notes: Apply through the Student Awards office at your post-secondary school. Deadlines vary by school, so ask as soon as you have your acceptance.
description: Worth $2,000 per term and up to $4,000 an academic year for Indigenous students enrolled full-time in a certificate, diploma, applied degree or bachelor program in Alberta. You need at least a 60 percent course load, or 40 percent with a documented disability, and satisfactory academic standing.
metaDetail: Apply through your post-secondary Student Awards office.

title: RE/MAX Quest for Excellence
audience: Grade 12 students anywhere in Canada except Quebec
notes: Dates and terms confirmed against RE/MAX's own Official Rules on 2026-09-08: the program opens August 24, 2026 and closes March 15, 2027, and forty applicants each receive $1,000. Two things the rules make plain that the marketing does not. Winners are picked by random drawing among entries that clear the essay bar, not ranked on merit, so a strong essay improves nothing beyond eligibility. And residents of Quebec are excluded, as are students finishing through high school equivalency courses. The essay must be at least 500 words on one of three themes: what home means to you, leadership or charity in your community, or a dream you hope to achieve. The /quest-for-excellence/ landing page carries the submission form while a cycle is open and 404s between cycles, so this points at the rules page, which stays up year-round.

items.text: An online submission form
An essay of at least 500 words on one of three themes, as a PDF or DOCX
The 40 winners are drawn at random from eligible entries

description: RE/MAX awards forty $1,000 scholarships to Grade 12 students across Canada who submit an essay on one of three set themes. Recipients are drawn at random from all eligible entries.
metaDetail: Forty $1,000 awards, drawn at random from eligible entries.

title: Alexander Rutherford Scholarship
audience: Alberta high school students based on academic averages
description: Alberta's flagship high school scholarship, worth up to $2,500 depending on your averages in Grades 10 through 12. If you only apply for one thing on this site, apply for this.
metaDetail: Applications open August 1 with no closing deadline.
notes: Alberta Student Aid names Lloydminster as a border community: all students living there are eligible, whether the Alberta side or the Saskatchewan side, provided they attend Holy Rosary High School or Lloydminster Comprehensive High School. Your courses still have to line up with the Alberta curriculum, so ask about your transcript early.

items.text: A verified Alberta Student Aid account, which asks for your SIN
Your Alberta Student Number, from your transcript
You apply once your final marks are in and you are enrolled full-time after high school. No essay or references.

evidence.summary: Apply when official high-school marks are available and full-time post-secondary enrollment has begun.
Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons may qualify; visa students do not.

requirements.explanation: Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons may qualify; visa students do not.

evidence.summary: Residence duration and family alternatives need provider verification.

condition.text: Check the applicant or parent/guardian residence alternatives and residence during each claimed high-school grade.

requirements.explanation: Residence duration and family alternatives need provider verification.

evidence.summary: The provider must assess the transcript, study program and remaining application conditions.

condition.text: Check designated course averages, transcript and graduation timing, eligible full-time undergraduate or apprenticeship enrollment, valid SIN, and the once-only award restriction. Graduate and specified professional programs are excluded.

requirements.explanation: The provider must assess the transcript, study program and remaining application conditions.

coverageEvidence.summary: Supported criteria checked; remaining provider conditions require manual verification.

title: Cypress County Agricultural Service Board Bursary
audience: Cypress County and Medicine Hat students in agriculture, agri-tech or environment
notes: The residency rule is wider than the County's name suggests: the application form counts residents of urban areas inside the County's outer boundaries, and names the City of Medicine Hat and the Town of Redcliff outright, so a student living in the city qualifies. That is the opposite of the County Council scholarship that closes the same day, which turns on living in the County itself. Environmental programmes count alongside agriculture, which widens this well past farm kids. You can win it only once, and you need last year's marks plus a letter of acceptance.

items.text: The county's online application form

description: Cypress County awards two $1,000 bursaries a year to students continuing at a college or university in an in-depth agricultural, agri-tech or environmental programme. Applications and supporting documents go to the County's agricultural fieldman, and the board decides on scholastic standing alongside social and community involvement.
metaDetail: Two each calendar year.

title: Servus Credit Union Young Adult Scholarship
audience: Servus Credit Union members entering post-secondary
notes: The link goes to the Servus home page because Servus does not keep a standing scholarship page. Ask your counsellor or your local branch whether this is running before you plan on it.
description: Servus Credit Union offers this $1,500 scholarship to support members who are entering post-secondary education. Applicants must be Servus Credit Union members in good standing. Contact your school guidance counsellor for application details.
metaDetail: You must already be a Servus member in good standing.

title: ATB Financial Bursary
audience: Indigenous students from Alberta in or heading into post-secondary
notes: Part of Indspire's Building Brighter Futures. One application covers every Indspire award you qualify for, and it stays in the running for all three cutoffs: August 1, November 1 and February 1 at 11:59 p.m. EST. Apply at indspire.microsoftcrmportals.com and use one account only.

items.text: One Indspire application covers all of Indspire's bursaries

description: ATB Financial funds Indigenous students at colleges, universities, technical colleges and apprenticeship programs across Canada. Demonstrated financial need is the main thing they weigh, then community involvement and academic record. First preference goes to Alberta students entering finance, commerce, technology or Indigenous studies, but other programs are eligible. Indspire does not publish a set dollar amount for this one.
metaDetail: One Indspire form covers every award.

title: ATA Local 21 Scholarship
audience: Children of Elk Island Catholic Schools teachers (Sherwood Park, Fort Saskatchewan, Camrose, Vegreville area)
notes: The board here is the parent's employer, not the school you attend, so you qualify wherever you go to school. Administered through your school, so the date shown is last cycle rolled forward. Ask your counsellor for this year's date as soon as school starts.
description: A $1,000 scholarship from Alberta Teachers' Association Local 21, only for children of Elk Island Catholic Schools staff in the Sherwood Park, Fort Saskatchewan, Camrose, and Vegreville areas. Awarded on academic standing.

title: Southeastern Alberta Regional Science Fair Award
audience: Top senior projects at the SEAR Science Fair
description: Senior-division projects (grades 11-12) at the Southeast Alberta Regional Science Fair compete for certificates, prizes and special awards, and up to five seniors advance to the Canada Wide Science Fair with expenses paid.
notes: Praxis has confirmed the 2027 Southeastern Alberta Regional Science Fair for March 20, 2027 at Medicine Hat College. The date here is the fair itself; registration closes earlier, so watch the Praxis page. Prizes range from certificates to national level awards and university scholarships, which is why no single amount is listed.
metaDetail: Top seniors advance to the Canada-Wide fair.

title: Belcourt Brosseau Métis Awards
audience: Métis students from Alberta entering or continuing post-secondary
notes: Applications open January 2 and close March 31 at 6:00 p.m. You need proof of Métis citizenship or membership, or a letter confirming your application for it is in progress.
description: The Belcourt Brosseau Métis Awards pay between $1,000 and $10,000 a year and have put more than $12 million toward roughly 3,900 Métis students over two decades, which makes them one of the largest non-governmental funders of Métis students in Canada. You need citizenship with the Otipemisiwak Métis Government or membership in a Métis Settlement, Alberta residency, Canadian citizenship, and a place in an eligible program at an eligible post-secondary school.
metaDetail: Needs Metis citizenship or proof your application is in progress.

title: Kermet Archibald & Jacoba Van den Brink Entrance Bursary
audience: Grade 12 CBE and Calgary Catholic students in sciences or designated trades
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here. Three rules apply to every EducationMatters award and are easy to miss: you must be 20 or younger as of September 1, you must not already be attending a post-secondary institution, and you must apply in your Grade 12 year. Once you leave high school you can no longer apply, so a gap year is fine only if you applied before you graduated.

items.text: An account on the EducationMatters award portal
An essay of about 500 words on what the funding would change and your goals
Proof of financial need
Reference letters are welcome but not required

description: $10,000 in year one, renewable up to three more years at $6,500, for hard sciences, engineering, geology, biology, veterinary medicine or health sciences. A trades and vocational stream is worth $15,000 in total. Financial need and a 500-word essay required.
metaDetail: Hard sciences or a designated trade, renewable for four years.

title: Marguerite Patricia P. Bannister Memorial Degree Awards
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE/CCSD high school students entering University of Calgary
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: This $4,000 award honors the legacy of Marguerite Patricia P. Bannister by supporting graduating high school students from Calgary's CBE and CCSD schools who are entering the University of Calgary. The scholarship recognizes academic achievement and assists students as they transition to university-level studies.
metaDetail: Confirm the date before you plan on it.

title: Bill Gibson Bursary
audience: Calgary public and Catholic grads entering first year in the city
notes: Established by the Stampede City Progress Club for Bill Gibson, its longest serving member. You must go straight from Grade 12 into first year: a gap year disqualifies you, and the program has to be a full-time undergraduate degree at a Calgary institution. Selection weighs leadership in Calgary communities alongside financial need. The value has moved between cycles, listed at $10,000 in an earlier year and at $7,500 renewable for three years on the most recent Calgary Board of Education listing, so confirm the figure with the Calgary Foundation. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward.
description: $7,500 for a Grade 12 student graduating from a Calgary public or Catholic school and entering first year of a full-time undergraduate degree at a Calgary post-secondary institution, renewable for up to three years.
metaDetail: Renewable three years; no gap year allowed.

title: Calgary Flames Foundation Community Involvement Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 CBE and Calgary Catholic students with volunteer records
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here. Three rules apply to every EducationMatters award and are easy to miss: you must be 20 or younger as of September 1, you must not already be attending a post-secondary institution, and you must apply in your Grade 12 year. Once you leave high school you can no longer apply, so a gap year is fine only if you applied before you graduated.
description: Four awards a year for students who show leadership through volunteering in their school or community. Essay and one reference letter required.
metaDetail: Four a year, on volunteering and one reference.

title: Edith Berger Memorial Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 CBE and Calgary Catholic students entering teaching
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here. Three rules apply to every EducationMatters award and are easy to miss: you must be 20 or younger as of September 1, you must not already be attending a post-secondary institution, and you must apply in your Grade 12 year. Once you leave high school you can no longer apply, so a gap year is fine only if you applied before you graduated.
description: For a student heading into post-secondary studies to become a teacher, with a 70 percent minimum average.
metaDetail: For students on the path to becoming a teacher.

title: Big Brothers Big Sisters Society of Calgary and Area Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 CBE and Calgary Catholic students involved with Big Brothers Big Sisters
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here. Three rules apply to every EducationMatters award and are easy to miss: you must be 20 or younger as of September 1, you must not already be attending a post-secondary institution, and you must apply in your Grade 12 year. Once you leave high school you can no longer apply, so a gap year is fine only if you applied before you graduated.
description: For a student with past or present involvement in Big Brothers Big Sisters of Calgary and Area.
metaDetail: Community involvement and mentorship both count.

title: Eimer Scholarship Fund Award for Health Care
audience: Grade 12 CBE and Calgary Catholic students entering health care
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here. Three rules apply to every EducationMatters award and are easy to miss: you must be 20 or younger as of September 1, you must not already be attending a post-secondary institution, and you must apply in your Grade 12 year. Once you leave high school you can no longer apply, so a gap year is fine only if you applied before you graduated.
description: Up to ten awards for students entering their first year of a practical health care program at Bow Valley College, Mount Royal University, SAIT or the University of Calgary.
metaDetail: Bow Valley, Mount Royal, SAIT or the U of C.

title: Alex Tutschek FCPA, FCA Award for Indigenous Student High School Achievement
audience: Grade 12 Indigenous Albertans accepted into an Alberta business program
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.
description: Two $1,500 awards for Grade 12 Indigenous students who are enrolled in or accepted into a business program at an Alberta college, polytechnic or university that offers the prerequisites for the CPA Professional Education Program. You have to be an Alberta resident, self-identify as First Nations (status or non-status), Métis or Inuit, and submit a letter or a two to three minute video on why you are heading into business or accounting, plus recent transcripts and one letter of support from an instructor. Preference goes to students who intend to pursue the CPA designation.
metaDetail: Two awards; video can replace the letter.

title: CPA Alberta Young Emerging Professional Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students demonstrating professionalism, integrity, and leadership
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.

items.text: A letter, or a 2 to 3 minute video, on the qualities a business leader needs
Recent transcripts
A teacher support letter and one more non-family reference

description: Two $1,500 awards for Alberta high school students, judged on professionalism, integrity, ethics and leadership on top of satisfactory academic standing. You submit a letter or a two to three minute video on the qualities that make a successful business leader, recent transcripts, a letter from a teacher and a second letter from someone who is not a teacher or family member. Preference goes to students interested in the CPA designation.
metaDetail: A video can replace it.

title: David Bentley FCPA FCA and Janet Bentley High School Excellence Award
audience: Grade 12 Albertans, preference for those relocating within Alberta for post-secondary
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.

items.text: A letter on your financial need and your interest in accounting
Proof you completed Grades 10 to 12 in Alberta and are enrolled in high school
Proof of post-secondary acceptance
Transcripts
At least one nomination letter about your volunteering

description: One $2,500 award for a Grade 12 student at any Alberta high school, based on volunteer involvement, satisfactory academic achievement and a stated interest in a professional accounting designation. Your application letter needs to indicate financial need. You must have finished Grades 10 and 11 in Alberta and provide proof of acceptance at an Alberta post-secondary. Preference goes to applicants who have to relocate within Alberta to attend, and to those living outside the major cities.

title: Empowered Young Woman Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students who identify as a girl or woman
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.

items.text: A letter, or a 2 to 3 minute video, on what being an empowered young woman means to you
Your acceptance letter from an Alberta post-secondary school
One support letter from a teacher or community leader

description: One $2,000 award from the CPA Education Foundation for a Grade 12 Alberta student who identifies as a girl or woman, judged on good character and leadership rather than marks. You submit a letter or a two to three minute video on what being an empowered young woman means to you, your post-secondary acceptance letter, and one letter of support that speaks to your character and any obstacles you have had to get past. Preference goes to students interested in the CPA designation.
metaDetail: Judged on character and leadership rather than marks.

title: Kelly & Creaghan Stepping Up in the Community Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students who demonstrate leadership through volunteering
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.

items.text: A letter, or a 2 to 3 minute video, about your volunteer work
Your acceptance letter from an Alberta post-secondary school
One support letter from a teacher or community leader

description: One $2,000 award for a Grade 12 Albertan with a real volunteer record at school or in the community. You submit a letter or a two to three minute video on a volunteer activity you actually do and what giving back has done for you, your post-secondary acceptance letter, and one letter of support. Preference goes to students interested in the CPA designation.
metaDetail: A video may replace the letter.

title: Michael Burnyeat FCPA, FCA Sparking Great Careers High School Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students entering BBA, B.Mgmt, or B.Comm at an Alberta institution
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.
description: Four $1,250 awards for Grade 12 students at Alberta high schools who have been accepted into a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Management or Bachelor of Commerce program at an Alberta post-secondary. Your letter has to indicate financial need, show professionalism, integrity, ethics and leadership, and state that you have no immediate family member who is a CPA. You also need proof of acceptance and at least one letter of support from a teacher or community leader.
metaDetail: No immediate family CPA.

title: WorldSkills Provincial Champion Scholarship
audience: Top 2 Grade 12 podium finishers at the Provincial Skills Canada Competition
notes: No fixed deadline. You qualify by finishing on the podium at the Provincial Skills Canada Competition, then send Alberta Student Aid the application form and your Skills Canada Alberta letter of endorsement. You have two years from the date of the letter to claim it.
description: $1,200 from the Alberta Heritage Scholarship Fund for a top podium finish at the Provincial Skills Canada Competition. It goes to the top two Grade 12 finishers and the top post-secondary finisher. You have to be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person, and an Alberta resident. Visa students are not eligible.
metaDetail: You qualify by placing at the provincials.

title: First Nations, Métis and Inuit Bursary
audience: Indigenous students in full-time post-secondary, with return of service in northern Alberta
notes: Two intakes each year: February 1 to June 1, and June 5 to November 1. Apply in one intake only, late applications are not accepted. You need a verified Alberta.ca Account, which can take up to two weeks to set up.
description: Up to $11,500 a year for First Nations, Métis and Inuit students in a degree program, or up to $7,000 for a certificate, diploma or pre-apprenticeship program. In exchange you sign a return of service agreement: one year of full-time work in northern Alberta for each year of funding. You reapply every year, to a maximum of four.

title: New Beginnings Bursary
audience: Alberta students who qualify for full-time student aid and enrol in an eligible high-demand program
notes: There is no separate application. Recipients are picked from full-time Alberta Student Aid applications on a first come, first served basis, so apply for student aid as early as you can. Lifetime maximum of two bursaries.

items.text: No separate application. You are considered when you apply for a full-time student loan.

description: A $5,000 bursary for students from low-income families who qualify for full-time Alberta Student Aid and enrol in an approved high-demand program. Alberta expanded it for 2026-27: 2,400 bursaries instead of 1,000, a $12 million budget, and more eligible programs in technology, health and energy. You do not apply separately, so get your student aid application in early.
metaDetail: No separate application form.

title: Loran Scholarship
audience: Canadian citizens or permanent residents entering university for the first time in 2027, with an 88% average
description: Canada's largest undergraduate merit award, worth approximately $150,000 over four years: a $12,000 annual stipend, a full tuition waiver at a partner university, and up to $14,000 for summer programs. Selection weighs character and service as heavily as marks, over online semi-finals and national interviews in Toronto.
notes: You apply directly at apply.loranscholar.ca; the 88% is calculated from Grade 10, 11 and 12 courses only. Applicants must be born between January 1, 2005 and September 1, 2011. Even if you do not make the final class, up to 54 finalists receive $6,000 and up to 70 provincial and territorial recipients receive $3,000. Applications close at noon ET on the deadline day, not at midnight.

items.text: An account at apply.loranscholar.ca
Short answers and several short essays
Timed video answers, opened after the written part, with no second take
One referee (not family or friends) who fills in a short online form
A transcript PDF from your guidance office or school board. Report cards are not accepted.
Interviews if you are shortlisted

title: Schulich Leader Scholarships
audience: Canadian high school students entering STEM at one of 20 selected universities; school nominates 1 student
notes: Your school nominates you, you cannot apply directly. Every Canadian high school can put forward one graduating student, two if the school had a Schulich Leader in 2026. Nomination deadline is January 27, 2027 and nominated students then have until February 17, 2027 to submit the application and reference letters. Talk to your counsellor in the fall, not in January.
description: The Schulich Leader Scholarships recognize exceptional Canadian high school students pursuing STEM at one of 20 select Canadian universities. One hundred are awarded each year: fifty at $120,000 for engineering and fifty at $100,000 for science, technology and math.
metaDetail: 100 awards a year.

title: TD Scholarships for Community Leadership
audience: No longer accepting applications
description: TD has ended this program. In its own words, after more than 30 years the TD Scholarships for Community Leadership has concluded, and no new applications will be accepted for 2026 and beyond. It is kept here so that students who were told to apply can see that it is over, rather than finding a dead form.
metaDetail: Ended by TD. Nothing to apply for.
notes: TD now points students at the TD Scholarship for Indigenous Peoples instead, run with AFOA Canada: 25 awards a year worth up to $60,000 over four years. That one now has its own listing here, checked on 2026-09-11.

title: Terry Fox Humanitarian Award
audience: Canadian students demonstrating humanitarian work, up to 4 years of funding
notes: Heads up: the Terry Fox Humanitarian Award had not posted the next cycle date when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last year's date rolled forward. Confirm on their site before you plan around it.
description: Up to $28,000 over four years for Canadian students with a sustained record of humanitarian work. The selection committee looks for years of service, not a single project.
metaDetail: The committee looks for years of service, not one project.

title: Advancing Futures Bursary
audience: Alberta youth aged 18 to 24 who have been in government care (foster care) at any point
notes: Three deadlines a year, tied to when you start school: apply by June 1 to start September to December, October 1 to start January to April, February 1 to start May to August. The next one is October 1, 2026. You reapply every year.

items.text: The Advancing Futures application form, every year you want funding

description: Alberta pays up to $40,000 toward post-secondary for youth aged 18 to 24 who have been in government care. If you've been in foster care, this is the largest source of funding available to you in the province.

title: UCalgary Pathways to Medicine Scholarship
audience: High school students applying to University of Calgary undergraduate programs
notes: Applications open October 1, 2026 and close December 1. Shortlisted applicants get a preliminary application in early December, due early January, with decisions in February.

items.text: Apply to the University of Calgary and its high school entrance awards by December 1
A nomination letter from someone in your community, such as a teacher, coach or Indigenous leader
Proof of low household income
Two more application rounds if shortlisted, then a Multiple Mini Interview in March

description: UCalgary's renewable award for low-income, rural, and Indigenous students entering its undergraduate programs: up to $5,000 a year, to a maximum of $20,000 over four years, with an eye toward students headed for medicine.

title: Keyera Energy: Peter J. Renton Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta residents entering first year of an oil and gas degree or diploma in AB
notes: Open August 1 to October 31 each year. Two awards of $3,000. Preference goes to the previous year's recipients if they hold a 3.0 GPA. You submit an essay on your community service, work, leadership and marks, and how your field connects to the energy sector.

items.text: An Alberta Student Aid account (or the paper form), between August 1 and October 31
An essay on your service, work, leadership, marks, how your studies connect to energy, and your plans

description: Keyera's $6,000 scholarship, in memory of Peter J. Renton, goes to a graduating Albertan starting an oil and gas related degree or diploma at an Alberta institution.
metaDetail: Two awards a year.

title: NADC Northern Alberta Development Council Bursary
audience: Students in the final two years of a post-secondary program, with return of service in northern Alberta
notes: Applications are accepted January 2 to May 15 each year for fall enrolment. Decisions go out by the end of July. You need a verified Alberta.ca Account, which can take up to two weeks to set up.
description: Up to $7,000 a year, for a maximum of two years, for students training for jobs northern Alberta needs. You commit to one year of full-time work in northern Alberta for each year of funding you receive. You must be 18 or older, an Alberta resident for the past 12 months, and in the last two years of your program.
metaDetail: You commit to a year of work up north.

title: Premier's Citizenship Award
audience: Alberta high school students; each school nominates ONE student per year
notes: No money is attached. The province runs three Alberta Citizenship Awards from one nomination process, and this is the one that pays nothing: the Alberta Centennial Award carries $2,005 and the Queen's Platinum Jubilee Citizenship Award carries $7,000, eight a year against 25 Centennial awards. Each high school may put forward one student, so the first competition is inside your own school. Academic achievement is explicitly not a criterion.
description: The Premier writes to one graduating student per Alberta high school in recognition of citizenship, leadership and community service, and winning it makes you eligible for the two cash awards beside it.
metaDetail: Recognition only, but it unlocks two paid awards.

title: Calgary Stampede Grade 12 Western Art Scholarship
audience: Southern Alberta Grade 12 students who create western art
notes: Six scholarships: three for students at Calgary high schools and three for students elsewhere in southern Alberta. The Stampede does not post the deadline, so this is last cycle rolled forward. Email stampedescholarshipart@gmail.com to confirm.
description: The Calgary Stampede gives $2,000 to a Grade 12 student in Southern Alberta for western art: work rooted in the culture and traditions of the Canadian West.
metaDetail: Six awards: three in Calgary, three elsewhere in southern Alberta.

title: School Sport Alberta Milk Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 student-athletes nominated by a School Sport Alberta member school
notes: Your school nominates, and it may put forward only one male and one female student, so the first hurdle is internal and the principal has to sign the form. You also owe a teacher reference, a reference from someone in the sports community, a two-page resume and a 500-word essay on what sport and healthy eating mean to you.
description: Alberta Milk funds two of these a year through School Sport Alberta, the body that was called the ASAA until it renamed itself, for grade 12 athletes heading to post-secondary in Canada.
metaDetail: One male and one female winner a year.

title: Anna & John Kolesar Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta grads entering a Faculty of Education, with no parent holding a university degree
notes: Open August 1 to October 31 each year. You submit the form to Alberta Student Aid, and the money is released once they confirm you are enrolled full time in a Faculty of Education.
description: One award of $1,500 from the Alberta Heritage Scholarship Fund for a student graduating from an Alberta high school this year and heading into a Faculty of Education full time at an Alberta public post-secondary. The catch that rules most people out, and lets others in: neither of your parents can hold a university degree. You also have to be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person, and an Alberta resident. Visa students are not eligible.

title: IODE Coronation Bursary
audience: Alberta high school students entering any degree program in AB, 3+ years AB resident, financial need
notes: IODE lists the value inconsistently, as two bursaries of $1,000 and also as $5,000 awarded one per year as funds allow. The application is a Word document you download from the IODE page. Confirm the amount and the deadline with IODE Alberta before applying.

metaDetail: The window runs January to late April.

metaDetail: Also listed as the Stirling Wind Project award; do not apply twice.

metaDetail: Opens in late January; check the site then.

metaDetail: Recognizes excellence and passion in piano performance.

metaDetail: Paid $1,000 in first year, $1,500 in second.

metaDetail: No application: consent in MyTradesecrets.

title: 4-H Canada Scholarships
audience: Senior 4-H members in Canada heading to post-secondary or a trade
notes: The six streams are listed separately here, because each has its own sponsor, cheque size and field of study: McDonald's Canada, John Deere Canada, TD, Maizex, MNP and the Campbellbrook Fund. Detailed criteria live in each stream's own application guidelines at apply.4-h-canada.ca. The 2026 cycle ran in the spring and has closed; no 2027 dates are posted yet, so check in April rather than treating April as a promise. Verified against the 4-H Canada scholarships page on 2026-09-09.
description: 4-H Canada runs six sponsored scholarship streams for senior 4-H members across Canada, worth $1,000 to $4,000 depending on the sponsor and the field you are heading into. One portal covers all six, and you can apply to more than one.
metaDetail: One portal covers all six sponsored streams.

title: McDonald's Canada Future of Agriculture 4-H Scholarship
audience: Senior 4-H members entering agriculture, food security or food-system studies
notes: The largest of the six sponsored streams by number of awards, tied with John Deere at 15. You must be a senior 4-H member to apply, and every stream is applied for through the same 4-H Canada portal. The 2026 cycle has closed and 4-H Canada has not posted 2027 dates yet.
description: McDonald's Canada funds 15 awards of $3,000 a year through 4-H Canada, for senior members heading into an agricultural program or one that supports food security, the food system or the value chain.
metaDetail: Fifteen awards a year, the most of the six.

title: John Deere Canada 4-H Scholarship
audience: Senior 4-H members entering any degree, certificate or trade program
notes: Worth the least per award, but open to the widest range of programs, so it is the stream to try if no other 4-H field requirement fits. You must be a senior 4-H member to apply, and every stream is applied for through the same 4-H Canada portal. The 2026 cycle has closed and 4-H Canada has not posted 2027 dates yet.
description: John Deere Canada funds 15 awards of $1,000 a year through 4-H Canada. It is the least restrictive of the six streams on field of study: any degree, certificate or trade-based program at a Canadian college or university qualifies.
metaDetail: No field-of-study requirement, unlike the other five streams.

title: TD 4-H Agriculture Scholarship
audience: Senior 4-H members entering agriculture, ag-science or agri-business
notes: Narrower than the McDonald's stream, which also counts food-system and food-security programs. You must be a senior 4-H member to apply, and every stream is applied for through the same 4-H Canada portal. The 2026 cycle has closed and 4-H Canada has not posted 2027 dates yet.
description: TD funds 12 awards of $3,000 a year through 4-H Canada, for senior members entering agriculture, ag-science or agri-business at a Canadian college or university.
metaDetail: Twelve awards a year for ag, ag-science or agri-business.

title: Maizex 4-H Canada Scholarship
audience: Senior 4-H members entering field crop production or crop science
notes: The biggest cheque of the six streams and the narrowest field requirement, so the applicant pool is the smallest. You must be a senior 4-H member to apply, and every stream is applied for through the same 4-H Canada portal. The 2026 cycle has closed and 4-H Canada has not posted 2027 dates yet.
description: Maizex Seeds funds 5 awards of $4,000 a year through 4-H Canada, for senior members taking an agriculture diploma or degree in field crop production or crop science.
metaDetail: The largest single award of the six 4-H streams.

title: MNP 4-H Canada Scholarship
audience: Senior 4-H members entering a business-related program
notes: The only 4-H stream aimed at business students rather than agriculture or trades. You must be a senior 4-H member to apply, and every stream is applied for through the same 4-H Canada portal. The 2026 cycle has closed and 4-H Canada has not posted 2027 dates yet.
description: MNP funds 5 awards of $2,000 a year through 4-H Canada, for senior members entering a business-related program: commerce, accounting, finance, data analytics or public administration.
metaDetail: The one 4-H stream for business students.

title: Campbellbrook Fund 4-H Canada Trade Scholarship
audience: Senior 4-H members entering a trade or apprenticeship supporting agriculture
notes: The trade stream, open coast to coast. A welding or heavy-equipment ticket aimed at farm work counts; a trade with no agricultural tie does not. You must be a senior 4-H member to apply, and every stream is applied for through the same 4-H Canada portal. The 2026 cycle has closed and 4-H Canada has not posted 2027 dates yet.
description: The Campbellbrook Fund pays 5 awards of $2,000 a year through 4-H Canada, for senior members entering a trade-based program or apprenticeship leading to a career that supports the agriculture sector.
metaDetail: The 4-H stream for apprenticeships and trade tickets.

metaDetail: One award a year, for Albertans aged 25 or under.

title: ENMAX Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students with a parent or guardian at ENMAX
notes: EducationMatters took down its page for this award in September 2026. Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here. Three rules apply to every EducationMatters award and are easy to miss: you must be 20 or younger as of September 1, you must not already be attending a post-secondary institution, and you must apply in your Grade 12 year. Once you leave high school you can no longer apply, so a gap year is fine only if you applied before you graduated.
description: Three $2,500 awards for Grade 12 students whose parent or guardian is a permanent ENMAX employee or retiree, at a CBE, Calgary Catholic or other school district high school. You need at least 70 per cent and two reference letters showing ENMAX's values through activities outside class.
metaDetail: A parent or guardian must work at ENMAX.

title: Indspire Building Brighter Futures Bursaries and Scholarships
audience: First Nations, Inuit and Métis students in post-secondary, trades or apprenticeships
notes: There is one application for almost all of Indspire's funding, and it is the single most important thing to know here. The named corporate awards you see elsewhere, such as the AltaLink Indigenous Student Awards, the Syncrude Indigenous Engineering Scholarship and the TD, Suncor and Rogers funds, are sub-funds inside this one application rather than separate programs with their own forms. Applying once considers you for every fund you match, so do not go hunting for individual application pages that do not exist. There are three deadlines a year, August 1, November 1 and February 1, all at 11:59 p.m. Eastern, and you can apply for the September to August academic year. Indspire awarded over $33 million to more than 9,500 students in its most recent year, but it says plainly it cannot fund every applicant, so apply at the earliest deadline you can meet. Wherever possible the money is unrestricted and can go to tuition, childcare, food, cultural support, shelter or travel.
description: Indspire is the largest non-governmental funder of Indigenous post-secondary students in Canada, with more than $313 million awarded through over 93,000 bursaries and scholarships since 1996. First Nations, Inuit and Métis students in college, university, skilled trades, apprenticeship and technology programs apply once for everything.
metaDetail: One form, every fund.

description: Awarded automatically to the top-scoring secondary student on Team Alberta at the Skills Canada National Competition: $5,000 a year toward post-secondary in their trade, for up to four years. There is no application.

metaDetail: A free two-minute entry, no essay or grades; earlier entries get more chances.

title: Football Alberta Scholarships
audience: Graduating Grade 12 ASAA tackle football players continuing to play at the post-secondary level in Alberta
notes: Verified 2026-09-09 against Football Alberta's own scholarships page, which corrected two facts this listing had wrong: there are FIVE awards a year totalling $10,000, not eight, and the deadline is June 15 at 4pm, not June 30. The five are split by region: Northern Alberta, Edmonton, Central Alberta, Calgary and Southern Alberta, one each. That regional split is the thing worth knowing, because a region needs a minimum of five applicants to award its scholarship at all; thin regions get pooled with the next smallest, and a vacant zone goes to the region with the most applicants. Your high school program must be a paid Football Alberta member in the year you apply, you must have played within School Sport Alberta, and the post-secondary program must run at least two years. Applications and reference letters go by email to Football Alberta. The 2026 cycle closed June 15; the date here carries that forward and was not published for the new cycle when checked.
description: Five $2,000 scholarships a year, one for each Football Alberta region, for graduating Grade 12 tackle football players continuing to play at an accredited Alberta post-secondary institution at the USport, CJFL or WWCFL level.

Volunteering in the community counts equally with volunteering at school, which matters if your school had no opening.

The application wants a two page letter, a resume, a program description, proof of age, a reference letter and audition materials.
description: The Queen's Platinum Jubilee Scholarship for Performing Arts awards $7,000 to one young Alberta performing artist showing extraordinary talent and potential. The discipline rotates on a three year cycle through music, theatre and dance, and the March 1, 2027 round is the music year. You have to be 25 or younger at the deadline, have lived in Alberta for a full year, and be enrolled in an eligible training program: an undergraduate degree with a performing arts focus, a technical or conservatory school, or a recognized mentorship or master class. Graduate programs do not count.
metaDetail: The 2027 round is the music year of three.

description: The Fraser Institute Student Essay Contest invites Canadian high school students to engage with ideas from the Fraser Institute's Essential Scholars series. Contestants write a 1,000–1,500 word essay exploring what one of those thinkers would say about Canadian economic prosperity today. Up to 15 awards of $1,500 are available across high school, undergraduate, and graduate categories. High school submissions must include the school name and grade. Strong essays demonstrate economic reasoning and cite academic references.
metaDetail: A 1,000 to 1,500 word essay on the Essential Scholars.

title: Valour Canada History and Heritage Scholarship
audience: Canadian youth under 21 not currently enrolled in post-secondary
notes: The 2025-26 contest closed June 10, 2026 at 23:59 EST. Valour Canada runs it annually on the same date. You submit an introductory document plus a video under 1 GB by email.
description: The Valour Canada History and Heritage Scholarship recognizes Canadian youth who engage with their country's military history and service. Applicants under 21 who are not currently in post-secondary education submit a 4–6 minute YouTube video visiting a local war memorial or monument, referencing at least two of Valour Canada's character pillars (communication, cooperation, courage, responsibility, resilience, or thoughtfulness), along with a short written statement. The top prize is $2,000; a runner-up award of $500 is also given. Quebec residents and those attending post-secondary during the 2025-2026 school year are not eligible.
metaDetail: You submit a 4 to 6 minute video at a local war memorial.

title: Communication Contest for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
audience: High school students with certified hearing loss of 40+ decibels
notes: June 15 is the date your District has to send its winner to Optimist International. Your own deadline is set by your sponsoring Optimist Club and is much earlier, so contact the local club in the fall.
description: The Optimist International Communication Contest for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing awards $2,500 to high school students who demonstrate communication skills despite certified hearing challenges. Contestants must have a documented hearing loss of 40 decibels or more (verified by audiogram within the past 24 months) and present a speech or sign language performance on the 2025-2026 topic: "The Moment I Realized I Belonged: My Definition of Community." The contest is organized at the local district level through Optimist Club chapters across Canada, the US, and the Caribbean, with up to 45 awards available.
metaDetail: Needs an audiogram showing 40dB loss within 24 months.

title: China-Alberta Award for Excellence in Chinese

notes: You need Chinese Language and Culture 10 and 20 done, be in or finished 30, be in Grade 12, and hold an 80 percent average overall and in Chinese. You submit a form, a two paragraph essay and a teacher reference. Date is rolled forward from last cycle.
description: The China-Alberta Award for Excellence in Chinese recognizes Alberta Grade 12 students who excel in the Chinese Language and Culture Program. Applicants must have completed Chinese Language and Culture 10 and 20 and be currently enrolled in or have completed level 30, with a minimum 80% average across all courses and a minimum 90% average in Chinese Language and Culture 10 and 20. The application includes a two-paragraph essay on how the program will apply to the student's future studies or career. Only Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or protected persons who are Alberta residents (with at least one parent residing in Alberta) are eligible; visa students do not qualify.

title: Lorilei and Arthur Jenkins Collaborative Member Scholarship
audience: Current members of the Red Deer Royals heading to post-secondary
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it. Applications close at 4:30pm, and the portal needs its own account, so leave time for the two reference letters.
description: A $500 scholarship for current members of the Red Deer Royals, the city marching show band. You must be enrolling in or already attending a post-secondary program at an institution in Canada, so graduating members can apply. The application asks for a completed form and two reference letters, submitted through the Community Foundation of Central Alberta portal.
metaDetail: Needs two references and a portal account.

title: Red Deer Catholic Grade 12 Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in Red Deer Catholic Regional Schools
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: The Red Deer Regional Catholic Education Foundation awards $1,000 to Grade 12 students in Red Deer Catholic Schools taking the next step after high school. It is deliberately wide: a degree or certificate from an institution that grants formal accreditation counts, and so does educational training or certification aimed at the workplace, so trades and workplace training routes are eligible alongside university. Applications are submitted online.
metaDetail: Trades and workplace certification count, not only degrees.

title: Daughters of Wisdom Social Justice Award
audience: Students in Red Deer Catholic Regional Schools who demonstrate their faith through social justice action
notes: The foundation had not announced a date or an amount for this award when it was checked in August 2026; the page says only that applications are submitted online and the date is to be announced. Watch the foundation page, or ask the Superintendent office at 403-343-1055.
description: Established in 2012 by the Moore family to honour the Daughters of Wisdom, the religious order that founded Catholic education in Central Alberta. It goes annually to a student in Red Deer Catholic Regional Schools who demonstrates their faith through social justice action.
metaDetail: Amount and date were still unannounced.

title: Health Care Professionals of Tomorrow Scholarship
audience: Graduating students who volunteer at Chinook Regional Hospital and are heading into a health care program
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it. Applications are due at noon, not end of day. The 40 volunteer hours are the gate to watch: they are lifetime hours at Chinook Regional Hospital specifically, so this is one to start in Grade 10 or 11 rather than in your graduating year.
description: Friends of Chinook Regional Hospital, the hospital foundation, and Alberta Health Services Volunteer Resources fund four scholarships a year. Two are set aside for graduating Grade 12 students, at $4,000 for first place and $3,000 for second. You must be an active, registered AHS volunteer at Chinook Regional Hospital with at least 40 lifetime hours, live in the hospital's service area, and be starting full-time post-secondary study in a health care field in the fall. Health care is defined broadly here and is not limited to careers giving direct patient care. Selection weighs your commitment to volunteering, why you volunteer, what your work contributed, your plans for a health care career, and your letters of support. Past recipients cannot apply again.

title: Ray Jolliffe Memorial Scholarship
audience: Canadian students entering theatre or media production design and management
notes: The Allied Arts Council lists March 31 as the deadline without tying it to a year, so this looks like a fixed annual date rather than one cycle. It is a behind-the-scenes theatre award rather than a performance one, so the eligible programs are narrower than they first sound: production design and management, or media production and design.
description: Established by the Jolliffe family in 2008 to recognize Ray Jolliffe and his contribution to theatre production in Lethbridge. The scholarship is worth $3,000 and goes annually to a Canadian student studying theatre production design and management, or media production and design, at a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution. The Allied Arts Council of Lethbridge manages it on behalf of the family, with the funding held by the Community Foundation of Lethbridge and Southwestern Alberta.

title: Aspiring Artist Award
audience: Students in grades 9 through 12 in the Lethbridge area who are working artists
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. This one runs on nominations rather than applications, so you cannot simply put yourself forward: ask an art teacher, an instructor, or someone in the local arts community to nominate you. It is also open from Grade 9, which is earlier than almost anything else here.
description: Established by the Allied Arts Council of Lethbridge in 2019, the Aspiring Artist Award recognises a student in grades 9 through 12 whose level of achievement stands out against peers at a similar stage of development. The award is worth $1,000 and is meant to support both artistic work and further educational opportunities. Recipients are chosen from nominations made by the community.
metaDetail: Runs on nomination, and opens from Grade 9.

title: Elsie Alexander Essay Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in the Lethbridge and district area who have shown leadership in encouraging respect for human life
notes: The 2026 cycle has closed and the association had not posted a 2027 date when this was checked in August 2026, so there is no deadline here to plan against. They run a newsletter that announces when applications reopen. The association draws its area wide: north to Nanton and Vulcan, east to the Saskatchewan border, south to the United States border, and west to the British Columbia border. You can apply for both of the Grade 12 awards, this one and the Elsie Alexander work and volunteer scholarship, in the same year.
description: An essay scholarship of $1,000 offered by the Lethbridge and District Pro-Life Association to a Grade 12 student. It is one of four awards the association gives each year, two for high school students and two for post-secondary students. Applicants are judged on having shown leadership in encouraging respect for all human life, and this is the award decided on a written submission rather than on service.

title: Elsie Alexander Work and Volunteer Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in the Lethbridge and district area with a record of pro-life work or volunteering
notes: The 2026 cycle has closed and the association had not posted a 2027 date when this was checked in August 2026, so there is no deadline here to plan against. They run a newsletter that announces when applications reopen. The association draws its area wide: north to Nanton and Vulcan, east to the Saskatchewan border, south to the United States border, and west to the British Columbia border. You can apply for both of the Grade 12 awards, this one and the Elsie Alexander essay scholarship, in the same year.
description: A $500 scholarship from the Lethbridge and District Pro-Life Association recognising work or volunteer service rather than a written submission. It is open to Grade 12 students who have shown leadership in encouraging respect for all human life. The association gives four awards a year, and this is the service half of the pair set aside for high school students.
metaDetail: Recognises service, with nothing to write.

title: Mac Nishiyama Memorial Scholarship
audience: Students graduating from a high school in southern Alberta and continuing to college or university
notes: The society does not publish a deadline or an application form on its site, so contact info@nikkeiculturalsociety.com for the date and the form. Its two pages also disagree on who can apply: the awards page says any southern Alberta high school graduate, while the society's about page describes it as being for students interested in Japanese language or culture. Ask which applies before you spend time on it.
description: A $500 scholarship awarded annually by the Nikkei Cultural Society, which is based in Lethbridge and supports Japanese Canadian culture in southern Alberta. The awards page states it is open to any student graduating from a high school in southern Alberta who will be continuing their studies at a college or university in the fall. The society also runs awards for University of Lethbridge Japanese language students and a professional development award, neither of which is open to high school students.
metaDetail: Its two pages disagree on this.

title: Cypress County Scholarship
audience: Cypress County residents in high school who are starting post-secondary
notes: This is the County Council award, which is separate from the Agricultural Service Board bursary that closes on the same date. You can be a candidate for both. What decides it is residency, not which school you attend: the terms of reference say applicants living in the County but attending high school in Medicine Hat, Brooks, Foremost or Bow Island are eligible, and so are students in the Crown Village of Ralston and the Townsite of Elkwater. You can only win it once. The application form is on the County's online registrations page, under Scholarship Application.
description: Cypress County Council awards two $1,000 scholarships a year to high school students from the County who are heading to post-secondary, with preference given to those entering a technical program. You need to be registered to start your first year, and the application wants a letter setting out your goals, your transcripts, and your letter of acceptance. A council committee picks the winners on citizenship and community involvement as well as marks.
metaDetail: Two a year.

title: Calgary Catholic School District Kerry Dyte Educational Scholarship
audience: Graduating Calgary Catholic students entering their first year with financial need
notes: This is the closest thing to a Calgary Catholic specific award on the Calgary Foundation list, which otherwise leans heavily toward the public board. The application asks you to show long-term volunteering rather than a one-off, and unusually it also asks you to show current part-time employment. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One scholarship of at least $4,000, paid straight to tuition, for a student graduating from a Calgary Catholic high school and heading into first year at a Canadian post-secondary. It was set up in 2005 so that money would not be the reason someone had to stop at Grade 12.
metaDetail: Asks for long-term volunteering and a part-time job.

title: Fraser W. Lockwood Memorial Scholarship
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE or CCSD students entering first year, with a Filipino community connection preferred
notes: The scholarship honours the ties Fraser Lockwood and his family built with the Filipino community, and preference goes to students whose families have that connection. It is a preference and not a bar, so do not rule yourself out if you do not have it. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: At least $2,500, renewable for three consecutive years if you stay full time. It goes to a student entering first year of undergraduate study immediately after graduating Grade 12 from a Calgary public or Catholic school, who has volunteered through a church, community organization, athletics, or cultural or political activity.
metaDetail: Renewable for three years.

title: Julia Turnbull Leadership Award
audience: Graduating CBE, Calgary Catholic or Calgary charter school students active in student leadership
notes: Preference goes to students already engaged in student politics such as student council, a student union or Model UN, in youth councils or committees, or in debate and speech clubs. Charter school students are eligible here, which is rarer than it should be on this list. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Four or more awards of $1,500 each for graduating Grade 12 students going directly into first year of full-time undergraduate study. It looks for sustained school and community leadership shown through initiative and volunteering.
metaDetail: Prefers student council, debate or Model UN.

title: Michael Gee Scholarship Fund Award
audience: Graduating Calgary students playing U18 AA or U18 AAA hockey through Hockey Calgary
notes: You cannot apply for this one on your own strength alone: it needs a nomination letter from your coach setting out why you are a deserving player on the team. Open to male and female players at U18 AA or U18 AAA. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One award of $5,000, claimable when you start first year of undergraduate study. It is decided on character, hockey and marks together, and you need a cumulative Grade 12 average of at least 85%.
metaDetail: Needs an 85 per cent average and a coach's nomination.

title: Owen Hart Foundation Awards
audience: Graduating students at six named Calgary high schools
notes: Eligibility is by school, not by board: Forest Lawn, Western Canada, Ernest Manning, Crescent Heights, Sir Winston Churchill and Lord Beaverbrook. You need a 70% average or acceptance to post-secondary on entry requirements, and preference goes to students holding part-time work. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Twelve or more awards of $4,000, two at each eligible school. One application is considered for both the Owen Hart Foundation Awards and, for Lord Beaverbrook students, the Jonathan Victor Trueman Memorial Awards, which recognise athletic achievement and artistic achievement in creative writing.
metaDetail: Two per school, and part-time workers are preferred.

title: Bradley Hillmo Anderson Memorial Award
audience: Students in any year of a first undergraduate degree or diploma at a Calgary post-secondary
notes: Preference goes to applicants with sailing experience: Brad Anderson crewed on the Glenmore Reservoir and raced with the Glenmore Sailing Club. It is a preference rather than a requirement. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One or more awards of about $500 toward tuition, for students registered full time in their first undergraduate degree or diploma at a Calgary post-secondary institution with a GPA of at least 2.75. Entering first year counts, so you can apply in your graduating year.
metaDetail: Sailing experience is preferred, not required.

title: Grace & Good Fortune Bursary for Single Mothers
audience: Single mothers in Calgary starting or continuing undergraduate study
notes: The listing does not restrict this to any particular year of study, so a student entering first year straight out of Grade 12 can apply. The application is built around an essay on your education and career plans and your experience as a single mother. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One or more bursaries of at least $2,000 for a single mother with one or more dependent children who lives in Calgary or the surrounding area and is attending undergraduate study at a Calgary post-secondary institution, full time or part time.
metaDetail: Entering first year straight from Grade 12 counts.

title: CEEA Indigenous Award
audience: First Nations, Metis and Inuit students entering first year of a petroleum-focused program
notes: The Canadian Energy Executive Association runs several awards through the Calgary Foundation, and this is the only one of them open to a student coming straight out of high school. The others all start at second year or later. You need a GPA of at least 2.7 or 70%. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One or more awards of $8,500 for diploma programs and $10,000 for degree programs, renewable for up to three consecutive years. It is for a First Nations, Metis or Inuit student going directly into first year of a full-time petroleum-focused program such as petroleum, mechanical or chemical engineering, geology, geophysics, or the matching engineering technology diplomas.
metaDetail: The only CEEA award open from Grade 12.

title: Bates Wardle Award for Lifeguards
audience: Students up to Grade 12 at named Cochrane and Innisfail schools training as lifeguards
notes: Eligibility runs by school: Bow Valley, Cochrane, St. Timothy Jr./Sr. High, Innisfail Middle, Innisfail High, St. Marguerite Bourgeoys, or Ecole Secondaire Notre Dame, with Innisfail catchment residency. Because it spans two towns with no facet of their own it sits under Alberta here. The reference letter is optional, which is unusual. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Two awards of $1,000, ideally one for an Innisfail student and one for a Cochrane student, paid through the school or post-secondary institution. It is for a student aged 12 through Grade 12 who is working toward lifeguard certification or advancing their training.

specificSchools: Ecole Secondaire Notre Dame High School

metaDetail: For students working toward lifeguard papers.

title: John and Ann Scheer Memorial Award
audience: Graduating students at Wheatland County high schools
notes: Eligible schools are Strathmore High School, Holy Cross Collegiate, Strathmore Storefront School, Golden Hills Learning Academy and Wheatland Crossing School. It asks for long-term volunteering and for evidence of personal perseverance, which the award was written around deliberately. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One award of $1,000 for a student graduating Grade 12 from a Wheatland County high school and enrolling in first year of a certificate, diploma or degree in any field at a Canadian post-secondary institution.
metaDetail: Five Wheatland County schools qualify, any field of study.

title: Okotoks Rotary Career Opportunity Awards
audience: Graduating students at Okotoks high schools
notes: Eligible schools are Foothills Composite High School, Holy Trinity Academy, St. Luke's Outreach Okotoks, Cameron Crossing School and The Centre for Learning@HOME. The Rotary Club of Okotoks has run this since 2018, and aims to give one award to a Christ the Redeemer student and one to a Foothills School Division student. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked, so the date shown is last cycle's and should be confirmed with student services.
description: Two awards of $1,500 each, ideally one for a Christ the Redeemer Catholic Schools student and one for a Foothills School Division student, for graduating Grade 12 students entering an accredited Canadian post-secondary institution.
metaDetail: Two awards, and five Okotoks schools qualify.

title: Kirby Morrow Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta or BC students entering a theatre, film or animation program
notes: The application is a video of three minutes or less rather than an essay: you show your passion for the field and say how the money would help. That is a very different kind of work from the rest of this list. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Two awards of $1,000 for an Alberta or British Columbia resident entering first or second year of a full-time undergraduate degree or diploma at an Alberta or BC institution, in theatre, theatre arts, drama, film, radio, television, animation or script writing.
metaDetail: The application is a three-minute video, not an essay.

title: Kids Cancer Care Derek Wandzura Memorial Scholarship
audience: Southern Alberta childhood cancer patients and survivors entering post-secondary
notes: Because it covers any year of study, a student entering first year straight from Grade 12 can apply. Southern Alberta here means Red Deer and everything east, west and south of it. You cannot hold this and the Kids with Cancer Society Bursary, which is the northern Alberta equivalent. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Awards vary each year but start at $2,500, with more available where cancer has caused extenuating circumstances. It is for a childhood cancer patient or survivor diagnosed at age 18 or younger who lives in southern Alberta and is enrolled in any year of an undergraduate degree, diploma or certificate.
metaDetail: Southern Alberta means Red Deer and south.

title: Smillie Family Education Award
audience: Students from rural Canadian communities entering agriculture, education or health care
notes: It asks for a GPA of at least 2.7 or 70% together with financial need, and for leadership and volunteering in both school and community. The rural residency is the real filter here rather than any particular province. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Three awards of about $2,000 each for a Canadian citizen or permanent resident who has lived in a rural Canadian community and is entering first or second year of a full-time undergraduate degree or diploma leading to a career in agriculture, education or health care.
metaDetail: Rural residency is the real filter, not province.

title: Shelagh Neary Mikulak Memorial Scholarship for Leadership and Innovation in Library Sciences
audience: Students in a library sciences or library technician program in any year of study
notes: It is open to any year of study, so a student starting a library technician diploma straight out of Grade 12 qualifies. It is a narrow field but a genuinely open door, and it needs a GPA of at least 2.7 or 70% plus demonstrated financial need. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Two awards of about $2,500, preferably one to an undergraduate and one to a graduate student, for someone enrolled in a Library and Information Sciences or Library Technician certificate, diploma or graduate program at a Canadian post-secondary institution.
metaDetail: A library technician diploma out of Grade 12 qualifies.

title: Royal Canadian Legion Branch 288 Scholarship
audience: Graduates of any Airdrie high school entering first year at the University of Calgary
notes: There is no separate form. You are considered through the High School Awards section of the My UCalgary portal once you have applied for admission, so the work is finishing that section rather than writing anything new. The award page publishes no closing date, which means the admission timeline is the one that matters.
description: Three awards of up to $1,300 each, funded by Airdrie's Royal Canadian Legion branch, for graduates of any Airdrie high school entering their first year at the University of Calgary in any faculty. Selection is on academic merit, and the award carries no citizenship or residency requirement beyond the Airdrie school.
metaDetail: Three awards, Airdrie grads to UCalgary.

title: Airdrie and District Agricultural Society Scholarship
audience: Airdrie area students, one award for agricultural studies and one for any field
notes: The society does not publish the award value. Applications go by email to airdrieagsocietysocial@gmail.com, and the essay topic has been the same one for years, so it can be drafted well before September. The non-agricultural award is the one students skip, which is exactly why it is worth an evening.
description: Two scholarships a year from the Airdrie and District Agricultural Society, one for a student entering agricultural studies and one for a student entering anything else. It asks for a 250 to 300 word essay on the value of volunteerism, three years of extracurricular and leadership activity, and a transcript that includes Grade 12 marks.
metaDetail: A 250 to 300 word essay.

title: Rocky View Teachers' Scholarship
audience: Rocky View graduates, and children of ATA Local 35 members graduating in Alberta
notes: The teachers fund this themselves out of ATA Local 35, and in 2022-23 the pool was about $90,000. Proof of enrolment is the catch: a letter of acceptance does not count, so you apply after you have registered, not when you get in. The forms are Cognito forms and do not work properly on a phone.
description: Rocky View teachers fund a set of scholarships each year for students graduating from a Rocky View high school, which covers the Airdrie public schools, and for children of ATA Local 35 members graduating from any Alberta high school. A Certificate of Achievement qualifies as well as a diploma. Applications opened May 1 and close September 30, the fall after you graduate.

title: Rocky View County 4-H Scholarship
audience: 4-H members from a Rocky View District club entering or returning to post-secondary
notes: Three years in a Rocky View District club is the real filter, and it is one you cannot fix in your Grade 12 year. It is a one-time award, so it cannot be won twice. Applications run through the 4-H Alberta registration site rather than the county's own page. The May 15 date is this year's rolled forward, since the county had not posted the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026.
description: Rocky View County funds two $500 scholarships a year for 4-H members entering or returning to post-secondary study. You need at least three years of membership in a club in the Rocky View District, which takes in the country around Airdrie, and the award can only be held once.
metaDetail: Two awards, and three years in a Rocky View club.

title: Rocky View County Agricultural Scholarship at Olds College
audience: Rocky View County residents in Agricultural Production or Land and Water Resources at Olds College
notes: Two intakes rather than one: October 15 for the fall term and December 31 for winter. Residency is in the county itself, so a student inside Airdrie's city limits does not qualify for this one even though the rest of the page applies to them. The application is Olds College's own awards portal.
description: A $500 award for a Rocky View County resident in the first or second year of the Agricultural Production or the Land and Water Resources program at Olds College, with a GPA of at least 3.00. The county funds it and Olds College administers it through its awards portal.

title: Sean Smith Memorial Scholarship
audience: Current or former Airdrie Minor Basketball players enrolled full time in post-secondary
notes: AMBA moved its site to TeamLinkt and the scholarships page went with it: the old link 404s and the word scholarship does not appear anywhere on the new site as of September 2026. The award may well still run, but nothing is published, so ask the association directly before counting on it. The last window AMBA advertised was January 8 to February 26, and essays were stripped of names before the committee read them. A past AMBA scholarship winner cannot win again.
description: One $500 award from Airdrie Minor Basketball for a current or former AMBA player who is enrolled full time in a post-secondary program. It is named for Sean Smith and marks sportsmanship and team spirit rather than scoring. The application is a short essay, and proof of enrolment is required before the money is paid out.
metaDetail: A short essay, and a very small applicant pool.
