description: Six Elk Island students are selected for this $500 award, which recognises students who have overcome some level of adversity to graduate and continue learning in any capacity. The last three words matter: the criteria cover students working toward an Alberta High School Certificate of Achievement as well as a Diploma, so it reaches students most graduation awards are closed to. It needs both a written student submission and a letter of support from the school.
metaDetail: Six awards, and a certificate of achievement qualifies.

title: WesTEC Scholarship
audience: Elk Island grade 12 students heading into STEM
notes: Elk Island runs this through myBlueprint, so you need a division account to see the form at all. The date the division published was dated to 2026 rather than left as a repeating day, so treat the month as the guide and confirm the exact day with your counsellor.
description: Dow Canada recognises two Elk Island students a year with $500 each for academic achievement and demonstrated innovation in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Selection comes down to a 300-word abstract on a single prompt: describe a time you took an innovative approach to solving a problem that made a positive impact, including the problem, the challenges and the outcome. The prompt explicitly says the example does not have to be a STEM activity.
metaDetail: Decided on one 300-word abstract about innovation.

title: Bunzl Scholarship
audience: Elk Island students who can write about sustainability
notes: Elk Island runs this through myBlueprint, so you need a division account to see the form at all. The date the division published was dated to 2026 rather than left as a repeating day, so treat the month as the guide and confirm the exact day with your counsellor.
description: Five scholarships of $750 for Elk Island students, decided on a 500-word essay about sustainability. Suggested angles include why sustainability matters to you personally, how it shows up in your daily life or community, how sustainable thinking creates long term change, and how it connects to your studies or career. Marking weighs clarity and organisation, original thinking and personal insight, relevance, quality of writing, and use of supporting evidence, so this is a writing competition rather than a transcript one.
metaDetail: Five awards, decided on a 500-word essay.

title: Glen Hauk Memorial Keyera Scholarship
audience: Fort Saskatchewan and Sherwood Park students entering a trade or power engineering
notes: Elk Island runs this through myBlueprint, so you need a division account to see the form at all. The date the division published was dated to 2026 rather than left as a repeating day, so treat the month as the guide and confirm the exact day with your counsellor.
description: Keyera fund a single non-renewable $2,500 scholarship in memory of Glen Hauk for a student entering the first year of a Registered Apprenticeship Program in a qualifying trade, or an accredited full-time power engineering programme. You have to graduate from one of six named schools across Fort Saskatchewan and Sherwood Park. The committee is looking for commitment to the community, a motivated and positive attitude with a desire to improve, and a clear vision of your career goals. Power engineering is rarely named in scholarship criteria at all, which makes this worth knowing about.
metaDetail: Power engineering counts alongside a RAP trade.

title: Kevin Gaetz Scholarship
audience: Elk Island students whose finances would restrict post-secondary
notes: You cannot apply for this one; each Elk Island school nominates up to two students, so the useful move is telling a counsellor you want to be considered. Black Gold School Division runs a separate award from the same Edmonton Community Foundation fund with its own application and a June 30 date, so a student who moves between the divisions is looking at two different routes. Elk Island describes the payment only as a monetary amount and publishes no figure.
description: Paid from the Edmonton Community Foundation, with up to two students at each Elk Island high school receiving an amount to support post-secondary study. The award goes to a student who meets the entrance requirements for the programme to be supported and has financial need that would restrict their ability to pursue it, together with perseverance and commitment to post-secondary education, described in the criteria as the desire and determination to keep learning in an area of interest.
metaDetail: Nomination only, up to two students per school.

title: Twice But Nice Scholarship
audience: Any Fort Saskatchewan high school graduate, including gap year students
notes: The store publishes a dated cutoff each year; the 2026 round closed June 14, and the date shown here assumes the same day repeats, so confirm it on their site. Applications must be one combined PDF emailed in, with letters of reference on letterhead, a conditional acceptance letter and a transcript. Recipients attend the March annual general meeting to report back, and anyone who withdraws within 30 days of a term start has to repay.
description: A thrift store funds the two largest awards in Fort Saskatchewan: $5,000 each, with the Anne Springman Scholarship for a student going to college or university and the Lesley Macmillan Scholarship for one going to a technical institute, trade school or apprenticeship. If nobody applies on one side they may award both on the other. Financial need carries 30 of the 100 selection points, work experience 20, personal challenges 15, and marks only 10, and the criteria say plainly that grades matter only insofar as they got you accepted. Eligibility reaches homeschooled students, Fort Saskatchewan Outreach, Strathcona Christian Academy and students in designated programmes outside the city, and you may apply in your graduating year or within one year of it.
metaDetail: Two at $5,000, one reserved for trades.

title: Lion Don Westman Legacy Scholarship
audience: Fort Saskatchewan graduates from Fort High and St. André Bessette
notes: Applications close September 15, a bare repeating date rather than one tied to a year, and they go to the Lions club directly by email or post rather than through a school. That places it after graduation, when most students have stopped looking.
description: The Fort Saskatchewan Lions Club run this in memory of Lion Don Westman, and their published recipient lists show it going to students from Fort Saskatchewan High School and St. André Bessette Catholic High School in alternating pairs each year. The application is a downloadable form sent to the club, not something the school collects, so it is easy to miss entirely if you are relying on the school awards package.
metaDetail: Closes after graduation, mid September.

title: NCIA Scholarship
audience: Industrial Heartland students entering engineering, trades or technology
notes: The association publishes recipients rather than criteria or a date, and Elk Island lists the application among its own, so the route in is your counsellor or myBlueprint. Recent recipients have come from Fort Saskatchewan and Sherwood Park schools.
description: The Northeast Capital Industrial Association is the industry body for Alberta's Industrial Heartland, headquartered in Fort Saskatchewan, and it awarded $2,000 to each of four students in its most recent round. Its recipients have been heading into electrical engineering, engineering at the University of Alberta, instrumentation engineering technology at NAIT and power engineering at NAIT, which tells you more about what wins it than any published rubric would: a concrete plan tied to industry in the region, in a degree or a diploma equally.
metaDetail: Four awards in the most recent round.

title: Andy Polanski Leader of Tomorrow Memorial Scholarship
audience: Fort Saskatchewan graduates who gave back to the community
notes: The foundation publishes no closing date on its scholarship page, so watch it through the spring or ask the foundation directly. Fort High lists it among its community scholarships, so a counsellor there will know the timing.
description: The Andy Polanski Charitable Foundation was established in 2014 after the death of Andy Polanski, a young man remembered for volunteering across his school and community. It offers $1,000 to a graduate of a Fort Saskatchewan high school going on to post-secondary who has demonstrated the importance of giving back and, through it, has had an impact on others. The foundation's own motto frames the criterion better than a rubric could: life is measured by the fingerprints you leave behind.
metaDetail: Judged on your impact on other people.

title: Footprints to your Future Scholarship
audience: Fort Saskatchewan students who completed high school requirements
notes: This runs alongside the foundation's Leader of Tomorrow award on the same page and in partnership with another organisation, and neither carries a published deadline, so ask the foundation or Fort High student services when it opens.
description: The second of the two Andy Polanski Legacy Scholarships, worth $1,000 to a Fort Saskatchewan high school student who has completed their high school requirements and is pursuing post-secondary education. It is run in partnership rather than by the foundation alone, and its criteria are written more broadly than its sibling award, which asks specifically about giving back.
metaDetail: The second of two Andy Polanski Legacy awards.

title: Josephburg Ag Society Scholarship
audience: Post-secondary students in any year, with no age limit
notes: The society published a dated cutoff of September 1, 2026 for its most recent round, which has now passed, and it has not yet posted the next one. No residency rule is stated anywhere in the criteria, so despite being a local society this is open well beyond Josephburg; it is listed on the Fort Saskatchewan hub because the schools there promote it.
description: The Josephburg Agricultural Society awards three $1,000 scholarships, judged equally on academic achievement and community involvement, with one reserved for a student in a programme leading to a career in agriculture and one given in memory of longtime director Doug Maschmeyer. The eligibility is unusually wide: any post-secondary student starting or already enrolled in any year of an accredited programme, degree or diploma, with no age limit, and you may win it up to three times. The application is a 500-word essay on what volunteerism means to you plus a video of no more than 90 seconds covering your community involvement, academics and career goals.
metaDetail: Three awards, and you can win it up to three times.

title: Calgary Black Chambers Cavalry FC Athletic Scholarship
audience: Black students on a varsity team at a Calgary post-secondary institution
notes: Two awards, with one going to a woman and one to a man, so you are competing inside your own half of a small field. Varsity is the hard requirement: a club or intramural team does not qualify. One application covers every Calgary Black Chambers award, so there is nothing to gain from choosing between them. The Calgary Foundation had not posted dates for the new cycle when this was checked on 2026-09-08; its page still shows the 2026 round, so the date here is last cycle's rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Two awards of $5,000, paid straight to tuition, for Black Canadian citizens or permanent residents who are active student athletes on a varsity women's or men's team at a Calgary post-secondary institution. Any year of a full-time undergraduate degree or diploma qualifies, the bar is a cumulative GPA of 2.7 or 70 per cent, and one reference letter is required.
metaDetail: Varsity only, and one award each for women and men.

title: Calgary Black Chambers TransAlta STEM Scholarship
audience: Black students in a STEM program at a Calgary post-secondary institution
notes: The list of qualifying fields is unusually long and worth checking against your own program before assuming you are out: biology, chemistry, computer science, data science, engineering, environmental sciences, geology, information systems, mathematics, microbiology, natural sciences, physics, statistics, technology and zoology all count. One application covers every Calgary Black Chambers award. The Calgary Foundation had not posted dates for the new cycle when this was checked on 2026-09-08; its page still shows the 2026 round, so the date here is last cycle's rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: A single $7,000 award, paid straight to tuition, for a Black Canadian citizen or permanent resident in second year or beyond of a full-time STEM degree or diploma at a Calgary post-secondary institution. It asks for a cumulative GPA of 2.7 or 70 per cent, school or community involvement that is preferably STEM focused, and one reference letter.
metaDetail: Fifteen named fields count as STEM here.

title: Beaumont Chamber of Commerce RCMP Scholarship
audience: A Beaumont grade 12 student going on to post-secondary who reflects the RCMP core values
notes: The Chamber lists this among its member benefits and publishes no amount, no criteria document and no date, so Beaumont Composite student services or info@beaumontchamber.ca is the only way to get any of the three.
description: An annual scholarship run by the Beaumont Chamber of Commerce in partnership with the RCMP for one grade 12 student heading to post-secondary. The Chamber describes the winner as a young person recognised for demonstrating the core values of the RCMP, which are honesty, integrity, professionalism, compassion, respect and accountability, so this is a character award rather than a marks award. It is the only scholarship any Beaumont organisation outside the school publishes.
metaDetail: No amount, criteria or date published.

title: Prix de l'Ambassadeur du Conseil scolaire Centre-Nord
audience: Grade 12 students graduating from a Conseil scolaire Centre-Nord francophone school
notes: The deadline is set relative to your own ceremony rather than to a calendar date, at three weeks before graduation, so the school office is the only place that can tell you the real day. In Beaumont the school is Ecole Quatre-Saisons.
description: The francophone division gives this to its graduating ambassadors: $500 at a school with one to nineteen graduates, and two awards of $500 where twenty or more graduate. The application is a letter to the principal describing yourself and what you intend to study or do, and candidates who make the shortlist are interviewed by a selection committee at the school. Because it is awarded per school rather than per division, a small francophone school is a much better place to win it from than a large one.
metaDetail: Per school, so a small class helps.

title: Bourse Paul-Charbonneau
audience: Centre-Nord graduates who have already won the Prix de l'Ambassadeur
notes: You cannot enter this one directly. Winning the Prix de l'Ambassadeur at your own school is the qualifying round, and the principal sets the date for the second letter.
description: One $1,000 award a year, chosen from across the whole francophone division but only from students who have already won their school's Prix de l'Ambassadeur. The second stage is a cover letter of no more than 600 words on academic success and community involvement. That two-step shape is worth knowing early, because the work that wins the $500 at your own school is also what puts you in the running for this.
metaDetail: Open only to Prix de l'Ambassadeur winners.

title: Balbiran-Weinkauf Group of Companies Scholarship
audience: Lloydminster Public School Division graduates in financial need
notes: This one does not go through the LPSD form. LCHS student services holds the application, and the deadline is two weeks after the LPSD cutoff, so it is easy to file it and forget it.
description: One $1,000 award for a graduating Lloydminster Public School Division student entering a recognised post-secondary program, decided on financial need. It is a local company award rather than a division one, so it is applied for separately from the May 1 bundle.
metaDetail: Financial need, outside the May 1 bundle.

title: Dai and Irene Jones Memorial Scholarship
audience: Lloydminster music festival participants majoring in music at post-secondary
notes: The qualifying condition is retrospective and cannot be fixed late: you need two consecutive years of Lloydminster and District Music Festival participation, with at least two classes in each of those years, already behind you.
description: One $500 award for a full-time post-secondary student majoring in music or music education who took part in the Lloydminster and District Music Festival for two consecutive years, entering at least two classes each year. It rewards a record built over years of festivals rather than anything you can assemble in grade 12.
metaDetail: Two consecutive festival years.

title: Dr. Malcolm Gray Memorial Scholarship
audience: Lloydminster students entering veterinary medicine or animal health technology
notes: Applications go to the Lloydminster Animal Hospital rather than to a school or a foundation, and the August 31 date sits well after graduation.
description: One $1,000 award for a student in a field related to veterinary medicine, with priority given to pre-vet and animal health technology. The package is a scholarship resume, a letter of intent and grade 12 marks, submitted directly to the Lloydminster Animal Hospital.
metaDetail: Priority to pre-vet students.

title: Dunstan Scholarship
audience: Lloydminster area students in agriculture or agriculture-related business
notes: The three-month minimum program length is the loosest in the Lloydminster set, so a short certificate qualifies where most agriculture awards demand a diploma or degree.
description: Three awards of $600 for education in agriculture or agriculture-related business, where the program need only run three months or longer. That short minimum is the point: it reaches students taking a certificate or a single season of training rather than a multi-year program.
metaDetail: A three-month program is long enough.

title: Friends of the Performing Arts Scholarship
audience: Lloydminster area grade 12 students and graduates entering the performing arts
notes: FOPA publishes no application page of its own, so LCHS student services holds the contact information and the form.
description: One award of up to $1,500 from Friends of the Performing Arts for a grade 12 student or recent graduate from the Lloydminster area entering post-secondary study in drama, dance, music or another performing art. It is the largest arts award in the Lloydminster set by some distance.
metaDetail: The largest arts award.

title: Integra Engineering Scholarship
audience: Lloydminster area graduates entering engineering or engineering technology
notes: Integra publishes a dated cutoff rather than a repeating day, and the 2026 round closed at noon on May 4, so check the form for the current year before relying on an early May date.
description: Two awards of $1,000 for high school graduates from Lloydminster and the surrounding area who are enrolled full time in engineering or engineering technology at a recognised institution. Together with the BAR and Collinge-Ingoldsby awards it means a Lloydminster student heading into engineering has four separate local shots at $1,000.
metaDetail: Two of the four local engineering awards.

title: Joe McLean Agricultural Scholarship
audience: Lloydminster area students in agriculture or veterinary medicine
notes: Held by LCHS student services rather than published by the sponsor, so the form comes from the school.
description: One $500 award for a student enrolled in a diploma or degree program in agriculture, veterinary medicine or a related agricultural field. It shares a May 31 deadline with the Dunstan award and covers much the same ground, so most applicants for one should file for both.
metaDetail: Pairs with the Dunstan award on one deadline.

title: Lloydminster and District Co-op Scholarship
audience: Students whose parent or guardian has held a Co-op membership for three years
notes: The qualifying condition belongs to your parent rather than to you: the Co-op membership must have been held for at least three years, so this is worth checking at home early rather than in May.
description: Four awards of $1,000 for students going to post-secondary full time in the fall whose parent or legal guardian has held a Lloydminster and District Co-op membership for at least three years. Four awards at $1,000 makes it one of the larger pools in the city, and the membership condition removes most of the competition rather than adding to it.

title: Lloydminster and District Fish and Game Scholarship
audience: Lloydminster-area students entering conservation, wildlife or renewable resources
notes: The eligible school list reaches well onto the Alberta side, naming Marwayne, Kitscoty and Paradise Valley alongside the two Lloydminster high schools and the Saskatchewan villages.
description: Two awards of $1,000 for students entering conservation, wildlife and fisheries, biology or renewable resource technology. Eligibility runs across the border by name: Lloydminster Comprehensive and Holy Rosary plus Lashburn, Hillmond, Maidstone, Neilburg, Marwayne, Kitscoty and Paradise Valley. The package is the form, marks, a letter of acceptance, two references, a resume and a covering letter. It may go unawarded in a year with no suitable applicants.
metaDetail: Reaches into Sask.

title: Lloydminster Minor Ball Association Scholarship
audience: Lloydminster Minor Ball players, umpires and coaches entering post-secondary
notes: Umpires and coaches count as active members alongside players, which widens this further than the name suggests.
description: Two awards of $500 for graduates entering full-time post-secondary who were active members of the Lloydminster Minor Ball Association. Being a player is one of three routes in, since umpiring and coaching qualify on the same terms, and the August deadline means it stays open long after the school awards have closed.
metaDetail: Umpiring or coaching qualifies.

title: Lloydminster Teachers' Association Scholarship
audience: Lloydminster students enrolled in a Bachelor of Education
notes: Held by the school rather than published by the association, and the August 31 date means it is decided after you are already registered.
description: Two awards of $1,500 for students enrolled in a Bachelor of Education program. It is the second largest local award for a single student in the Lloydminster set, and the late August deadline suits someone who only settles on teaching after the spring round has passed.
metaDetail: Two at $1,500, decided after you have registered.

title: Lloydminster Region Health Foundation Scholarships
audience: Lloydminster region students entering nursing, mental health and other health fields
notes: The foundation names seven awards but publishes no amount and no deadline for any of them, so the foundation itself is the only source for both. Deadlines are described only as varying.
description: A group of seven named awards from the Lloydminster Region Health Foundation, split between general health and nursing. The general ones are the Sunrise Scholarship for mental health programs and the Dustin Cody McConnell Memorial. The nursing ones are the Pat Redden Memorial, the Goodfellow, the Jane Ruptash for students who have finished second year of an RN program, the Crude Master Cutter Rally For Cancer, and the Arnold Family Scholarship.
metaDetail: Seven named awards, no published amount.

title: Robyn Gray Memorial Scholarship
audience: Students who spent a year at a Camrose city or county high school
notes: Run by the Rotary Club of Camrose Daybreak, and it closes on the first Friday in April, months before the school awards close. A transcript and a reference letter go in with the form.
description: One $1,000 award from the Rotary Club of Camrose Daybreak, open to new and continuing post-secondary students who attended at least one year of high school at a Camrose city or county school. It asks for leadership qualities in line with the beliefs of Rotary International, a 75% minimum or 2.7 GPA, a transcript and a reference letter. The renewability is the unusual part: you may win it again in each of four years of study, so it is worth up to $4,000 to someone who keeps applying.
metaDetail: Renewable four years, so worth $4,000.

title: Battle River Power Coop Scholarship
audience: Dependents of Battle River Power Coop members entering first year
notes: The co-op publishes a dated cutoff rather than a repeating day, and the 2026 round closed on Friday, February 27, which is far earlier than any school award. The tuition receipt is due separately by August 31.
description: Five awards of $1,500 for dependents of Battle River Power Coop members entering their first year of post-secondary, chosen by a board committee. Graduates of the previous or current calendar year both qualify. The package is a transcript, proof of registration, an acceptance letter, a reference letter and a letter on need and program, with a tuition receipt to follow by the end of August.
metaDetail: Five at $1,500, and it closes in February.

title: W. F. MacDonald Scholarship
audience: June graduates who formerly lived in Bashaw, Bawlf, New Norway or Daysland
notes: Mr. Kendall at Camrose Composite holds this one; there is no online form. The residency condition is historic rather than current, so a family that has since moved into Camrose still qualifies.
description: Two awards for students who graduate in June and start a post-secondary program that same fall, one given for academic work and one for trades or technical study. What makes it reachable is the residency rule: it is for former residents of Bashaw, Bawlf, New Norway or Daysland, four small communities around Camrose, which is a much smaller field than the school as a whole.
metaDetail: Two awards, one academic and one trades.

title: Linton and Debbie Falk Scholarship
audience: Battle River School Division graduates entering agriculture or a supporting field
notes: Administered at the division level rather than by any one school, and the value is set each year by the Battle River Community Foundation from the return on the fund, so no fixed amount is published.
description: For a Battle River School Division graduate entering full-time study at an institution in Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba or Saskatchewan in an agricultural program, or in a program which supports agriculture. The criteria say that second phrase is meant to be read broadly and name veterinary medicine, research, climate, commerce and economics as examples, inviting applicants to present their case. BRACE and the division home school count as division schools.
metaDetail: Supports agriculture is read broadly.

notes: Augustana awards are administered by the campus rather than applied for at school, and the annual awards list publishes values and criteria but no dates. Ask the Augustana student awards office once you have accepted an offer.
title: Ryan Henderson Memorial Entrance Award
audience: First-year Augustana students, preferably Camrose Composite graduates
description: One $1,000 entrance award for a student in the first year of an undergraduate degree at Augustana, with preference given to a student graduating from Camrose Composite High School. It is the only award on the Augustana list that names a single high school, which makes it the closest thing Camrose has to a guaranteed local entrance scholarship.
metaDetail: The only Augustana award naming one high school.

notes: Augustana awards are administered by the campus rather than applied for at school, and the annual awards list publishes values and criteria but no dates. Ask the Augustana student awards office once you have accepted an offer.
title: Alberta Blue Cross Entrance Scholarship
audience: Alberta residents entering first year at Augustana
description: One $1,500 entrance scholarship for an Alberta resident starting an undergraduate degree at Augustana, on academic standing and demonstrated financial need. Full-time registration is required, and there is a ceiling that catches people out: recipients may not hold awards totalling more than $3,500.
metaDetail: A $3,500 ceiling on your total awards.

notes: Augustana awards are administered by the campus rather than applied for at school, and the annual awards list publishes values and criteria but no dates. Ask the Augustana student awards office once you have accepted an offer.
title: Feth Family Award
audience: Vikings hockey players entering first year at Augustana
description: One $1,000 award for a Vikings hockey team member entering the first year of an undergraduate degree at Augustana, decided on academic standing. Both conditions are first-year ones, which makes it one of the few Augustana athletic awards a graduating high school student can win immediately.
metaDetail: An athletic award you can win in first year.

title: Federation of Alberta Gas Co-ops Achievement Award
audience: Children of rural Alberta gas co-op members entering post-secondary
notes: The date is not a submission deadline in the usual sense: the form has to be signed by your local gas co-op, band, town, village or county office no later than October 1 following graduation, so the office you need is a third party with its own hours.

items.text: A PDF application form, with proof of gas co-op membership and your marks

description: Four awards of $1,000 handed out at the FedGas annual general meeting to children of co-operative members of gas utilities in the federation, and to children of landowners serviced by member towns, villages, counties or First Nations. The membership must have been in place a full year, and at least 75% in core subjects is required rather than preferred. Preference goes to fields that apply to the natural gas industry, such as gas utility operator, gasfitter, pipefitter, power engineering and heavy equipment technician, or to rural-based programs.
metaDetail: 75 per cent in core subjects is a floor.

title: CWO Peter Stauffer Memorial Scholarship
audience: Dependents of 4 Wing Cold Lake military, DND and NPF personnel
notes: Application forms come from Mrs. Jennifer Johnson at Cold Lake High. Your high school must be in the City of Cold Lake, Town of Bonnyville, MD of Bonnyville or RM of Beaver River.
description: Three awards of $2,500 from The Medley CFB Society for graduating students who are dependents of personnel currently serving at 4 Wing Cold Lake in the Canadian Armed Forces, regular or reserve, or working there as DND or NPF employees. Created in 2005 at $1,000 and since raised. The criteria go out of their way to say that consistent academic standing does not mean the honour roll: Peter Stauffer never insisted that people be the best, only that they do their best. You submit a 500-word essay on quality of life, leadership or community spirit, two references from outside your family, proof of acceptance and your grade 12 marks.
metaDetail: Three at $2,500; honour roll not required.

title: Billion Barrel Scholarship
audience: Cold Lake area students in their graduation year
notes: The largest single award on the Cold Lake High list and one of the last to close, at the end of July, well after the school year ends.
description: A $5,000 award for a student in their graduation year, asking only for a completed form, your latest transcript and proof of acceptance to a college or university program. No essay, no reference letters and no field of study: for the biggest cheque on the local list, it is also the shortest application.
metaDetail: The biggest local award and the shortest form.

title: Lakeland Credit Union Post-Secondary Scholarship
audience: Lakeland Credit Union members and members' children heading to post-secondary
notes: Two published dates disagree, May 2 on the school list and May 4 on the division list, so the earlier one is used here. Membership is the real gate: half a year in good standing for you, or a full year for a parent.
description: $2,500 for university or college and $1,500 for a trade or technical institute, judged on leadership, community volunteering, school involvement, educational goals, academic achievement, an essay and letters of recommendation. The trades stream at $1,500 is separately funded, so a student heading to an apprenticeship is not competing against university applicants.
metaDetail: Has a trades stream.

title: Lakeland Co-op Scholarship
audience: Graduating students whose family holds a Lakeland Co-op membership
notes: Applications open January 25, nearly four months before they close, and the membership must have been held for at least a year before you apply, so this is one to check at home early.
description: Three awards of $1,000: two for students entering an accredited post-secondary institution and one reserved for a student entering a trades program. Your parent or guardian must be a current Lakeland Co-op member of at least a year, and you must hold a valid diploma from a school in the Co-op trading area. The package is a personal essay, a resume and two letters of recommendation.
metaDetail: One of three is for trades.

title: Grand Centre Lions Club Scholarship
audience: Cold Lake area students with a record of volunteer service
notes: The school lists the amount as $2,000 while the description alongside it says $1,000, so confirm the figure with Mrs. Jennifer Johnson when you request the form.
description: An award from the Grand Centre Lions Club for a young person committed to humanitarian causes who shows the Lions philosophy of active volunteer service in their own community. You submit a transcript, proof of acceptance, up to four reference letters and a one-page essay on why you deserve it. Four reference letters is the most any Cold Lake award asks for, so line them up early.
metaDetail: Accepts up to four reference letters.

title: Cold Lake Medical Development Fund Society Healthcare Education Grant
audience: Cold Lake area residents in full-time healthcare studies
notes: The form is not online. It comes from the Cold Lake Medical Development Fund Society at the Cold Lake Healthcare Centre administration office, 314 25 Street. Two awards are given at each year level.
description: Six awards a year for residents of the Cold Lake district in full-time healthcare studies leading directly to healthcare employment: two of $500 for first-year students, two of $750 for second-year and two of $1,000 for third-year. Because it pays more as you go, it is worth reapplying each year. Preference goes to people who have worked in Cold Lake healthcare and intend to return to it.
metaDetail: Pays more each year, so reapply as you go.

title: Lynn McFarlane Scholarship
audience: Cold Lake students with a disability, or entering disability studies
notes: Applications go by email to Bob Mattice and Audrey McFarlane rather than through the school, and no value is published.
description: Named for Lynn McFarlane, born in Cold Lake in 1966 and diagnosed with Down syndrome at birth, who was one of the first students with a developmental disability to graduate from Cold Lake High School and who then worked at the same Cold Lake pharmacy for thirty years. The scholarship began when she retired in 2018. Two separate routes qualify: being accepted into a disability studies program, or being a student with a disability accepted into any post-secondary program. The application is a single 500 to 1,000 word response covering who you are, what you want to study and why.
metaDetail: Two routes: studying it, or having one.

title: Maynard Metchewais Scholarship
audience: Cold Lake students with attendance and twenty hours of sports involvement
notes: Contact Shawn Metchewais for the form. The bar is deliberately reachable rather than competitive, so read the four conditions as a checklist.
description: A $1,000 award with four plain conditions: full-time enrolment, a 60% class average, 80% attendance, and twenty hours of sports involvement through school or organized sport. The twenty hours do not require you to play. Timekeeping, scorekeeping, officiating or general help at any sporting event all count, which makes this one of the few athletic awards a non-athlete can win.
metaDetail: Scorekeeping counts toward the hours.

title: Beaver River Fish and Game Bursary
audience: Beaver River Fish and Game Association members going straight to post-secondary
notes: Membership in the Beaver River Fish and Game Association is required, and the award goes only to students continuing directly after their graduation year.
description: A $1,000 bursary for a member of the Beaver River Fish and Game Association. The substance of the application is an essay of 500 to 1,000 words on a current issue facing Alberta or Canadian wildlife or the environment, which has to offer solutions rather than only describe the problem, plus a list of community involvement and extracurricular activities.
metaDetail: Propose solutions.

title: Northern Lights Public Schools Student Leadership Award
audience: Northern Lights graduates who have led in their school for two years
notes: A Northern Lights Public Schools award, so every high school in the division competes for it, Cold Lake High included. The division publishes no value for it.
description: Created by the Board of Trustees to recognise students who have shown exceptional leadership. It asks for a high degree of empathy for others and a leadership role within your school held for at least two years, which rules out anyone who started in grade 12. Apprenticeships count as post-secondary here, alongside universities, colleges and trade schools.
metaDetail: No value is published.

title: Northern Lights ATA Local #15 Scholarship
audience: Northern Lights graduates heading to post-secondary in September
notes: A Northern Lights Public Schools award, so every high school in the division competes for it, Cold Lake High included. Two published figures disagree, three awards of $1,500 on the division site and $1,000 on the school site, and the division also notes each school may grant one of its own students $120. Applications go to president@atalocal15.com.
description: Three awards from the teachers' local for graduating Northern Lights students, decided on an essay of no more than 500 words about a Northern Lights teacher who had a positive impact on your life. That is the whole submission besides the form and a letter of acceptance, and it is a topic no other award in the corpus asks for.
metaDetail: Write about a teacher who mattered.

title: Walter Hayduk Memorial Scholarship
audience: Northern Lights graduates entering the U of A Faculty of Education
notes: A Northern Lights Public Schools award, so every high school in the division competes for it, Cold Lake High included. You may apply only in your graduating year.
description: A $100 award in memory of Walter Hayduk, a teacher, superintendent, trustee and friend of education, for a Northern Lights graduate entering the Faculty of Education at the University of Alberta with a grade 12 average of 80% or better. The money is small and the conditions are narrow, but the field is correspondingly tiny: it wants one specific faculty at one specific university.
metaDetail: One faculty at one university, 80%.

title: Xerox Scholarship Award for Business and Entrepreneurship
audience: Northern Lights graduates entering business or entrepreneurship with a 65% average
notes: A Northern Lights Public Schools award, so every high school in the division competes for it, Cold Lake High included. Two recommendation letters are required, one from your principal and one from a teacher, so ask both well before mid-June.
description: A $1,000 award from Xerox Canada for a Northern Lights graduate entering a recognised business or entrepreneurship program, needing an overall grade 12 average of 65% or better. Priority goes to applicants who intend to return to their home community to start a local business, which is the rare case of an award that rewards planning to come back to a small town rather than leave it.
metaDetail: Prefers locals.

title: Northern Lights Aboriginal Achievement Scholarship
audience: Indigenous graduates of a Northern Lights high school
notes: A Northern Lights Public Schools award, so every high school in the division competes for it, Cold Lake High included.
description: A $1,500 award to help Indigenous youth reach a university degree, a college diploma or a technical certificate. The resume it asks for covers grades 10 to 12 and counts four kinds of involvement equally: student government, sports, Indigenous cultural or recreational activity such as Métis dancing, Pow-Wow dancing, drumming, fiddling or Native art, and Indigenous community activity such as youth councils or the Native Friendship Centre. A one-page statement of career goals and at least one recommendation letter go with it.
metaDetail: Cultural activity counts as much as council.

title: Lakeland FASD Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in the Lakeland FASD service area with an FASD diagnosis
notes: You must be living in the Lakeland Centre for FASD service area at the time you graduate and be in grade 12 at a high school in that area, so both conditions are geographic as well as diagnostic.
description: A $500 award for a grade 12 student diagnosed with Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder who lives in the Lakeland Centre for FASD service area and is planning to attend a post-secondary program. It is the only award in the corpus that names FASD, and the eligible group is small enough that anyone who qualifies should apply.
metaDetail: The only FASD award here.

title: MCSNet Scholarship Program
audience: Graduating students in the MCSNet service area entering computer science or STEM
notes: Eligibility follows the rural internet provider's coverage map rather than any municipal boundary, so check the service area before assuming Cold Lake addresses qualify. Up to four awards go to graduating Grade 12 students going into computer science or another STEM field; marks count for 60% and community involvement for 40%. Send a transcript, a principal or counsellor reference, your acceptance letter and an 800 to 1,000-word essay to marketing@mcsnet.ca between April 1 and August 31.
description: Four awards of $1,000 from MCSNet, the rural Alberta internet provider, for graduating students in its service area who are pursuing computer science or STEM-related studies. An August 31 close makes it one of the last deadlines of the year, which suits a student who decided on a STEM program late.
metaDetail: Four awards.

title: Rural Municipalities of Alberta Post-Secondary Scholarship
audience: Residents of rural Alberta municipalities in their first four years of study
notes: Your municipality has to be a member in good standing of the RMA, which covers municipal districts, counties, specialized municipalities and the Special Areas, so a town or city address does not qualify even when a member county surrounds it. Preference goes to applicants studying in Alberta unless the programme is not offered here. The cutoff is the same late-August date each year and the one shown is next year's.
description: Six scholarships of $1,500 a year from the Rural Municipalities of Alberta, running since 1995, for a resident of an RMA member municipality in the first four years of study with no previous degree or diploma, taking a programme relevant to local government or rural communities.
metaDetail: Rural residency is the gate.

notes: The form is available at the school and on the LCHS scholarships page.
title: Wolf Creek ATA Scholarship
audience: Wolf Creek graduates entering a two-year or longer program
description: The Wolf Creek Local of the Alberta Teachers' Association gives one award of $400 to a student going on to a diploma or degree of two years or more at a recognised institution. Preference goes to someone entering a faculty of education, but the award is not restricted to future teachers.
metaDetail: Prefers education, but any program works.

notes: The school does not publish an amount for this one. The form is linked from the LCHS scholarships page and goes to the Career Centre.
title: Frank Freeman Educational Scholarship
audience: Former Blackfalds School students entering a faculty of education
description: Given in memory of a former principal of Blackfalds School, this award is for a student who attended Blackfalds School and is enrolling in a faculty of education. Preference goes to applicants majoring in social studies, language arts or elementary education. The amount is not published.
metaDetail: Your elementary school decides it.

notes: The form is linked from the LCHS scholarships page.
title: Fred Millar Memorial Award
audience: Lacombe County residents connected to firefighting
description: A $1,000 award in memory of Fred Millar, a fire chief with Lacombe County, for Lacombe County residents. There are three separate ways in: training for a career as a firefighter, volunteering or training with a volunteer fire department, or being the child or dependant of a Lacombe County firefighter who lives in Lacombe.
metaDetail: Three separate routes in, only one of them a career plan.

notes: A letter of acceptance from a post-secondary institution is required. The current application is linked from the LCHS scholarships page.
title: Lacombe & District Chamber of Commerce Annual Scholarship
audience: Lacombe and Lacombe County students tied to a Chamber member
description: Two awards of $1,250 for grade 12 students at a school in the City of Lacombe or Lacombe County who live in Lacombe or the county. The condition most students miss is employment: you must be employed by, or the child of an employee of, a Chamber member in good standing. The Chamber also says it would like recipients to come back and serve the community afterwards.
metaDetail: The employment link disqualifies most people.

notes: Applications are made through kincanada.ca and the window runs October 1 to February 1, which is far earlier than the rest of the Lacombe awards.
title: Lacombe Kinsmen Kin Canada Bursary
audience: Lacombe students entering full-time post-secondary training
description: The Lacombe Kinsmen sponsor entries to the Kin Canada bursary, worth $500 locally and $1,000 nationally. Applicants are judged on school and community involvement, knowledge of Kin Canada and financial need, and must be registering full time in university, college, trade school or a technical institute.
metaDetail: One form, judged locally then nationally.

notes: Two reference letters and a Detailed Academic Report are required. There are two dates: April 29 direct to Lacombe Rotary, or April 27 if you hand it in at the LCHS Career Centre. The earlier one is used here so nobody misses it.
title: Lacombe Rotary District #5360 Scholarship
audience: Graduates of any Lacombe high school
description: One $1,000 award for a student graduating from a high school in Lacombe, weighed on leadership and motivation in school and community activities, academic achievement good enough for admission to the institution of their choice, and a need for financial help. Unlike most of the Lacombe awards this one is open to any Lacombe high school, not just Lacombe Composite.
metaDetail: Open to any Lacombe high school, not just LCHS.

notes: Listed on both the Wolf Creek division page and the Lacombe Composite page. The application is linked from either.
title: Rental Housing Providers Award
audience: Students from Alix, Bentley or Lacombe
description: A $1,000 award for students from Alix, Bentley or Lacombe, decided on what you can show you know about renting a place to live. Proof of enrolment in a trade school, college or university program in the fall after graduation is required before the money is paid.
metaDetail: The subject is renting, and that is the whole test.

notes: Six are available at Lacombe. The award is paid once the student enrols at a post-secondary institution within twelve months. Deadlines are set by each school's scholarship committee; the Lacombe page gives June 15.
title: Wolf Creek Public Schools Scholarship
audience: Wolf Creek students not eligible for the Rutherford
description: Six of these $300 awards are set aside for Lacombe alone, out of twenty across the division, given for contribution to school affairs, personal attributes and community involvement. The eligibility is unusual and worth reading: students who qualify for the Rutherford Scholarship in grade 12 cannot apply, which makes this one deliberately aimed at students whose marks fall below the Rutherford line.
metaDetail: Six of the twenty are Lacombe's.

notes: One is available at Lacombe. Paid on proof of enrolment within twelve months. The Lacombe page gives June 15.
title: Wolf Creek Public Schools CTS Scholarship
audience: Wolf Creek students with a heavy CTS, RAP or Green Certificate load
description: One $300 award at Lacombe for a student taking a significant part of their program in Career and Technology Studies, the Registered Apprenticeship Program or the Green Certificate, who is going on to a related program. Apprenticeship counts as post-secondary here.
metaDetail: Apprenticeship counts here.

notes: Applications are available at the LCHS Career Centre and linked from the Wolf Creek scholarships page.
title: Ellis Nature Centre Environment Scholarship
audience: Wolf Creek students going on in conservation or natural history
description: A $1,000 award to encourage further study in conservation, the environment and natural history. The recipient must start post-secondary in the fall of the year they apply, so it cannot be deferred.
metaDetail: No deferral; start in the fall.

notes: Open to a high school senior accepted at a post-secondary institution or a student already enrolled. The association took applications online and extended the deadline to May 31.
title: Lacombe Fish and Game Association Scholarship
audience: Lacombe and Lacombe County students in conservation fields
description: A $1,000 award for students going into conservation, environmental science, wildlife management or a similar field. Residents of Lacombe or Lacombe County may apply with no connection to the association at all. Everyone else needs two years of membership, their own or a parent's or grandparent's. Applicants must show active participation in conservation or outdoor initiatives.
metaDetail: Lacombe residents skip the membership requirement.

notes: Details and the form are linked from the Wolf Creek scholarships page.
title: Linda Tee Memorial Scholarship
audience: Wolf Creek grade 12 students entering nursing in Alberta
description: One thousand eight hundred dollars for a Wolf Creek grade 12 student registered at an Alberta institution in a nursing degree, diploma or certificate. All three levels count, which is not always true of nursing awards.
metaDetail: Degree, diploma or certificate all qualify.

notes: The station describes the award as up to $2,000, so the amount can be less. A current letter of recommendation is helpful but not required. Applications go to the Career Centre or scholarship committee by April 17.
title: Sunny 94 Scholarship
audience: Wolf Creek students entering music, broadcasting or journalism
description: Up to $2,000 from the local radio station, for a student enrolling within twelve months in an accredited music, broadcasting or journalism program. It is one of the few awards in central Alberta that treats broadcasting and journalism as fundable fields in their own right.
metaDetail: Enrol within twelve months.

notes: The application is online and is handed in at the Career Centre.
title: Bentley Seed Cleaning Scholarship
audience: Graduates of Lacombe, Rimbey, Alix, Bentley, Eckville and CACHS
description: A $1,000 award for graduating students of Lacombe, Rimbey, Alix-MAC, Bentley, Eckville and CACHS. Applicants need a graduating average of at least 70 per cent, must be registered in a post-secondary program, and must have lived in the area for the past three years. Preference goes to agriculture-related study.
metaDetail: Three years local, and a 70 per cent floor.

notes: No application, but the admission average is calculated from at least five approved academic courses on a government-issued grade 12 transcript, and GED students are not eligible. Above 95 per cent, the President's Award for Superior Academic Achievement applies instead. Burman publishes no calendar date for this one. The university's scholarship submission deadline governs it, and that moves each year, so check the Burman deadlines page once you have an offer of admission.
title: Burman University Academic Excellence Scholarship
audience: First-year students entering Burman University in Lacombe
description: A renewable entrance award at Burman University in Lacombe, given automatically on the admission average with no application: $3,500 a year at 90 to 94.9 per cent, $2,000 at 85 to 89.9, $1,000 at 80 to 84.9 and $500 at 75 to 79.9. It can be renewed for up to four years of a four-year degree.
metaDetail: Paid on the admission average, with nothing to apply for.

notes: Requires admission to Burman, twelve completed credits excluding PLAR and audits, and Canadian citizenship or permanent residence. Students receiving a second degree discount or a full-tuition scholarship are not eligible. Winter entrants may receive half if funding allows. Burman publishes no calendar date for this one. The university's scholarship submission deadline governs it, and that moves each year, so check the Burman deadlines page once you have an offer of admission.
title: Burman University Central Alberta New Students Scholarship
audience: New Burman students living within 100km of Lacombe
description: One thousand dollars for new students beginning first year at Burman who live within 100 kilometres of the Lacombe campus. The university names Olds, Rocky Mountain House, Leduc and Stettler, and includes the cities along the QE2 corridor between and including Edmonton and Calgary, so the catchment is far wider than the name suggests. Everyone who qualifies is paid.
metaDetail: The 100km catchment reaches Edmonton and Calgary.

notes: Transcripts, proof of citizenship, English proficiency scores and the application fee all have to be in by February 1. Students receiving a second degree discount are not eligible, and a student who defers to the winter term may receive $500 instead.
title: Burman University Early Admission Tuition Scholarship
audience: Students who complete a Burman application by February 1
description: One thousand dollars for applicants who complete their Burman application, including every supporting document, by February 1 for the following September. It is the cheapest thousand dollars on this page: the only thing being rewarded is doing the paperwork early.
metaDetail: Paid for applying early, nothing else.

notes: Requires fifteen academic credits each term, three more than most Burman awards. A confirmation letter from your principal confirming class standing goes to the university. Winter starters may get half. Burman publishes no calendar date for this one. The university's scholarship submission deadline governs it, and that moves each year, so check the Burman deadlines page once you have an offer of admission.
title: Burman University President's Award for Valedictorians
audience: Valedictorians entering Burman University
description: A one-time $3,000 award for the valedictorian of any high school graduating class in Canada, the United States, Bermuda or the Bahamas who comes to Burman in the fall directly after graduation. Everyone who qualifies is paid.
metaDetail: Every qualifying valedictorian is paid, not just one.

notes: A confirmation letter from your principal confirming class standing goes to the university. Winter starters may receive half. Burman publishes no calendar date for this one. The university's scholarship submission deadline governs it, and that moves each year, so check the Burman deadlines page once you have an offer of admission.
title: Burman University President's Award for Salutatorians
audience: Salutatorians entering Burman University
description: A one-time $1,500 award for the salutatorian of any high school graduating class in Canada, the United States, Bermuda or the Bahamas who starts at Burman in the fall after graduation. Twelve credits a term are required, and everyone who qualifies is paid.
metaDetail: Second in your class is worth $1,500 at Burman.

notes: Below a 95 per cent average the Academic Excellence Scholarship applies instead. Renewal is not automatic: it requires a full course load and a 3.9 GPA every year.
title: Burman University President's Award for Superior Academic Achievement
audience: Burman entrants with a 95 per cent admission average
description: A full tuition scholarship, the largest award tied to Lacombe. It goes to first-year students with a Burman admission average of 95 per cent over at least five qualifying academic courses, and covers a minimum of fifteen Burman credits per term. It can be renewed for a further three years on a full course load and a 3.9 GPA each year.
metaDetail: Full tuition, but renewal needs a 3.9 GPA.

notes: The award is paid half in the fall and half in the winter, and you must register in the Orchestra, Camerata Ensemble or another approved group each term, for credit or audit. If no submission is good enough the award may not be given at all.
title: Burman University Orchestral Scholarship
audience: Orchestral instrumentalists entering Burman University
description: Up to two awards of $8,000, the largest arts award anywhere in the Lacombe set. You submit a video of yourself playing an approved piece on an orchestral instrument and the Burman music faculty adjudicates. Strings, woodwinds, brass, percussion and keyboard all qualify, and other instruments may be considered case by case. Preference goes to a student entering a music program, but any student who meets the criteria is eligible.
metaDetail: You need not be a music major to win $8,000.

notes: References are required to verify every claim of service or leadership, and there is a separate reference form. Open to Canadian citizens and to anyone who previously attended a Canadian or American high school or post-secondary institution. Burman publishes no calendar date for this one. The university's scholarship submission deadline governs it, and that moves each year, so check the Burman deadlines page once you have an offer of admission.
title: Burman University Leadership & Service Scholarship
audience: Burman entrants with two years of leadership or service
description: A sliding award of $250 to $2,000 based on leadership and service over the last two years, at school, in the community, at church or elsewhere. Everyone who qualifies receives something; a committee reads the application and the references and sets the amount. One line in the criteria decides most applications: paid positions do not count as service or leadership.
metaDetail: Paid positions do not count as service here.

notes: Twelve credits each term are required. Students receiving a second degree discount or a full-tuition scholarship are not eligible. Burman publishes no calendar date for this one. The university's scholarship submission deadline governs it, and that moves each year, so check the Burman deadlines page once you have an offer of admission.
title: Burman University School of Business Scholarship
audience: New Burman students in a Bachelor of Business program
description: A one-time $5,000 award, limited in number, for newly admitted students starting a Bachelor of Business degree at Burman. It is paid half in the fall term and half in the winter.
metaDetail: The largest single-field entrance award at Burman.

notes: Recipients are notified by August 15. The renewable award requires twelve credits a term, a cumulative 2.5 GPA and a qualifying student loan every year.
title: Richard and Irma Kutzner Entrance Bursaries
audience: Burman entrants receiving a government student loan
description: Four bursaries: three one-time awards of $6,000 and one renewable award worth $2,000 a year, which can reach $8,000 over a four-year degree. You must apply for and receive a Canadian government student loan of at least $8,500, or the American equivalent, and hand the notice of assessment to student financial services. The donors choose the recipients anonymously, on the strength of a short written response and nothing else.
metaDetail: Donors pick anonymously on a written answer.

notes: You must apply for the Alberta Indigenous Careers Award and any other entrance scholarships you are eligible for; this one fills the remainder. Apply or enquire by email to student financial services. It renews each year of a first four-year degree.
title: Mamawi Atosketan Native School Scholarship
audience: Mamawi Atosketan Native School graduates entering Burman
description: A renewable award that covers whatever is left of tuition and mandatory fees at Burman after education authority funding, the Alberta Indigenous Careers Award of $2,000 a term and any other entrance scholarships have been applied. In practice it closes the gap to zero for a graduate of Mamawi Atosketan Native School, the Indigenous school north of Ponoka.
metaDetail: It tops up whatever other funding leaves unpaid.

notes: Applications go to the Kinette Club directly, not through the school, and the club asks for a transcript on school letterhead plus proof of Canadian citizenship or landed immigrant status. It also asks you to write about your own experience of the local Kinette Club, and it says outright not to send resumes, clippings or reference letters. The 2026 deadline was June 1, so look for the next form in the spring.
title: Leanne Wright Memorial Bursary
audience: Wetaskiwin students entering full-time post-secondary study
description: A $1,000 bursary from the Kinette Club of Wetaskiwin, created in memory of a club member who died in 2004 and whose last motion was to stop sending the club's money to the national Kin Canada fund and keep it for a Wetaskiwin student instead. It rewards high ideals and qualities of citizenship.
metaDetail: The club kept this money local on purpose.

notes: The family connection reaches further than most veteran awards, as far as great-grandchildren and great nieces and nephews. The catch is age: the auxiliary states this is not intended for mature students over twenty. It is a separate award from the auxiliary's main command bursaries, so you can be considered for both.
title: Constance Gowers Memorial Bursary
audience: Alberta and N.W.T. students connected to veterans, RCMP, reserves or firefighting
description: A $500 bursary from the Ladies Auxiliary of the Alberta-N.W.T. Command of the Royal Canadian Legion, for a student entering the first term of a certificate, diploma or degree. It is aimed at the child, grandchild, great-grandchild, niece or nephew of a veteran, at descendants of serving RCMP members, and at reservists and firefighters, paid or volunteer, with a year of service.
metaDetail: A Legion Auxiliary bursary with a wide family net.

notes: Two things narrow it. Postgraduate study is not admissible for branch bursaries, and the award is needs-based rather than competitive on marks; the standard is only that you are likely to succeed. A student who finished high school and took a break still qualifies.
title: Royal Canadian Legion Branch Bursary (Wetaskiwin)
audience: Descendants of Canadian and Commonwealth forces members
description: A needs-based Legion bursary for students whose parent, grandparent or great-grandparent served or is serving in the Armed Forces of Canada or the British Commonwealth forces. It is meant to bridge the gap between what a student needs and what family, work and government assistance provide.
metaDetail: It bridges the gap the loans leave behind.

notes: The fifteen credit requirement is the one that stops people, and it has to be in the automotive field specifically, evidenced by a transcript. At least one letter of reference is required. The application asks what car you would most like to work on, so the club is reading for genuine enthusiasm rather than marks. The 2026 deadline was May 29.
title: Central Alberta Vintage Auto Club Bob and Jean Spencer Scholarship
audience: Central Alberta students entering automotive trades
description: A $1,000 scholarship from the Central Alberta Vintage Auto Club for a graduating student entering automotive body or mechanical work. You need at least fifteen credits already earned in that field and either a place in an automotive pre-employment programme at an Alberta post-secondary institution or an apprenticeship already arranged.
metaDetail: Fifteen automotive credits are the entry price.

notes: The three year residency window is unusually generous: a student who moved away for work or a first year of study still qualifies. County policy allows you to receive this bursary only once. Participation in 4-H or agricultural fairs is described as desirable rather than required. Applications go to the Director of Agricultural Services and are reviewed by the Agricultural Service Board at its first meeting after the deadline; the county's page still shows the previous year's October 1 date.
title: County of Wetaskiwin Agricultural Bursary
audience: County of Wetaskiwin residents entering agriculture
description: Five bursaries of $1,000 each from the County of Wetaskiwin for students entering a post-secondary faculty relating to agriculture. You must be a current resident of the County of Wetaskiwin No. 10, or have been one within the last three years, and you must send a copy of your acceptance letter with the application.
metaDetail: Five awards of $1,000 for county residents.

notes: Two gates and no more: you graduated from a school inside the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo, and you carried an 80 per cent average. There is no essay and no reference letter in the criteria. Keyano runs this as a standing programme rather than a one-off competition, so check the admissions page for the current year's application window.
title: Keyano College Excellence Award
audience: Wood Buffalo high school graduates with an 80 per cent average
description: Free first-year tuition at Keyano College for a student entering from a secondary school inside the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo with an average of 80 per cent or better. It is the largest single thing a Fort McMurray graduate can win and it is not a competition against the whole province, only against the region.
metaDetail: Free first-year tuition at 80 per cent.

notes: It is a voucher rather than a cheque, so it pays tuition and books rather than rent. Military service counts alongside volunteering, which is unusual. With sixty awards on offer the odds here are better than on almost anything else a Fort McMurray student can apply for.
title: Keyano Board of Governors Local Leaders Entrance Award
audience: Wood Buffalo students entering Keyano who are active in the community
description: Sixty awards of $1,000, issued as a voucher against tuition or eligible costs such as books, for students who represent the Wood Buffalo region through extracurricular activity, volunteer work, military service or community initiatives. Sixty recipients makes it the widest award anywhere in this directory.
metaDetail: Sixty $1,000 vouchers for community builders.

notes: Certificate and degree students are not eligible; it has to be a diploma. Marks and financial need count equally.
title: Alberta Blue Cross Entrance Award
audience: Students entering the first year of a Keyano diploma
description: One award of $1,000 for a student in the first year of any diploma programme at Keyano. It is one of the few awards in the book restricted to first-year students, which removes the continuing students you would otherwise be competing against.
metaDetail: Diplomas only, not certificates.

notes: The booklet says the Indigenous preference is a preference and not a bar, so everyone else is still considered. What actually narrows the field is that your programme must be one you started this academic year.
title: ATCO Award (Keyano)
audience: Students starting a new programme at Keyano
description: One award of $1,200 from ATCO for a student in a new post-secondary programme in the current academic year, judged on academic achievement and financial need, with preference given to a student of Indigenous ancestry.
metaDetail: Indigenous preference, not a bar.

notes: This is scored one hundred per cent on academic achievement, so financial need will neither help nor hurt. It is one of the few pure merit awards in the book.
title: GKO Entrance Scholarship
audience: First-year Keyano students in a new programme
description: One award of $1,700 from GKO Design Consultants for a student entering the first year of a new post-secondary programme, judged entirely on academic performance together with self-motivated and enthusiastic participation in class and student activities.
metaDetail: Judged on marks alone, no need component.

notes: This is one of the few Keyano awards written for someone who has just left high school, so your grade 12 activities are the evidence rather than anything you have done at college. Marks and community involvement split the score evenly.
title: Keyano College Community Award
audience: Students entering first-year full-time study at Keyano
description: Two awards of $1,100 for students entering their first year of full-time study, judged on academic merit through high school together with contributions to school and community life showing leadership and interpersonal skills.
metaDetail: Judged on your high school record.

notes: At $360 this is the smallest award in the Keyano book, which is exactly why fewer people bother with it. The same single application form covers it.
title: Lynda Costello Award
audience: Keyano students starting a new programme
description: One award of $360 for a student in a new post-secondary programme in the current academic year, based on academic achievement and financial need, with preference given to a female student.
metaDetail: A small award with a light application burden.

notes: There is nothing else in the criteria. If you are in first-year Business Administration you meet the eligibility in full.
title: Three M Shopping Centre Business Administration Program Award
audience: First-year business administration students at Keyano
description: One award of $1,350 for a student in year one of the Business Administration programme at Keyano, judged equally on academic achievement and financial need.
metaDetail: Nothing else in the criteria.

notes: The five tiers mean this award almost never goes unclaimed. A Composite graduate is at the front, but by the fifth tier any education student at the college is eligible.
title: C.D. MacRae Office Administration Award
audience: Fort McMurray graduates in office administration at Keyano
description: One award of $1,000 for an Office Administration student, with a cascading preference: first a former student of Fort McMurray Composite High School, then a graduate of any Fort McMurray high school, then any Office Administration student, then a Composite graduate in the Bachelor of Education programme, and finally any Bachelor of Education student.
metaDetail: A five-step cascade starting at one high school.

notes: Academic achievement is not scored. Need and volunteering split the decision evenly.
title: Keyano Office Administration Certificate Award
audience: First-year office administration students at Keyano
description: One award of $1,000 from the college's own Office Administration department for a first-year student, judged on demonstrated financial need and community involvement, with a letterhead reference confirming volunteer hours.
metaDetail: The department funds this one itself.

notes: University Studies is the transfer route to a degree elsewhere, so this reaches students who intend to leave Fort McMurray after a year or two.
title: Kathy and Bill Fitzgerald Memorial Award
audience: First-year University Studies students at Keyano
description: One award of $500 for any first-year student enrolled in University Studies at Keyano, selected on academic success and financial need.
metaDetail: University Studies is the transfer route.

notes: The booklet says outright that all students are encouraged to apply despite the Indigenous preference, so do not screen yourself out.
title: ATCO Energy and Environmental Technology Award
audience: Students entering environmental technology at Keyano
description: One award of $1,200 from ATCO for a student entering the Environmental Technology programme, judged on academic achievement and financial need, with preference to a student of Indigenous ancestry although all students are encouraged to apply.
metaDetail: ATCO funds it; all may apply.

notes: The published criteria are a single line, which makes this the least demanding award in the entire Keyano book to qualify for.
title: Finning Canada Environmental Studies Award
audience: First-year environmental studies students at Keyano
description: One award of $1,250 from Finning for a student enrolled in an environmental studies programme at Keyano. The booklet lists no academic or financial condition beyond enrolment.
metaDetail: Enrolment seems the only condition.

notes: Another award with a fallback tier, so a first-year University Studies student is a legitimate candidate.
title: Sally Hansen Memorial Commerce Award
audience: First-year commerce students at Keyano
description: One award of $500 for a first-year Bachelor of Commerce student, based on academic achievement and financial need, opening to all first-year University Studies students if no commerce student is eligible.
metaDetail: It opens to University Studies if commerce is empty.

notes: The words recent local high school graduate are in the criteria, which makes this one of the few Keyano awards a student can plan for while still in grade 12. A separate second-year version exists for later.
title: Alberta Teachers' Association Local #48 Award
audience: Recent Fort McMurray graduates entering education at Keyano
description: One award of $500 from the Fort McMurray local of the Alberta Teachers' Association for a recent local high school graduate enrolled in the Bachelor of Education degree at Keyano, based on academic achievement and financial need.
metaDetail: Written specifically for a recent local graduate.

notes: Graduating from a Fort McMurray high school is a hard requirement rather than a preference here, and money plays no part in the decision.
title: Cotter MacGillivray Memorial Scholarship
audience: Fort McMurray graduates entering education at Keyano
description: One award of $1,100 for a student entering the Bachelor of Education programme who is a graduate of a Fort McMurray high school. Selection is one hundred per cent on academic achievement.
metaDetail: Fort McMurray graduates only, decided on marks.

notes: Unlike the other two education awards this one carries no Fort McMurray residency condition, so a student from outside the region qualifies.
title: Kim Farrell Memorial Bachelor of Education Award
audience: First-year education students at Keyano
description: One award of $500 for a first-year Bachelor of Education student at Keyano, judged on overall academic performance and financial need.
metaDetail: First-year education students, no local requirement.

notes: The award commemorates the fourteen women killed at Ecole Polytechnique in 1989. Marks and extracurricular activity split the score evenly.
title: C.I.M. Oil Sands Branch Ecole Polytechnique Memorial Award
audience: Permanent Fort McMurray residents entering engineering at Keyano
description: One award of $1,000 from the Oil Sands Branch of the Canadian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy for a first-year Bachelor of Science in Engineering student who is a permanent resident of Fort McMurray. Proof of residency and a letterhead volunteer reference are both required.
metaDetail: Commemorates Ecole Polytechnique, 1989.

notes: Like the Teachers' Association award, the criteria name a recent local graduate, so this is aimed squarely at someone leaving a Fort McMurray high school this year.
title: James Carter Sr. Memorial Engineering Award
audience: Recent local graduates entering engineering at Keyano
description: One award of $1,300 for a recent local high school graduate in the first year of the Bachelor of Science in Engineering programme, based on financial need and academic achievement.
metaDetail: Written for a recent local graduate.

notes: One of four engineering awards at Keyano restricted to first year, which is a heavy concentration for a small programme.
title: Tony Fullwood Memorial Award
audience: First-year engineering students at Keyano
description: One award of $750 from Jacobs Catalytic for a first-year Bachelor of Science in Engineering student, judged on academic achievement and financial need.
metaDetail: First-year engineering, no residency condition.

notes: Keyano's engineering intake is small and four separate awards are reserved for its first year, so the odds here are far better than the dollar figure suggests.
title: WorleyCord LP Engineering Award
audience: First-year engineering students at Keyano
description: One award of $1,400 from WorleyCord for a first-year Bachelor of Science in Engineering student, selected on academic standing and financial need.
metaDetail: Keyano's largest first-year engineering award.

notes: Because there is one per school rather than one for the city, your competition is your own graduating class rather than every graduate in Fort McMurray. It honours two educators who helped build the public system from 1975 on. Applications come from student services in late April.
title: Jack and Louise Corless Memorial Scholarship
audience: Graduating students at every Fort McMurray high school
description: One award of $500 at each high school in Fort McMurray, recognising leadership and citizenship. The selection committee is told to give particular attention to a student who has overcome personal difficulties or who is in financial need. It is tenable at any accredited post-secondary school.
metaDetail: One award at every high school in the city.

notes: This is one of very few awards in the province open to a grade 10 or 11 student. Nomination comes from your music teacher, and the only thing you write is a short essay on your interest in music and your band experience.
title: Northwinds Marching Band Scholarships
audience: Fort McMurray high school band students in any grade
description: Awards of $300 in each of three categories, woodwinds, percussion and brass, recognising three students at each of the three Fort McMurray high schools. You do not have to be in grade 12, and a music teacher nominates you.
metaDetail: Nine awards, and grade 12 is not required.

notes: The scoring is published in full: one point for an Alberta programme, two for involvement with 4-H or riding clubs or personal riding experience, one for a 70 per cent average.
