Riding experience is worth twice what your marks are. The third tier opens it to any student in any Alberta programme, so it is worth applying even with no horse in your life. A short essay and proof of acceptance are required, and the winner writes back to the club after first term.
title: Clearwater Horse Club Equine Scholarship
audience: Fort McMurray graduates entering equine and animal science fields
description: One award of $500 from the Clearwater Horse Club for a grade 12 student eligible for a high school diploma. Equine studies come first, then animal science, veterinary and agriculture, and finally any Alberta post-secondary programme at all. Recipients are scored on a four point scale and ties are settled by drawing names.
metaDetail: A four-point score, ties broken by draw.

notes: At $3,000 this is the biggest thing the public district hands out, and financial need rather than marks is what it turns on. Applications go to student services in March and to the district office in April.
title: Lorraine and Doug Demers Scholarship
audience: Fort McMurray Public School District graduates in financial need
description: One award of $3,000 for a graduating student of the Fort McMurray Public School District continuing into an accredited Canadian programme, with financial need as the central criterion. If no district student applies, it opens to any student in a Canadian post-secondary programme.
metaDetail: The largest local award in the public district.

notes: The age cap is unusual and it cuts the other way from most awards: turning eighteen makes you ineligible, so a grade 12 student with a late birthday should be nominated early. The municipality sets the value and the nomination window each year.
title: RMWB Distinguished Youth Citizenship Award
audience: Wood Buffalo residents under 18
description: A municipal award from the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo recognising young citizens. Nominees must have lived in the municipality for at least a year and must be under eighteen at the time of nomination.
metaDetail: A municipal award for nominees still under eighteen.

notes: There is a ceiling most students miss: you are ineligible if you are already receiving more than $3,500 in other awards. Winning big elsewhere can cost you this one. Northwestern Polytechnic's standard award criteria require two full semesters already completed at NWP, which shuts most of its 359 awards to a student coming straight out of grade 12. Entrance awards are the exception and this is one of them. Applications sit in your NWP account document library once you are admitted.

description: One award of $1,000 for an Alberta resident entering post-secondary study immediately after high school with an 80 per cent average in grade 12, carrying a full course load and holding satisfactory standing through the fall semester.
metaDetail: 80 per cent and a full course load.

metaDetail: For students whose hometown is 100km or more away.

metaDetail: It pays for the extra costs a disability creates.

notes: No marks, no programme, no residency and no need test appear in the criteria. Two of these exist, which makes it one of the least demanding awards on the list. notes: This is the foundation's general award, separate from the Weyerhaeuser and Career and Technology Studies scholarships it also administers. All three run on their own forms and you can hold more than one.
title: Friends of the Foundation Scholarship
audience: Grande Prairie Public School Division graduates
description: Two scholarships of $900 from the Grande Prairie Public School Division Education Foundation, awarded to graduating students of the division and presented at the Striving for Excellence Awards Dinner in October.
metaDetail: Two $900 awards from the division's own foundation.

notes: There is a single award for the division rather than one per school, so the field is every Indigenous graduate in Grande Prairie public schools. Ask student services for the form, since the foundation does not publish it separately.
title: GPPSD Indigenous Scholarship
audience: Indigenous graduates of the Grande Prairie Public School Division
description: One scholarship of $500 from the Grande Prairie Public School Division Education Foundation, available to Indigenous students across the whole division and presented at the Striving for Excellence Awards Dinner.
metaDetail: One award across the entire public division.

notes: This is a closed pool: the only people eligible are those who went through the programme, often years earlier in elementary school. If you were one of them it is one of the least competitive large awards in the city.
title: Reading University Alumni Student Award
audience: Former Reading University participants in Grande Prairie
description: A $2,500 award for former students of Reading University, the Grande Prairie literacy programme, applied for through the programme's own website rather than through a school.
metaDetail: Only past Reading University students can apply.

notes: Improvement rather than achievement is the criterion, so a student who climbed from the fifties to the seventies is a stronger candidate than one who sat at ninety throughout. Each school nominates, and recipients attend a Rotary meeting with a staff member. Ardrossan lists five awards across the town; Bev Facey lists six.
title: Sherwood Park Rotary Club Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students at every Sherwood Park high school
description: Scholarships of $1,000 awarded annually by the Rotary Club of Sherwood Park, one to a student from each Sherwood Park high school. They go to students who have shown significant academic improvement during high school and who have contributed to school or community in line with the Rotary motto, service before self.
metaDetail: One award at each Sherwood Park high school.

notes: This one has to be posted to the Elks at their Eastgate box number rather than filed through a school portal, and the deadline is August 31 each year, well after graduation. That timing is why it gets missed. A conditional post-secondary acceptance is required.
title: Sherwood Park Elks Scholarship
audience: Sherwood Park grade 12 students with financial need
description: Two scholarships of $400 from the Sherwood Park Elks for grade 12 students pursuing post-secondary study who are involved in school or community activities and require financial assistance. Applicants are notified in late September or early October.
metaDetail: Applications are mailed, not submitted online.

notes: The third tier is the one to notice: if no teacher's child applies, any grade 12 student accepted into a Faculty of Education is eligible. A separate application is required and the deadline falls in September, after you have graduated.
title: Elk Island ATA Local #28 Award
audience: Children of Elk Island teachers entering education
description: Two annual scholarships from the Elk Island local of the Alberta Teachers' Association for a child of an Elk Island teacher accepted into a Faculty of Education, with a high level of achievement. If nobody qualifies it opens to the child of any teacher, and then to any grade 12 student accepted into education.
metaDetail: Open to anyone if no teacher's child.

notes: The catchment crosses both school divisions, which is unusual, but you must both live in the boundaries and attend one of their high schools. You need to have already applied to a teacher education programme, not merely intend to. The 2026 deadline was June 15.
title: Delta Kappa Gamma Eta Chapter Education Grant
audience: Elk Island public and Catholic students entering teacher education
description: One grant of $500 from the Sherwood Park Eta Chapter of the Delta Kappa Gamma Society International for a Canadian citizen living within the boundaries of Elk Island Public Schools or Elk Island Catholic Schools, attending one of their high schools, who has applied to a teacher education programme and shows exceptional potential in the field.
metaDetail: It covers both the public and the Catholic division.

title: Johnathan Doody Memorial Scholarship
audience: Male students entering their first year at the University of Alberta
notes: Nothing restricts this to Edmonton students, only to students heading for the University of Alberta, so applicants from anywhere in Alberta qualify. Two Edmonton schools list conflicting September cutoffs and the fraternity publishes none, so check the application form for the current date.
description: Three awards of $800 each from the Epsilon Alpha chapter of Phi Gamma Delta for male students graduating high school and entering their first year at the University of Alberta, judged on friendship, knowledge, morality, service and excellence.
metaDetail: Three awards, and the pool is first-year U of A men.

title: Gordon Scott Memorial Scholarship
audience: Foothills area graduates continuing in the performing arts
notes: The eligible schools are the Alberta High School of Fine Arts and Foothills Composite in Okotoks, County Central in Vulcan, Highwood in High River, J.T. Foster in Nanton, Oilfields in Diamond Valley and Willow Creek Composite in Claresholm. Acting, directing, singing, dancing, writing and technical work all count as participation.
description: A $1,000 award for a graduating student from one of seven Foothills area high schools who is continuing to post-secondary study in the performing arts, is in high academic standing, and has taken part in school or community theatre.
metaDetail: Seven schools share one award, across five towns.

title: Okotoks Royal Canadian Legion Branch 291 Scholarship
audience: Graduates of Foothills Composite or Holy Trinity Academy entering post-secondary
notes: The handbook lists the number of awards but not their value, so ask the branch or student services what it has paid recently. Academic achievement, extracurricular involvement, community involvement, work experience and citizenship are all weighed together.
description: The Okotoks Legion offers two scholarships to graduating students from either Foothills Composite or Holy Trinity Academy who have been accepted into a recognised professional, technological, trade or other approved programme starting within a year of graduation.
metaDetail: Open to both Okotoks high schools.

title: Okotoks Elks Lodge Grade 12 Scholarship
audience: Okotoks grade 12 students with a record of community volunteering
notes: The handbook states that academics are considered secondary to volunteer work, which puts three $1,000 awards within reach of a student whose transcript is ordinary. Holy Trinity Academy students apply too, by emailing the lodge a short essay on where they volunteered, and preference goes to anyone who has volunteered with the Elks themselves.
description: The Okotoks Elks Lodge funds three awards of $1,000 for graduating students attending post-secondary in the year of graduation, selected mainly on volunteer work that has enhanced the community.
metaDetail: Strong marks are explicitly the secondary factor.

title: Big Rock Runners Award
audience: Okotoks runners in grades 10 through 12
notes: Selection runs on a coach's recommendation for team contribution and a teacher's for effort, so this is not decided by finishing times. You must live within Okotoks town boundaries or attend a school in the town.
description: The Okotoks Running Club pays $750 to a graduating grade 12 runner, $150 to a grade 11 and $100 to a grade 10, for a dependable and supportive team member who is working to their full potential.
metaDetail: Pays across all three grades, not just grade 12.

title: Foothills Chartered Accountants Centennial Scholarship
audience: A Foothills School Division graduate heading for an accounting degree
notes: The money is held by the school division and paid out only when you produce a receipt for tuition in a qualifying business degree, so it cannot be spent on anything else. Open across the division rather than to one school.
description: Up to $1,500 a year, paid until the fund is exhausted, for a graduating Foothills School Division student with consistent superior academic achievement and a record of service to their school or the Foothills region, who is entering a university business degree majoring in accounting with the aim of a Chartered Accountant designation.
metaDetail: Held in trust and released against a tuition receipt.

title: Josephine Bews Award
audience: A rural Alberta graduate beginning agricultural study
notes: It appears in the Foothills Composite handbook but the criteria reach every rural high school in the province, so students well outside the Foothills region are eligible. Scholastic achievement and community service are weighed together rather than one gating the other.
description: A $500 award for an Alberta resident who has completed high school at a rural Alberta high school, has demonstrated scholastic achievement and community service, and is about to begin study in agriculture at any post-secondary institution in the province.
metaDetail: Any rural Alberta school qualifies, not just Okotoks.

title: Rotary Club of Cochrane U-START Bursary
audience: A Cochrane high school student with demonstrated financial need
notes: Rotary is explicit that a bursary is not a scholarship: the money follows need, not the top transcript. Each school picks its own recipient with the club advising, and Rotary asks that students in the trades be considered alongside academic students. The programme has paid out over $75,000 since 1997.
description: The Rotary Club of Cochrane funds one $5,000 bursary at each of the three Cochrane high schools every year. It is a grant based on clearly demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement rather than on academic excellence alone.
metaDetail: Cochrane's largest award, and need-based.

title: Kiwanis Club of Cochrane Dirk Bannister Scholarship
audience: Cochrane grade 12 students with leadership and volunteer records
notes: Two per school is a far better ratio than a single town-wide competition, so the pool you compete in is your own graduating class. The club has posted a May 7 cutoff while the Cochrane High package lists April 1, so file through your school and treat the earlier date as the real one.
description: The Kiwanis Club of Cochrane, with Bow Valley Credit Union, funds six $1,000 scholarships a year, two at each of Cochrane High, Bow Valley High and St. Timothy. They recognise outstanding leadership and a strong commitment to volunteering in the Cochrane community.

description: One of the district scholarships the Calgary Catholic School District names for its students, awarded in the fine arts. Applications go to the scholarship coordinator in your school's Student Services rather than to the district directly.

title: Mary Ngo Family Bursary

metaDetail: Need-based, so marks are not the deciding factor.

notes: Twelve awards, and the draw is what makes this one worth the fifteen minutes: if more eligible students apply than there are scholarships, the recipients are picked at random rather than ranked, so a middling transcript costs you nothing. description: The Calgary Catholic Teachers' Association, ATA Local 55, funds these from its own members' fees, and the parent connection is the hard requirement: your parent must be an active Local 55 certificated teacher.

description: A $500 bursary from the Kinette Club of Coaldale for a Canadian citizen registering at a post-secondary institution in the fall who has shown dedication and service to the Coaldale area community.

metaDetail: Four departments, one award each.

title: Kinsmen Club of Red Deer General Entrance Scholarship
audience: Central Alberta residents entering Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. No single one of the three criteria carries it, so a student who is solid on community involvement and can show need is competitive without a standout transcript.
description: The Kinsmen Club of Red Deer funds a $1,000 entrance scholarship for a Central Alberta resident starting full-time studies at Red Deer Polytechnic, weighed on academic achievement, financial need and leadership in the community.
metaDetail: Residency, need and leadership weighed together.

title: Lampard Family Scholarship for Sciences
audience: First-year Bachelor of Science students at Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. Optometry is a preference rather than a condition, so a science student with another career in mind is still eligible. It is the largest science entrance award on the list.
description: A $2,500 award for a student entering the first year of the Bachelor of Science programme at Red Deer Polytechnic, with preference given to a female student planning a career in optometry.
metaDetail: Optometry preference, but not a requirement.

title: Leslie G. Wadey Memorial Scholarship
audience: Recent high school graduates entering Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. There is no programme restriction and no residency requirement, which makes this one of the widest-open entrance awards Red Deer Polytechnic lists.
description: Two awards of $1,000 for recent high school graduates entering full-time studies at Red Deer Polytechnic, judged on academic achievement and leadership.
metaDetail: Two awards, and the criteria are deliberately broad.

title: Alberta Blue Cross Away from Home Scholarship
audience: Students relocating at least 100 kilometres to attend Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. The 100 kilometre rule is the whole filter and it is measured from your hometown, so a student from a small central Alberta community may qualify where a Red Deer student never can. Programmes shorter than two years do not count.
description: A $1,500 award for a recent high school graduate who had to move at least 100 kilometres from their hometown to attend Red Deer Polytechnic full time, in an undergraduate programme of at least two years.
metaDetail: Distance from home is the condition.

title: Alberta Blue Cross Entrance Scholarship (Red Deer Polytechnic)
audience: Alberta residents entering Red Deer Polytechnic from high school
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. Alberta Blue Cross funds separate entrance awards at several institutions, so this is not the same award as the ones at Augustana or Keyano and you would apply through whichever college you are attending.
description: A $1,500 entrance scholarship for a recent high school graduate who is an Alberta resident, registered full time in an undergraduate programme of at least two years at Red Deer Polytechnic.
metaDetail: Alberta Blue Cross funds one at each college.

title: Barrier Free: An Alberta Blue Cross Bursary
audience: Students with special needs facing extra costs at Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. The award is written around the additional cost of attending rather than around the disability itself, so the case to make is a practical one about what your education actually costs you.
description: A $1,500 bursary for a recent high school graduate entering Red Deer Polytechnic full time who, because of special needs, has to carry extra expenses to attend.
metaDetail: For costs disability adds, not tuition.

title: EQUS Business Rural Community Scholarship
audience: Rural students entering business studies at Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. The certificate and diploma count alongside the degree, which is unusual: most business entrance awards want a degree student. The rural connection is what the sponsor is looking for.
description: EQUS funds a $750 award for a recent high school graduate entering the first year of the Bachelor of Business Administration, the Business Diploma or the Business Certificate at Red Deer Polytechnic.
metaDetail: All three business credentials qualify.

title: Ethel Olafson Bachelor of Education Scholarship
audience: Students entering the Bachelor of Education at Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. The Olafson endowment funds a second entrance award for science students, so a candidate deciding between education and science should look at both before choosing which to argue for.
description: An $800 entrance award for a student starting full-time Bachelor of Education studies at Red Deer Polytechnic, on academic achievement and financial need.
metaDetail: One of a pair funded by the same endowment.

title: Narfi Olafson Memorial Entrance Scholarship
audience: Students entering the Bachelor of Science at Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. The agriculture and environmental conservation preference narrows the real field considerably, because most science entrants at the polytechnic are not in those streams.
description: An $800 entrance award for a student starting full-time Bachelor of Science studies at Red Deer Polytechnic, with preference for those in agriculture or environmental conservation streams.
metaDetail: Agriculture and conservation get the preference.

title: Wendy Cawson Memorial Engineering Entrance Academic Award
audience: Students entering Bachelor of Science in Engineering at Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. Academic achievement is the only stated criterion, with no financial need test, no essay and no leadership requirement, which makes it the most straightforward large award on the list.
description: A $3,000 entrance award for a recent high school graduate starting full-time studies in the Bachelor of Science in Engineering at Red Deer Polytechnic, judged on academic achievement alone.
metaDetail: Marks alone; no essay or reference.

title: Ron MacLean Foundation Entrance Scholarship
audience: Students entering Red Deer Polytechnic with a 74 per cent average
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. The 74 per cent minimum is well below the 80 per cent that most entrance scholarships ask for, and community involvement is listed first among the criteria.
description: Two awards of $750 from the Ron MacLean Foundation for students entering full-time studies at Red Deer Polytechnic with a minimum grade of 74 per cent, weighed on community involvement, academic achievement and financial need.
metaDetail: A 74 per cent floor, which is lower than most.

title: Red Deer Bottling Leadership Scholarship
audience: Students entering Red Deer Polytechnic with a record of leadership
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. No programme is specified and no residency is required, so the deciding factor is the leadership record rather than what you are studying or where you are from.
description: Two awards of $1,000 for students entering their first year of full-time study at Red Deer Polytechnic, on academic achievement and demonstrated leadership through extracurricular activities and community participation.
metaDetail: Extracurriculars carry as much as marks.

title: Norm Jacobs Memorial Bursary
audience: Students entering the Practical Nurse programme at Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. Marks are not mentioned anywhere in the criteria, which is rare for a nursing award and means a student who scraped into the programme is on the same footing as the top of the intake.
description: A $1,500 bursary for a recent high school graduate entering the first year of the Practical Nurse programme at Red Deer Polytechnic full time, awarded on financial need.
metaDetail: Financial need is the only criterion.

title: Red Deer Polytechnic Support Staff Legacy Entrance Scholarship
audience: AUPE members and their families entering Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. This is the kind of award families miss because nobody thinks to check a parent's union. Sponsorship by an AUPE member also qualifies you, so the connection does not have to be a family one.
description: Two awards of $1,500 for students entering Red Deer Polytechnic full time who are members of the Alberta Union of Provincial Employees, immediate family of an AUPE member, or sponsored by one, with Red Deer Polytechnic support staff first in the order of preference.
metaDetail: Check whether a parent is an AUPE member.

title: Georgia Belknap Endowment Early Learning and Child Care Entrance Scholarship
audience: Students entering Early Learning and Child Care at Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. Certificate programmes rarely carry dedicated entrance awards, and the applicant pool for a one-year certificate is much smaller than for a degree.
description: A $1,000 entrance award for a student starting the Early Learning and Childcare Certificate programme at Red Deer Polytechnic, on academic achievement and financial need.
metaDetail: A certificate with its own award.

title: Georgia Belknap Endowment Educational Assistant Entrance Scholarship
audience: Students entering the Educational Assistant programme at Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. The same estate funds a matching award for Early Learning and Child Care, so a student choosing between the two programmes has an equivalent award waiting either way.
description: A $1,000 entrance award for a student starting the Educational Assistant programme at Red Deer Polytechnic, on academic achievement and financial need.
metaDetail: Twin of the early learning award.

title: Northlands Academic Upgrading Scholarship
audience: Students entering Academic Upgrading at Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. Upgrading students are almost invisible in scholarship listings, and Red Deer Polytechnic carries three awards aimed at them. Clearly defined career goals is a stated requirement, so the application is about the plan rather than the transcript.
description: A $450 award for a student entering the first year of the Red Deer Polytechnic Academic Upgrading programme full time who can show clearly defined career goals, awarded on financial need.
metaDetail: For upgrading students, who rarely get one.

title: Red Deer Advocate Adult Re-Entry Bursary
audience: Adults returning to study through Academic Upgrading or Open Studies
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. Open Studies qualifies as well as Academic Upgrading, which widens it past students who left school without finishing. Evidence of career planning is what the application turns on.
description: Three bursaries of $1,600 from the Red Deer Advocate for students entering Academic Upgrading or Open Studies at Red Deer Polytechnic, who can show evidence of career planning and goal setting, awarded on financial need.
metaDetail: Aimed at people returning.

title: Nicole McKenzie Memorial Scholarship
audience: Rocky Mountain House graduates entering Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. Despite being a polytechnic award it is closed to students from Red Deer itself, and mature students aged 22 and over get preference. At $3,000 drawn from a pool of two small-town schools, the odds here are far better than on any open entrance award.
description: Two awards of $3,000 for students entering full-time studies at Red Deer Polytechnic who graduated from Confluence Campus in Rocky Mountain House, meaning West Central High School or St. Dominic High School, with preference for mature students.
metaDetail: Mature students 22 and up get preference.

title: Meagan Kirstein Memorial Entrance Scholarship
audience: Rocky Mountain House graduates entering Red Deer Polytechnic
notes: Red Deer Polytechnic runs one General Application that closes May 31 and puts you in the running for every award you qualify for, so this is one box on a form rather than a separate submission. Despite being a polytechnic award it is closed to students from Red Deer itself, and mature students aged 22 and over get preference. At $3,000 drawn from a pool of two small-town schools, the odds here are far better than on any open entrance award.
description: Two awards of $3,000 for students entering full-time studies at Red Deer Polytechnic who graduated from Confluence Campus in Rocky Mountain House, meaning West Central High School or St. Dominic High School, with preference for mature students.
metaDetail: One General Application covers it.

title: Central Alberta Human Resources Scholarship
audience: Central Alberta students studying human resources management
notes: Human resources is narrow enough that the applicant pool is small for a $1,000 award. You need a resume, confirmation of enrolment, recent marks and documentation of what tuition actually costs you, so gather the paperwork before the June cutoff.
description: A $1,000 award, given annually to a Central Alberta resident enrolled in or planning to enrol in a post-secondary programme focused on human resources management.
metaDetail: A field almost nothing else funds.

title: Murray Family Career Opportunity Award
audience: Central Alberta students entering a diploma or degree, with a leaning toward athletics or mechanics
notes: Technical institutes count equally with universities here, which suits a student heading into the trades. You need two signed and dated reference letters with phone numbers, a grade 11 and 12 transcript, and proof of enrolment, and you can defer if you explain why.
description: An award from the Murray family for Central Alberta students enrolling at a post-secondary institution or technical institute in a diploma or degree programme, open across fields with a stated preference for athletics or mechanics.

title: Burns Memorial Fund High School Bursary Program
audience: Low-income Calgary students in their final two semesters of grade 12
notes: Unusually, the money is paid while you are still in high school rather than after it, and attendance and marks are checked every month. You need a referral from your school counsellor and an interview with the Grants Manager, so start with Student Services rather than the form. Applications close April 30 each year.

items.text: A referral from your high school counsellor, on their own form
The application form
An interview with the Grants Manager

description: A living allowance for Calgary grade 12 students whose finances are getting in the way of finishing, covering everyday costs like rent, food and transportation rather than tuition.
metaDetail: Paid during grade 12, not after it.

title: Senator Patrick Burns Legacy Scholarship
audience: Calgary grade 12 students in low-income circumstances
notes: The fund does not publish a fixed closing date or a fixed value, and both the number of awards and the amounts change year to year. The application asks for grade 10 to 12 transcripts, a letter about your plans, financial documents and a counsellor referral form, so it takes longer to assemble than most. Checked 2026-09-08: the fund's own scholarships page says the application period is now closed, and it publishes no reopening date, so this sits as a next-cycle listing rather than an open one.
description: The Burns Memorial Fund scholarship for Calgary students who are graduating by June, living on a low income, and heading to post-secondary in September.
metaDetail: Value and count change every year.

title: Inspiring Futures Scholarship
audience: Calgary grade 12 students who are parents themselves
notes: This is the parenting-student twin of the Legacy scholarship at the same fund, with the same documents and the same September start requirement, so a student who qualifies for both should ask which application covers which. Neither the value nor the number of awards is fixed. Checked 2026-09-08: the fund's own scholarships page says the application period is now closed, and it publishes no reopening date, so this sits as a next-cycle listing rather than an open one.
description: A Burns Memorial Fund award for Calgary students who are raising a child while finishing high school and are going on to post-secondary in the fall.
metaDetail: For parenting students, on a low income.

title: Burns Fire Fund Post-Secondary Grant
audience: Children of serving, retired or deceased Calgary firefighters
notes: You reapply every year, and the cap is four years of funding with the first application made before your 25th birthday. Stepchildren qualify where the firefighter has been financially responsible for at least three years before the child turned 18, but grandchildren never do. The next cycle opens in November 2026.
description: An education grant from Senator Patrick Burns' bequest for the children of Calgary Fire Department members, paid toward full-time study at an accredited post-secondary institution.

title: Burns Police Fund Post-Secondary Grant
audience: Children of serving, retired or deceased Calgary police officers
notes: Retired counts only after 20 years with the service, or at any length of service if the officer left on a disability. Full-time means at least three credit courses. Late applications are refused outright, so apply by the June date even if you have not settled on a school or a program yet.
description: The Calgary Police Service counterpart to the Fire Fund grant, funded by the same bequest and paying the children of officers toward post-secondary study.

title: Open Door Bursary
audience: Low-income Calgary youth aged 16 to 25 with no other funding
notes: It pays for the things other awards will not touch: application fees, upgrading courses to qualify for a program, supplies, short training tickets such as security or food handling, and even work boots for a first job. Anyone already attending post-secondary is excluded, which is what makes it useful in the gap year. One exclusion the page states plainly and this listing was missing: applicants who have attended or are attending a post-secondary program are not eligible.

description: A Burns Memorial Fund bursary for Calgary youth who do not meet the criteria of any other bursary, aimed at getting them into education, training or work.
metaDetail: For students other bursaries turn away.

title: Local 38 Heritage Scholarship Award
audience: Children of Calgary Public Teachers, ATA Local 38 members
notes: There are two sets of guidelines under one name. The first is the merit stream, which asks for an 80% average across five 5-credit grade 12 courses, or 75% for a student with an Alberta Education identified learning need. The second is for students with developmental disabilities entering a vocational program, and it is judged on its own terms. A retired or deceased member still counts as a member. Local 38 runs its awards through a members-only portal, so the opening date is not published anywhere public; all four of its awards share the end-of-May closing date and one application site.
description: The main award from the union representing Calgary public school teachers, open to the child, stepchild or ward of a current, retired or deceased Local 38 member.
metaDetail: Two streams: 80 per cent merit, or vocational.

title: John Laurie Scholarship
audience: Indigenous students at Calgary Board of Education schools
notes: One award a year, so the field is the whole public board rather than your school. John Laurie taught at Calgary's Crescent Heights and spent much of his life working alongside Treaty 7 leaders, which is why his name sits on the union's Indigenous award. The amount is only published in the portal during the application window. Local 38 runs its awards through a members-only portal, so the opening date is not published anywhere public; all four of its awards share the end-of-May closing date and one application site.
description: The Calgary Public Teachers award for an Indigenous student of outstanding merit in the Calgary Board of Education, funded by the union rather than by the district.
metaDetail: One award across the whole public board.

title: Violet King Scholarship
audience: Black students at Calgary Board of Education schools
notes: Violet King graduated from Calgary's Crescent Heights and became the first Black woman called to the bar in Canada, in Alberta in 1954. All four Local 38 awards share one closing date at the end of May and one portal, so a single trip through the site covers whichever of them you qualify for. Local 38 runs its awards through a members-only portal, so the opening date is not published anywhere public; all four of its awards share the end-of-May closing date and one application site.
description: Named for Alberta's first Black female lawyer, this Local 38 award recognises a Black student of outstanding merit within the Calgary Board of Education.
metaDetail: Alberta's first Black woman lawyer.

title: TIES Founder's Scholarship
audience: Calgary students entering a field that serves newcomers to Canada
notes: Your program has to start within a year of applying, so a grade 12 student can apply on next year's acceptance. The essay is the whole application: 750 to 1,000 words naming a specific barrier immigrants face and proposing something concrete to fix it. Recent winners have been university students with running non-profits, so a strong idea matters more here than a strong transcript.
description: One award a year from The Immigrant Education Society, for a Calgary-area student training in non-profit management, social innovation, international relations, immigrant consultation or a related field.
metaDetail: The essay is the whole application.

title: CKSF Special Talent Award
audience: Korean-Canadian grade 11 and 12 students with a non-academic talent
notes: The geography is set by where your parent lives, not your school: anywhere south of and including Airdrie qualifies, which the foundation spells out as reaching Lethbridge and Medicine Hat, while families north of Airdrie are refused. Children of work permit holders may apply. The application instructions on the same page still carry dates from an older cycle, so confirm the July close by email before relying on it.
description: The Calgary Korean Scholarship Foundation reserves this one for high school students, judged on talent in music, art or sport rather than on marks.
metaDetail: CKSF's only pre-university award.

title: CCSPE Indigenous STEM Scholarship
audience: Indigenous students starting a STEM program at an Alberta institution
notes: A September deadline is unusual and it works in a graduate's favour: you apply after you have your acceptance, with a confirmation of enrolment letter attached. Open to First Nations status and non-status, Métis and Inuit applicants alike. The society posts only the previous cycle's form, so email ccspe.scholarship@calgary.ca to confirm this year's date.

items.text: A PDF application form, with proof of Indigenous identity

description: One award from the City of Calgary Society of Professional Engineers, decided on a 500-word essay about why STEM interests you and how your actions have affected your community.
metaDetail: Decided on a 500-word essay.

title: CEEA Energy Industry Award
audience: Students entering a petroleum-focused engineering technology diploma
notes: The degree stream needs you to be entering second year or beyond, but the diploma stream accepts first year, which is the door a graduate can walk through: petroleum, mechanical, chemical or instrumentation engineering technology all count. It renews for a second year of a diploma and needs a cumulative 80% and one reference.
description: The Canadian Energy Executive Association pays $8,500 for a diploma or $10,000 for a degree, applied straight to tuition, for students heading into the petroleum industry.
metaDetail: Diploma stream takes year one.

title: Rutherford Scholar Award
audience: The ten highest-scoring Alberta students on their first diploma exams
notes: There is nothing to fill in. Recipients are drawn from the pool of Alexander Rutherford applicants, so applying for the Rutherford is the entire application, and only the first writing of each diploma exam counts. A rewrite cannot put you back in contention, which is worth knowing before you decide to rewrite for a higher Rutherford total.
description: A $2,500 top-up the province gives to the ten highest-scoring students in Alberta, identified from the first writing of the diploma exams.
metaDetail: No separate application exists.

title: Dr. Robert and Anna Shaw Scholarship
audience: Alberta students who graduated this year entering agriculture, engineering, arts, health or trades
notes: Three awards, and the window is the unusual part: it opens August 1 and closes October 31, so you apply after you have started, not during grade 12. Preference goes to a graduate of Sexsmith Secondary School, but it is a preference and every Alberta graduate can apply. Judged on grade 12 standing.

description: One of the few provincial scholarships written specifically for students who graduated from an Alberta high school in the current year and enrolled full-time in the fall.

title: Janet and Horace Allen Science Scholarship
audience: Alberta students who graduated this year and enrolled full-time in post-secondary
notes: The word science is in the title and in the government summary, which names accomplishments in the sciences, but the published eligibility list itself asks only that you graduated from an Alberta high school this year and are enrolled full-time. Preference goes to a graduate of Crowsnest Consolidated High School. One award, autumn window.

items.text: An Alberta Student Aid account (or the paper form), between August 1 and October 31

description: A provincial scholarship of $1,500 for a student who finished an Alberta high school this year, with the Crowsnest Pass at the front of the queue.

title: Air Access Bursary
audience: Alberta students in the aviation and pilot training programs at Mount Royal University
notes: A hundred and fifty of these exist and there is no year-of-study bar, so a first-year student qualifies. The province does not run the intake; Mount Royal's awards office does, and it sets the deadline. Full-time here means at least 60% of a course load in both fall and winter, or 40% for a student with a disability. Lifetime maximum of two.
description: The province pays $10,000 to students entering aviation and pilot training at Mount Royal, an unusually large bursary aimed at Alberta's pilot shortage.
metaDetail: 150 available; Mount Royal sets the date.

title: Dr. Gary McPherson Leadership Scholarship
audience: Alberta post-secondary students who lead in improving other people's lives
notes: A hundred awards a year and no year-of-study restriction, which makes it one of the better odds on the provincial list for a first-year student. Leadership in the area of disability is named first in the criteria. You apply to your own institution's student awards office, with a resume and an essay of up to 1,000 words, and each school sets its own date.
description: Named for the Alberta disability advocate, this provincial scholarship rewards leadership and initiative that improved the lives of other people rather than academic standing.
metaDetail: A hundred awards, any year of study.

title: Alex Decoteau Award of Honour
audience: Canadian Armed Forces members and their spouses and children studying in Alberta
notes: Up to two hundred of these are available, which is a large field for a $5,000 award, and there is no year-of-study bar. The service test is specific: the member must have served in a designated military operation, or have been permanently disabled through Armed Forces training. A journeyperson certificate counts as an academic credential here alongside degrees and diplomas. Lifetime maximum of two.
description: Named for the Olympic runner who became Canada's first Indigenous police officer, this award supports returning soldiers and their families through post-secondary study in Alberta.

title: Charles S. Noble Scholarship for Study at Harvard
audience: Alberta students enrolled full-time as undergraduates at Harvard College
notes: Three of these exist and Harvard adds up to $5,000 of its own financial aid on top, so the package can reach $10,000. The application goes to Harvard College, not to Alberta Student Aid. There is no year-of-study restriction, so an Alberta student admitted straight out of grade 12 is eligible in first year.
description: A provincial scholarship that exists for exactly one destination: an Alberta resident enrolled full-time in an undergraduate program at Harvard College.
metaDetail: Harvard may add $5,000 more.

title: Women in STEM Scholarship
audience: Women studying science, technology, engineering or mathematics in Alberta
notes: Fifty awards from a $125,000 pool. Read the timing carefully: high school students are explicitly barred even when they already hold an offer for a STEM program, so a graduating student applies in the September after grade 12, not during it. You may apply to this, the Persons Case and the Women in Technical and Applied Arts scholarships together, but you can only win one in a calendar year.
description: The province funds fifty of these each year for women registered in a post-secondary STEM program in Alberta, full-time or part-time, with no age limit.
metaDetail: You apply the September after Grade 12.

title: Persons Case Scholarship
audience: Alberta students in the arts, humanities or social sciences advancing gender equality
notes: Forty awards, and unlike its two sister scholarships this one is not restricted to women: it is open to any student whose gender is underrepresented or disadvantaged in their field, which is how men in nursing-adjacent and care fields have qualified. Graduate students may study outside Alberta; undergraduates must be at an Alberta institution.
description: Named for the 1929 ruling that made women legally persons in Canada, this $2,500 award goes to students working to advance gender equality in the arts, humanities and social sciences.
metaDetail: Not restricted to women.

title: Women in Technical and Applied Arts Scholarship
audience: Women in technical roles in film, audio production and game design
notes: Twenty awards, and the target is narrow and worth naming: the technical side of the cultural industries, such as audio production, film production and game design, rather than performance or fine art. The province publishes a list of qualifying programs. Like the other two, it opens in mid-September and excludes anyone still in high school.
description: A provincial scholarship for women entering the technical crafts behind Alberta's film, music and video game industries, where they remain underrepresented.
metaDetail: Twenty awards; not open in Grade 12.

title: AEHL Scholarship
audience: Current and just-graduated Alberta Elite Hockey League U18 AAA players
notes: Sixteen awards, roughly one per U18 AAA team, which makes the field your own dressing room rather than the province. You can still apply up to one year after your last registered season. The money never reaches you directly; it is paid to your institution, and you have five years to collect it before it is forfeited. The league page gives only a January opening, so the March date comes from Hockey Alberta's own announcement.
description: The Alberta Elite Hockey League has paid out more than $500,000 since 2006, weighing character, hockey ability, marks and financial need together.
metaDetail: Sixteen awards, roughly one per U18 AAA team.

title: Ringette Alberta Scholarship
audience: Registered Ringette Alberta players entering full-time post-secondary studies
notes: Five awards in 2026: four at $1,500 and one at $2,000. The summer window is the thing to note, because it opens June 1 and closes August 7, after most school awards are long decided, so it is worth keeping on a list for the summer rather than the spring. You need a ringette resume, a personal letter, two references and a transcript.
description: Ringette Alberta rewards players who kept up both their marks and their commitment to the sport, on the ice and off it, as they move into post-secondary study.
metaDetail: A summer deadline, long after the spring rush.

title: Cara Brown Scholarship
audience: Elite ringette players entering a Canadian university full-time for the first time
notes: Two awards a year, and the first-time condition means this one is aimed squarely at graduating students rather than at players already partway through a degree. Elite here means AA, or the highest level offered where you live, so a small community is not penalised for having no AA team. Applications go to the Ringette Canada office.
description: Funded by a former World Ringette Championship captain, this award pairs academic excellence with play at the top level your community offers.
metaDetail: AA, or the best near you.

title: Agnes Jacks Scholarship Awards
audience: Ringette players, coaches and officials heading to post-secondary study
notes: Coaches and officials qualify alongside players, which is unusual and useful: refereeing or coaching a younger division counts as commitment to the sport here. Ringette Canada’s board decides how many are given in a year, so the number is not fixed. Named for the widow of the sport’s founder, who spent decades promoting it.
description: Ringette Canada gives a variable number of $1,000 awards to people who have shown a strong commitment to the sport, whichever side of the boards they are on.
metaDetail: Coaches and referees count too.

title: Michael Vaughan Spirit of Sport Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 multi-sport athletes at School Sport Alberta member schools
notes: The third and least-known of School Sport Alberta's three scholarships, and the criteria are about character rather than results: putting teammates first, enhancing culture, servant leadership. You need three written answers of up to 500 words each and two references, at least one from a teacher or coach in your sport, and neither may be a family member. You must already hold an acceptance. The value is not published.
description: For a grade 12 athlete who plays several sports, one of them a School Sport Alberta sport, and who is held up as a role model by the rest of the school.
metaDetail: Judged on sportsmanship, not on winning.

title: Mary Kehoe Memorial Scholarship
audience: High school students who are AUPE members or their dependants
notes: The union created this in 2017 specifically so high school students would stop losing to university students in one shared pool, so the two awards here are the whole field. Your parent needs two consecutive years of AUPE service and you must be under 25. The essay is marked by independent adjudicators and has to be formal: title page, footnotes, citations, bibliography.
description: Two awards from the Alberta Union of Provincial Employees, ring-fenced for high school students, funded through the Members' Education Assistance Fund.
metaDetail: High school students compete only against each other.

title: Brent Gawne Memorial Scholarship
audience: Post-secondary students who are AUPE members or their dependants
notes: Set up at the union's 2004 convention to raise awareness of the privatization of public services, which is the subject the essay circles. It is the post-secondary half of the pair, so a graduate applying in the summer before first year should check with the education sub-committee which stream they fall into. Same July cutoff and the same formal essay rules.
description: Two AUPE awards for students already in post-secondary study, the twin of the high school scholarship the union runs alongside it.
metaDetail: The post-secondary half of a matched pair.

title: AUPE Members' Education Assistance Bursary
audience: AUPE members, their spouses and their dependants in full-time study
notes: Unlike the two scholarships beside it there is no essay, so it is much less work for the same summer deadline. How much is paid out each year depends on the interest the fund earned. First-time applicants may be given preference, and priority goes to students who have not had it before. Dependants of retired and deceased members qualify too.
description: A need-based bursary from the interest on the Alberta Union of Provincial Employees education fund, open to members and to the family members they support.
metaDetail: No essay, unlike the union's scholarships.

title: Livingstone Range ATA Local #14 Scholarships
audience: Livingstone Range School Division graduates and the children of its teachers
notes: Six awards in two streams, and the streams have different gates. Three entrance scholarships go to students whose parent teaches in the division, and those can be used in any faculty anywhere. The other three go to any Livingstone Range graduate enrolled in a Faculty of Education. The entrance stream is first year only, so it is now or never. Verified 2026-09-09: the local rebuilt its site and the old application.html now 404s, so this points at the current scholarship page. One useful detail from the criteria, since it saves a calculation: the entrance stream is selected on the highest high school average, computed the same way as the Alexander Rutherford Scholarship. A student may hold only one of the six in a year and cannot win twice. Cheques go out in December once enrolment is verified, and applications go by mail to the Local in Blairmore.
description: The teachers of the Livingstone Range division, covering Claresholm, Pincher Creek and the Crowsnest Pass, fund six of these a year out of their own local.
metaDetail: Two streams of awards.

title: John Hasselfield Endowment Foundation Scholarship
audience: Alberta public school students facing obstacles outside their control
notes: The foundation keeps no website of its own and is advertised through school divisions, so your career practitioner is the reliable route in. The essay is about 500 words and asks three specific things: how and when you would use the money, what you have already put toward the goal, and what is standing in the way. Older division lists put the award at $400, which is worth confirming.
description: A small Alberta foundation supporting young people whose desire to keep learning, or to keep at sport or music, is blocked by circumstances they did not choose.
metaDetail: Advertised only through school divisions.

title: Pattison Media Equity Scholarship
audience: Western Canadian journalism and broadcast students from under-represented groups
notes: Western Canada only, despite the national scope of the page: recent recipients came from SAIT, Mount Royal, Red River and BCIT. The four named groups are Indigenous people, people with disabilities, members of visible minorities, and women. It used to be called the Prairie Equity Scholarship, which is the name still printed on most school lists. Pattison does not post a closing date; ask the program office at your institution.
description: Four awards from the broadcaster behind a large share of western Canadian radio and television, aimed at the groups its own newsrooms are short of.
metaDetail: Still listed elsewhere as Prairie Equity.

title: Beaverlodge Community Band Fund
audience: Beaverlodge-area students carrying on in music
notes: Beaverlodge sits about 40 kilometres west of Grande Prairie, and awards like this one are the reason the universal application is worth filing even if you do not live in the city. One universal application covers every fund the foundation holds, so there is nothing separate to file for this one. The foundation publishes the roster of fund names but keeps each fund's value and criteria inside the portal, which tells you what you qualify for once you submit.
description: A Northwestern Alberta Foundation award endowed by the community band in Beaverlodge, one of the small-town music funds in the Peace Country roster.
metaDetail: A small-town band fund, west of the city.

title: Hythe Colts Women's Hockey Student Award Fund
audience: Women who played hockey in Hythe

audience: Students from the Bezanson area
notes: Bezanson has a K-12 school and no separate foundation of its own, so this fund is the local money and it is reached only through the regional application. description: A community-endowed award for the hamlet of Bezanson, east of Grande Prairie, held among the Northwestern Alberta Foundation's student award funds.

audience: Students from the North Kleskun district

audience: Grande Prairie students, particularly in business

audience: Peace Country student athletes
notes: It is the oldest legacy fund on the roster and the clearest illustration of why the universal application is worth the hour: nobody would think to search for a 26-year-old games surplus. One universal application covers every fund the foundation holds, so there is nothing separate to file for this one. The foundation publishes the roster of fund names but keeps each fund's value and criteria inside the portal, which tells you what you qualify for once you submit.
