metaDetail: A 2000 games surplus, still paying out.

title: Aquatera Environment Fund
audience: Peace Country students in environmental programs
notes: Environmental is one of the named award categories at the foundation, and this is the fund behind it, which matters if you are choosing between an environmental science program and something adjacent. One universal application covers every fund the foundation holds, so there is nothing separate to file for this one. The foundation publishes the roster of fund names but keeps each fund's value and criteria inside the portal, which tells you what you qualify for once you submit.
description: An environmental studies fund endowed by Aquatera, the utility that runs water and waste services for Grande Prairie and the surrounding county.
metaDetail: Endowed by the regional water utility.

title: Utility Safety Partners Scholarship
audience: Alberta students entering trades, safety or engineering programs
notes: Read the academic bar carefully, because it is written twice: entering students need an 80 percent average, while students already in a program need a 3.0 GPA. That first line is the one that matters to you, and it is the reason this award is worth filing in grade 12 rather than waiting. Utility Safety Partners is the organization formerly called Alberta One-Call, the people behind Click Before You Dig, and they want a letter of recommendation plus evidence you care about safety through work, coursework or volunteering. Only two are given each year and the applications run through the ScholarTree platform rather than their own site.
description: A $2,500 award from the organization behind Click Before You Dig, for Alberta students entering skilled trades, power lineperson, health and safety or civil engineering programs.
metaDetail: Two a year; entering students qualify.

title: UNA Nursing Education Scholarship
audience: First-year Alberta nursing students related to a UNA member
notes: This is a relative-of-a-member award, which is the kind almost nobody thinks to check. If a parent, grandparent or guardian is a United Nurses of Alberta member or associate member in good standing, you are eligible and most of the field is not. It is for first-year Registered Nurse or Registered Psychiatric Nurse programs only, so it is an entrance award, and it explicitly excludes postgraduate study. Up to fifteen are awarded plus one funded by the Canadian Federation of Nurses Unions, the essay is a single 300-word answer, and the money is paid the following January once you show proof of full-time first-year registration.
description: Sixteen awards of $1,500 for students starting a nursing program in Alberta who are related to a United Nurses of Alberta member in good standing.
metaDetail: Applications close at 4:30 p.m. on October 15.

title: Don Moore Scholarship
audience: Alberta students in recreation facility operations programs
notes: You do not apply for this one, someone nominates you, and the nomination form takes about twenty minutes. That is worth knowing early because it means telling an instructor or a supervisor at the arena or pool you work at that the award exists. Any year of study counts, including your first, and you do not need to be an AARFP member. Note that several aggregator sites still list this at $750, which is the old value. The association's own awards page says $1,500, and the same page carries the February 15 nomination deadline that applies to every award they hand out.
description: A $1,500 nominated award from the Alberta Association of Recreation Facility Personnel for students in recognized recreation services operation programs.
metaDetail: Nomination-based; membership not required.

title: Alberta Athletic Award
audience: Alberta post-secondary athletes competing in ACAC or AUAA sport
notes: Worth knowing before you pick a school, because this one is decided inside your institution rather than by a provincial committee. Your athletic department selects the recipients and pays them, so the person to ask is your team coach, not Alberta Student Aid, and there is no public deadline. You need to be in your second or subsequent term, which means a student starting in September can be selected in the winter term of first year. The bar is deliberately low at a 2.0 GPA and 60 percent of a full course load, and selection is split evenly between male and female athletes. Upgrading and college preparation students qualify after one term but only for a single year, and apprentices qualify after one period if they are progressing.
description: An $1,800 award from Alberta Student Aid for students competing in a sport sanctioned by the Alberta Colleges Athletic Conference or the Alberta University Athletic Association.
metaDetail: Your school's athletic department picks and pays the recipients.

title: French for the Future National Essay Contest
audience: Grade 10 to 12 students writing in French, immersion or first language
notes: This is the highest ratio of money to effort in the corpus: 750 words in French, and 100 scholarships are handed out from a pool of $388,000. Two categories keep the field fair, so immersion and Core French students compete as French Second Language and are not measured against students who speak French at home. You can enter in grade 10, 11 or 12, which means a grade 10 student can enter three times. The scholarship is tied to studying wholly or partly in French at one of 15 partner institutions, so check that list before you write. Registration runs October 14 to December 18 and the theme changes every year.
description: A 750-word essay in French for grade 10 to 12 students, with 100 scholarships worth $1,000 to $28,000 shared out of a $388,000 pool at 15 partner universities and colleges.
metaDetail: Immersion students have own category.

title: NUPGE Tommy Douglas Scholarship
audience: Children, grandchildren and foster children of NUPGE union members entering first year
notes: A parent or grandparent's AUPE membership can qualify you because AUPE is a NUPGE component. Foster children of members also qualify. It is decided on a 750 to 1,000 word essay about how Tommy Douglas made Canada a more just and equitable society, so it rewards writing rather than marks. You have to be entering the first year of a Canadian public post-secondary institution full time.
description: One of about five $1,500 scholarships the National Union of Public and General Employees awards each year to the children, grandchildren and foster children of its members, decided by essay.
metaDetail: AUPE family qualifies.

title: NUPGE Terry Fox Memorial Scholarship
audience: Students with disabilities whose parent or grandparent is a NUPGE member
notes: You must have a disability, and a parent, grandparent or foster parent must belong to a NUPGE component union, which in Alberta usually means AUPE. The essay is 750 to 1,000 words on why quality public services matter to the quality of life of people with disabilities, so lived experience is the point rather than a disadvantage. Not to be confused with the Terry Fox Humanitarian Award, which is a separate and much larger national program with no union requirement.
description: A $1,500 award for students with disabilities entering first year whose parent, grandparent or foster parent belongs to a NUPGE member union, decided on an essay about public services.
metaDetail: A disability award, union family only.

title: Otipemisiwak Métis Government Community-Based Awards
audience: Métis students registered in post-secondary studies in Alberta
notes: One Google form puts you in for nine named awards at once, so read the list and say which ones fit you. Bruce Gladue, Cecil Bellrose and Marlene Lanz are the three Otipemisiwak Legacy Awards at $2,500. Art L'Hirondelle at $1,000 is for construction and trades, Tom Ghostkeeper at $1,000 is for justice studies, and Gary Pruden at $500 is for music and sports. Delia Gray, Pearl Calahasen and Ernest Poitras are $1,000 and open to any area of study. You need proof of current post-secondary registration, a personal statement about your involvement in the Otipemisiwak Métis community, and a reference letter from a Métis knowledge keeper, leader or active citizen. That registration requirement means you apply in the fall after you start, not while you are still in grade 12. Winners are honoured during Métis Week in November.
description: Nine named awards from the Otipemisiwak Métis Government worth $500 to $2,500, covering trades, justice, music and sport as well as any area of study, all through a single application.
metaDetail: One form covers all nine awards.

title: Métis Scholar Awards
audience: Métis citizens in full-time studies at Alberta post-secondary institutions
notes: This is an endowment program, not a single scholarship. The Métis Education Foundation and Rupertsland Institute have negotiated endowments at 22 Alberta institutions including the University of Alberta, University of Calgary, University of Lethbridge, NAIT, SAIT, MacEwan, Mount Royal, Athabasca, Bow Valley, Concordia, Keyano, King's, Lakeland, Lethbridge College, Medicine Hat College, NorQuest, Northern Lakes, Northwestern Polytechnic, Olds, Portage and Red Deer Polytechnic. Each institution administers its own award, sets its own criteria and its own deadline, so apply directly to the school you are attending and ask their awards office. The University of Calgary runs a separate entrance stream, which is the one to look at if you are coming straight out of grade 12. The October 15 deadline here is for the two awards the Foundation holds itself, which are open to Métis citizens at institutions where no endowment exists. You must be a citizen of the Otipemisiwak Métis Government, a registered member of the Otipemisiwak Métis Student Association, enrolled full time and an Alberta resident, and you cannot be receiving other Rupertsland funding.
description: Métis Education Foundation endowments at 22 Alberta post-secondary institutions, each administered by the school, plus two awards the Foundation holds for students elsewhere.
metaDetail: Calgary runs an entrance stream.

title: Modern Métis Woman Scholarship
audience: Self-identified Métis women entering or attending a Canadian or US university
notes: A small charity award decided on a single essay of 1,000 to 1,500 words, on your definition of the Modern Métis Woman, how your Métis heritage has affected you personally, or any topic you choose that relates to Métis women. Only one award is given each year, so the field is small but so is the prize pool, and the amount is not published. You are eligible if you will be attending university, not only if you already are, so a grade 12 student heading to first year can apply. You must be a Canadian citizen, enrolled full time at a minimum of three courses a semester, and identify as both a woman and Métis. Essays are checked for plagiarism. Submissions go by email.
description: A yearly essay award for self-identified Métis women heading to or already at a Canadian or US university, decided on a 1,000 to 1,500 word essay.
metaDetail: Not only current students.

title: Arctic Institute of North America Jim Bourque Scholarship
audience: Canadian Indigenous students in education, environmental studies, Indigenous knowledge or telecommunications
notes: One award a year, administered by the Arctic Institute of North America at the University of Calgary but open to Indigenous students across Canada. It honours James W. Bourque, who was Cree and Métis, born at Wandering River in Alberta, and who founded the Fur Institute of Canada and was sworn into the Privy Council in 1992. Grade 12 students can apply: the application asks for your most recent transcript from college, university or high school, and accepts proof of application to a post-secondary institution rather than proof of enrolment. You need a cover letter, a 500-word description of your intended program, a recommendation from a community leader such as a band or town council, chamber of commerce or Métis local, a statement of financial need, and proof of Indigenous descent. Applications went in by July 8 in the 2026 cycle. The committee weighs financial need heavily.
description: A $1,000 award for Indigenous students across Canada entering education, environmental studies, Indigenous knowledge or telecommunications, accepting high school transcripts.
metaDetail: Proof of application is enough.

title: BioTalent Canada I.D.E.A.L. Scholarship
audience: Students entering first year of a biosciences program who are Indigenous, have a disability, or are newcomers
notes: Three awards of $10,000, one for each of the three groups: Indigenous students, students with a disability, and newcomers who have been in Canada less than five years. CEGEP students receive $5,000. This is strictly an entrance award and BioTalent says so plainly: students beyond first year or in non-biosciences programs are screened out. Eligible programs are broad and include biotechnology, biochemistry, health sciences, environmental biology and biomedical programs, so anything that leads into the bioeconomy is worth checking. Because it splits three ways by category rather than pooling everyone, the odds are much better than a general national scholarship. You need your acceptance letter. Canadian citizens, permanent residents and newcomers already in Canada qualify, but international students on a visa do not. Applications in the 2026 cycle closed June 8.
description: Three $10,000 awards, one each for Indigenous students, students with a disability and newcomers, for students entering first year of a biosciences program.
metaDetail: First year, one per category.

title: Merck Canada Indigenous Student Scholarship
audience: Indigenous students under 29 entering or returning to a first bachelor degree
notes: Up to eight awards of $5,000, and the program is capped at 60 applications, which makes the odds better than almost anything else at this value. Applying early matters because of that cap. You qualify if you are entering or returning to full-time studies in your first bachelor degree, so a grade 12 student heading into first year is eligible. You must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident and under 29 at the deadline. In the 2026 cycle the portal opened January 20 and closed March 19, and you have to create a user profile before you can apply. Check the program guidelines on the portal for the list of eligible fields of study.
description: Eight $5,000 awards for Indigenous students entering or returning to a first bachelor degree, with applications capped at 60 so the odds are unusually good.
metaDetail: The program caps applications at 60.

title: IPPC Indigenous Pharmacy Scholarship
audience: First Nations, Métis or Inuit students accepted to a PharmD or pharmacy technician program
notes: Run by the Indigenous Pharmacy Professionals of Canada with the Canadian Pharmacists Association. The route worth knowing about from grade 12 is the pharmacy technician stream, funded by the Sobeys National Pharmacy Group at $10,000, because a pharmacy technician diploma is a college program you can enter straight out of high school. The two PharmD scholarships are worth $20,000 a year and matter later, since PharmD programs in Canada generally want undergraduate study first. Being accepted counts, not just being enrolled, so you can apply on an acceptance letter. You must provide verification of ancestry such as a status card, a parent's status card with proof of relationship, or a Métis citizenship card, and you must be a member of IPPC. The application needs a letter of intent of up to 500 words or a three-minute video, plus a reference letter from someone outside your household. Recipients meet annually with IPPC and the sponsor. The 2026 to 2027 cycle has closed.
description: Pharmacy awards for First Nations, Métis and Inuit students worth $10,000 for pharmacy technician studies and $20,000 a year for PharmD, open on acceptance.
metaDetail: The technician stream is open from Grade 12.

title: Ted Rogers Legacy Scholarship
audience: Students entering a technology-focused program at one of six partner universities, including the University of Calgary
description: Ten awards a year worth $100,000 over four years, covering full tuition, living expenses and other costs for students in a technology-focused program. Rogers calls it Canada's largest scholarship program. There is no central application: each partner university runs its own selection, and the University of Calgary is one of the six.
notes: Do not look for a Rogers application form, because there isn't one. The six partner universities are UBC, the University of Calgary, Waterloo, Toronto Metropolitan, Polytechnique Montreal and UNB, and each handles its own nomination and selection. For an Alberta student the practical route is the University of Calgary's own awards process, so ask their admissions office how the Ted Rogers award is assessed there.

title: Canadian Hearing Services National Scholarship
audience: Deaf, deafblind and hard of hearing Canadians aged 17 or older starting or returning to post-secondary study
description: Pays $3,000 to full-time and $1,000 to part-time students, and stays available at the same level for up to four consecutive years. Selection weighs financial and accommodation need alongside community engagement, and Canadian Hearing Services gives additional recognition to Indigenous Deaf and hard of hearing applicants.
notes: The medical bar is specific: a documented hearing loss of 50dB or greater in each ear, not just one. Like the Rutherford, this is applied for once you are enrolled rather than while you are still in Grade 12, so a graduating student applies in the year they start post-secondary. It is not a token programme: Canadian Hearing Services awarded 29 scholarships for the 2025-26 year, to both first-time and returning students, and the money can go to tuition, residence or accessibility services rather than tuition alone. The 2026 round closed April 24 and notified winners in July; the 2027 dates were not posted when this was checked, so expect a late-April deadline and confirm. Applicants must be 17 or older. Re-verified against chs.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Renewable.

title: Burger King Scholars Program
audience: Students graduating from Grade 12 in Canada with a 2.0 GPA or higher, enrolling full-time in post-secondary
description: A North American program that has awarded nearly $64 million to over 55,000 students, and it is open to Canadians rather than US-only. The bar is deliberately low: a 2.0 cumulative average on a 4.0 scale, with selection weighing work experience, extracurriculars, community service and financial need alongside marks.
notes: Employment at a Burger King restaurant is not required for the general track. The 2025 cycle ran October 15 to December 15 and the program describes its 2026 details as tentative, so treat the autumn window as the shape to watch rather than a confirmed date. Awards can be used at an accredited college, university or vocational school in Canada or the United States.
metaDetail: A 2.0 average is enough.

title: Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes
audience: Canadian residents aged 8 to 18 who have organized and led a service project benefiting people or the planet
description: One of the few national awards open well below Grade 12: applicants must be 8 to 18 and not yet 19 on the April 15 deadline. It rewards a service or research project the applicant started and led themselves, and Canadian residents compete on the same footing as American ones.
notes: There are two deadlines, and missing the first ends it: a pre-application closes March 15 and is not accessible after that date, and only applicants judged eligible are invited to the full application by April 15. Both close at 5 PM Mountain Time, which is Alberta time for once. The project must be one you initiated, not a school assignment.
metaDetail: Pre-application closes March 15.

title: CEMF John Evans Engineering Entrance Award
audience: Women entering an accredited Canadian engineering program directly from high school
description: A $5,000 entrance award from the Canadian Engineering Memorial Foundation for a young woman entering an accredited Canadian engineering program from high school. It also carries a potential paid summer engineering work placement with Fortis at one of their Canadian utilities after second or third year.
notes: The foundation states plainly that this award is not based on academic achievement, which makes it unusual among engineering entrance awards and worth applying for on a mid-range average. You must self-identify as a woman and hold Canadian citizenship or permanent residency.
metaDetail: Not judged on marks, and carries a paid Fortis placement.

title: Manulife Life Lessons Scholarship
audience: Students aged 17 to 24 who lost a parent or legal guardian who had little or no life insurance
description: A $10,000 award for students entering college, university or trade school who have experienced the death of a parent or legal guardian carrying little or no life insurance. Manulife describes it as the first Life Lessons program in Canada.
notes: The age window runs to 24, so this stays open for years after Grade 12 rather than closing at graduation. Trade school counts alongside college and university. The 2026 round has closed and Manulife had not posted 2027 dates when this was checked.
metaDetail: Open to age 24, and trade school counts.

title: Spina Bifida and Hydrocephalus Association Bursary
audience: Canadians with spina bifida or hydrocephalus who are SBHAC members in good standing
description: Two bursaries of $1,000, awarded through two intakes a year rather than one. Open to Canadian citizens and permanent residents who have spina bifida or hydrocephalus and hold a current SBHAC membership.
notes: There are two application windows a calendar year, closing at noon on the third Wednesday in July and the third Wednesday in November, but you can only receive one award per year. Membership must be in good standing before you apply, so join first rather than at the deadline.
metaDetail: Two intakes: the third Wednesday of July and November.

title: DCCI Scholarship for Canadian Students with Disabilities
audience: Canadian high school students with a documented disability entering health care, criminal justice, or community and social services
description: A $1,000 tuition award for a graduating Canadian high school student with a documented disability heading into health care, criminal justice, or community and social services at an accredited post-secondary institution.
notes: Unusually for a disability award, this one is aimed at high school graduates rather than students already enrolled. You submit an essay plus proof of graduation and proof of acceptance. The 2026 round closed July 31; the 2027 date had not been posted when this was checked.

title: AEBC and Allyant Scholarship Program
audience: Blind, deafblind and partially sighted Canadian students
description: A $1,000 award from the Alliance for Equity of Blind Canadians, run with Allyant. Judged on academic performance, community involvement and overcoming adversity, with the association stating that the three criteria are weighed together rather than equally.
notes: The most recent posted cycle closed at 1:00 p.m. Eastern on May 30, and the association says it intends to run the program again, so watch the page from the spring. It had not posted the current cycle's date when this was checked.
metaDetail: Judged on adversity and community work as well as marks.

title: CHHA Scholarship Program
audience: Canadian students with hearing loss entering or continuing post-secondary study
description: The Canadian Hard of Hearing Association has run this program for over twenty years, helping students with hearing loss attend post-secondary schooling. It is funded by private donations and by CHHA branch networks across the country.
notes: The association states that applications for the 2027 program open in November 2026, which makes this one of the few national awards with a published reopening month rather than a vague promise. Distinct from the Canadian Hearing Services scholarship, and you can look at both.
metaDetail: Applications for 2027 open in November 2026.

title: Dick Martin Scholarship Award
audience: Students enrolled in an occupational health and safety program at a Canadian college or university
description: Two $3,000 awards a year from the Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety, for students in any occupational health and safety course or program leading to a certificate, diploma or degree. Full-time and part-time students are both eligible.
notes: You apply once you are enrolled rather than in Grade 12, so this is one to note now and act on in your first term. It takes a 1,000 to 1,200 word essay and a cover letter. CCOHS runs a second award on the same page, the Chad Bradley Scholarship, open to women in the same field.
metaDetail: Applied for once enrolled, not in Grade 12.

title: Loans Canada Student Award
audience: Canadian students entering or attending post-secondary study
description: A $750 award decided on a written personal story rather than marks. Applications open January 1 and close July 31, with the winner announced August 31. Past recipients are named publicly, which is a reasonable sign the money is actually paid.
notes: A summer deadline is rare and useful: this stays open through the months when almost every other award has closed. The application is a form plus your story, so it is one of the cheapest applications on the site in time.
metaDetail: Still open through July, when most have closed.

title: EnergyRates.ca Scholarship
audience: Students writing an essay on energy topics, entering or attending post-secondary study
description: A $500 essay award run by an Alberta energy comparison site, with winners named publicly every year since 2022. Essays are submitted as Word, RTF or PDF documents.
notes: The cutoff is 11:59 PM MST, which is Alberta time, so unlike most national awards there is no timezone arithmetic to get wrong.
metaDetail: Closes 11:59 Mountain.

title: BigSun Athletics Scholarship
audience: Student athletes in any sport, in their final year of high school or already in post-secondary
description: A $500 award open to student athletes regardless of sport or the capacity in which they take part, so coaches, officials and team managers are not excluded. The application is an essay about how your participation has shaped you.
notes: The organisation states that AI-generated essays will not be accepted. Recipients are named each year. A June deadline puts it after most of the spring rush.
metaDetail: Any sport or role.

title: Double A Solutions Blitz Scholarship
audience: Students in their final year of high school, transitioning, or enrolled in Canada or the US
description: A $1,000 award on a workplace-themed essay question. The scholarship opens January 1 and closes April 1, and is paid by cheque made out jointly to the winner and the institution they attend.
notes: The eligibility is unusually wide: final-year high school, transitioning, or already enrolled at any level in Canada or the United States. The 2026 round has closed and the page takes email reminders for 2027.
metaDetail: Paid to the school.

title: Pretty Lightroom Presets Scholarship
audience: Students in their final year of high school, transitioning, or enrolled in Canada or the US
description: A $500 writing award run annually on April 15 by a photography presets company. The winning entry is published on the company's blog and the winner is notified about three weeks after the deadline.
notes: Grammar and punctuation are named in the entry requirements, which tells you what the judging actually rewards. Open to Canadian students alongside American ones.
metaDetail: Grammar is judged.

title: Pretty Photoshop Actions Scholarship
audience: Students in their final year of high school, transitioning, or enrolled in Canada or the US
description: A $500 writing award from the same company as the Pretty Lightroom Presets scholarship but on a different annual date, October 15, so a student can enter both in the same school year.
notes: The winner is notified about four weeks after the deadline and the entry is published on the company blog. Same eligibility as its April sibling: final-year high school, transitioning, or enrolled, in Canada or the United States.

items.text: An emailed tutorial essay of at least 800 words, with your own screenshots and photos, on one of five topics
A headshot photo and the mailing address of your school's financial aid office

metaDetail: Winner published.

title: North American Van Lines Logistics Scholarship
audience: Canadian citizens and permanent residents enrolling full-time at an accredited university
description: Four awards of $1,000 each, open across fields of study rather than restricted to logistics despite the name. Applicants must be Canadian citizens or permanent residents attending an accredited Canadian institution.
notes: The application form specifies an accredited four-year degree institution, so a two-year diploma or a trades program may not qualify; confirm with the company before spending time on it if that is your path.
metaDetail: Any field counts.

title: IWSH Essay Scholarship Contest
audience: Students writing on global sanitation and safe water access
description: An essay contest from the International Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Foundation, with awards of $1,000, $750 and $500 on a topic set each year around sanitation and safe water access.
notes: The 2026 contest has closed and the foundation says the 2027 topic will be announced in the spring of 2027, so this is a calendar reminder rather than something to act on now.
metaDetail: The 2027 topic is announced in spring 2027.

title: editing.services Scholarship
audience: Students 18 or older attending or entering an accredited college, university or trade school
description: A $1,000 USD award on a 300 word essay answering how writing impacts today's world. The contest runs a full year, from November 30 to November 29, and past winners are published.
notes: Two things to check before you spend time on it. You must be at least 18 on entry, which rules out a good share of Grade 12 students, and the award is in US dollars. This was listed on Alberta counsellor sheets as the ServiceScape scholarship; the company has since rebranded to editing.services and the old name still points at the right page.

title: Haywood Hunt Annual Scholarship
audience: Canadian post-secondary students; the firm publishes its criteria when each cycle opens
description: An annual award from a Canadian investigations firm. The current cycle has closed and the winner was announced in early September, so the page to watch reopens ahead of the next round.
notes: Listed here because the cycle is genuinely current rather than abandoned, but be aware the provider strips the page down to a closure notice between rounds, so the amount and the entry criteria are not published year-round. Check the page before building any plan around it.
metaDetail: Criteria are only published while the cycle is open.

title: USW Post Secondary Scholarships
audience: United Steelworkers members and their children, age 25 or under
description: The United Steelworkers awards 22 scholarships of $1,500 each year to members and children of members who are heading into post-secondary education.
notes: Open to a USW member or the child of a member in good standing who is 25 or younger. The application is a form plus either a three-minute video or a 250-word written statement, in English or French, on one of four set topics. The 22 awards are split across USW Districts 3, 5 and 6 and the national locals; District 3 covers Western Canada including Alberta. You cannot win more than twice. The 2026 cycle closed June 30, 2026. Dates for the next cycle were not posted when checked on September 30, 2026.
metaDetail: 22 awards for USW members and their children.

title: USW Indigenous Post-Secondary Scholarships
audience: First Nations, Inuit or Métis members of USW families
description: Six scholarships of $1,500 from the United Steelworkers for First Nations, Inuit and Métis students in USW families who are heading to a Canadian post-secondary institution.
notes: Separate from the general USW post-secondary scholarships and judged on its own. Open to active or retired USW members and their children, grandchildren and immediate family who self-identify as First Nations, Inuit or Métis. The six awards are split two apiece across three regions, and Alberta sits in the Western and Northern Canada region. Application is a form plus a three-minute video or a 250-word statement on one of three set topics. The 2026 cycle closed June 30, 2026. Dates for the next cycle were not posted when checked on September 30, 2026.
metaDetail: Two of the six are set aside for Western Canada.

title: Unifor National and Regional Council Scholarships
audience: Unifor members and children of members entering first year
description: One application to Unifor puts you in the running for 23 named entrance scholarships, awarded to members and children of members starting their first year of full-time post-secondary study.
notes: One form, 23 named awards behind it, including the Bob White, Buzz Hargrove, Nelson Mandela, Rosemary Brown and Truth and Reconciliation scholarships. You must be a Unifor member or the child of a member in good standing, a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, and entering your FIRST year of full-time study at a public institution in Canada; these are entrance awards and are not renewable. Children of members also submit a transcript and a letter of recommendation from a teacher, principal or community activist. Quebec residents apply through a separate Quebec Council process. Unifor has not published the award value on its scholarship page, so no amount is claimed here. The 2026 cycle has closed and Unifor's own page says to check back in March 2027 for the awards covering September 2027 entry. Verified against unifor.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Unifor's page says the next details post in March 2027.

title: CNIB Post-Secondary Scholarships
audience: Students who are blind, Deafblind or have low vision
description: A single CNIB application considers you for every scholarship you qualify for, worth $1,000 to $8,000, if you are blind, Deafblind or have low vision and heading to post-secondary study anywhere in Canada.
notes: One application covers the whole slate: CNIB says submitting it automatically considers you for any scholarship you are eligible for. Graduating high school students can apply, using interim proof of secondary completion. You need best-corrected visual acuity of 20/70 or worse or a visual field of 20 degrees or narrower, and must be a Canadian citizen or have held landed immigrant status for at least a year. Eligible programs include diplomas, degrees, skilled trades certificates and apprenticeships. The 2026/27 cycle has closed; CNIB's page says applications for 2027/28 open in spring 2027. Questions go to scholarships@cnib.ca. Verified against cnib.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: One application covers every CNIB award you qualify for.

title: Air Cadet League of Canada National Educational Scholarships
audience: Air cadets across Canada heading to post-secondary study
description: A single ACC64 form puts air cadets in the running for the Air Cadet League of Canada's slate of national education scholarships, including engineering and aviation-specific awards.
notes: One online form, the ACC64, covers the national slate. The named awards include the Alex Venables Scholarship in Engineering, the Birchall Scholarship, the CAE Limited Scholarships, the Dr. William Weston Scholarship, the KC Lett Scholarships, the Legion National Foundation Scholarship, the Thomas Colfer Scholarship and up to five Royal Canadian Air Force Association Trust awards of $2,500. You must be an air cadet, and the form routes through your Commanding Officer and Squadron Sponsoring Committee Chair, so start with your squadron rather than the website. The League does not publish a per-award amount table, so no single figure is claimed here. The 2026 deadline was April 1, 2026 and April 1 has been the recurring date; confirm with awards@aircadetleague.com before counting on it. Verified against aircadetleague.com on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: One ACC64 form covers the whole national slate.

title: Horatio Alger Indigenous Achievement Scholarships
audience: First Nations, Inuit and Métis students in their final year of high school
description: Five awards of $10,000 for First Nations, Inuit and Métis students, and the one Horatio Alger stream that takes Grade 12 applicants rather than Grade 11.
notes: Worth knowing about specifically because it breaks the Grade 11 rule that governs the rest of the Horatio Alger slate: this stream takes Grade 12 students, or CEGEP students in their final year. The academic bar is a 2.0 GPA rather than the 70 percent average the other streams ask for. You must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Open across Canada. Verified against horatioalger.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: The one Horatio Alger stream open to Grade 12 students.

title: Horatio Alger Vocational and Technical Education Scholarships
audience: Students starting hands-on trades or technical training, under 35
description: Twenty-five awards of $3,000 for students across Canada starting hands-on vocational, technical or trades training, aimed at people facing real financial need.
notes: A separate application from the Horatio Alger undergraduate scholarships, on a later calendar, and it does NOT have the Grade 11 gate: you need to have finished high school or an equivalency by July 1 of the year you start. Twenty-five awards of $3,000, open in every province and territory, for hands-on vocational, technical or trades training at a public or not-for-profit institution. Household net income must be $80,000 or less and you must be under 35. Two related Horatio Alger trades awards, the Seaspan VTE and the Skills and Trades Scholarship, are British Columbia only and Alberta students cannot apply, whatever a scholarship aggregator tells you. The 2026 round closed June 15, 2026; the page says to come back for 2027 details. Verified against horatioalger.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: No Grade 11 gate here, unlike the undergraduate streams.

title: Horatio Alger Crown Lift Vocational and Technical Education Scholarships
audience: Trades and technical students in specific fields, under 35
description: Three awards of $3,000 from Crown Lift through Horatio Alger Canada, for certificate or diploma students in a defined set of trades and technical fields.
notes: Narrower than the main Horatio Alger trades stream and much smaller: only three awards. Your program has to be a certificate or diploma in business administration, construction trades, engineering, graphic design, manufacturing, production or welding, or sales and marketing. Otherwise the gates match: high school finished by July 1, household net income of $80,000 or less, under 35, Canadian citizen or permanent resident, open in every province and territory. Applied for on the same VTE application, so there is no cost to being considered for both. The 2026 round has closed. Verified against horatioalger.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Only three awards, and your field of study has to match.

title: RBC Elevate Scholarship
audience: Students aged 17 to 29 entering a degree or diploma program
description: Forty awards a year of up to $15,000 from RBC, administered by Universities Canada, for students aged 17 to 29 who are accepted into a Canadian degree, diploma or certificate program and need the money.
notes: The largest of the three RBC Next Step scholarships, and the one a graduating Grade 12 student can actually use: you qualify once you are accepted, not only once enrolled. The value tracks your program: up to $15,000 a year for a bachelor's degree, $8,000 for a diploma, $2,000 for CEGEP technical training. Ages 17 to 29, Canadian citizen or permanent resident, financial need required. Apply EARLY. Universities Canada caps the round at 500 submitted applications and closes the portal once it fills, so the posted deadline is a ceiling, not a plan. The 2026 window ran February 2 to March 26. The companion RBC Ignite Scholarship is listed separately here; the third, RBC Reimagine, is for people 25 and over who have been out of school three years or more. Verified against rbc.com on 2026-09-08.

items.text: An account on the RBC scholarship portal
A financial need self-assessment inside the form

metaDetail: The round closes at 500 applications, so apply early.

title: PSAC Scholarship Program
audience: PSAC members and their dependent children under 26
description: Twenty-four scholarships from the Public Service Alliance of Canada, fourteen of them reserved for dependent children of members, awarded on a written or creative submission rather than on grades.
notes: Twenty-four awards in four buckets: 14 for dependent children of members heading to full-time study, 3 for members in full-time study, 2 for members part-time, and 5 for members or dependents who self-identify as a woman, Indigenous, a person with a disability or racialized. You must be a member, or the dependent child under 26 of a member, in good standing as of March 31 of the application year. Judged on the merit of a 750 to 850 word essay OR a creative submission: a video, infographic or song, up to five minutes, answering that year's set question. Not limited to first-year students, and past winners cannot win twice. PSAC does not publish the award value in its guidelines, so no figure is claimed here. The 2026 round closed June 22, 2026 and PSAC says the 2027 program opens in April. Verified against psacunion.ca and the PSAC scholarship guidelines on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: A song or video counts as a submission, not just an essay.

title: Knights of Columbus Pro Deo and Pro Patria Scholarships
audience: Knights of Columbus members in Canada and their children
description: Twelve scholarships of $1,500 a year, renewable for up to four years, for Knights of Columbus members in Canada and their sons and daughters entering first year of a bachelor's degree.
notes: Funded by the Fourth Degree but open to the family of ANY Knights of Columbus member in Canada, not just Fourth Degree members, which is the detail most council notices leave out. You must be entering freshman year of a four-year bachelor's degree at a Canadian college or university, and be a member in good standing, or the son or daughter of a member, including a member who died in good standing. Awarded on academic excellence and renewable each year of undergraduate study to a maximum of four. Applications go through the ISTS portal at aim.applyISTS.net/KofC using program key KofC; use a personal email address, not a school one, because school addresses expire at graduation. The Knights do not publish a deadline on this page, so confirm the date through ISTS or your council before relying on it. Verified against kofc.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Open to any Canadian member's family, not only Fourth Degree.

title: Girl Guides of Canada National Scholarship Program
audience: Girl Guides of Canada members continuing their education
description: The national scholarship program of Girl Guides of Canada, open to members across the country and awarded on accomplishment in and beyond Guiding.
notes: National and separate from the provincial council bursaries, which are administered per province and have their own smaller awards. Named memorial scholarships within the program include the Doris Ingram Memorial Scholarship, the Norma Osler Education National Scholarship and the Miranda Friz Memorial National Scholarship. Girl Guides does not publish the award values or the application window on this page, so no figure or date is claimed here; recipients for the 2026 round were notified in June 2026. Applications were closed as of 2026-09-08. Ask scholarship@girlguides.ca for the next cycle's dates. If you are in Guiding, check your provincial council page too, because those are separate applications. Verified against girlguides.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Provincial council bursaries are separate applications.

title: Navy League of Canada Maritime Affairs Scholarship
audience: Active sea cadets entering a maritime post-secondary program
description: One $3,000 scholarship a year, formally the Honourable Rear-Admiral Fred Mifflin Memorial Scholarship, for an active sea cadet entering an accredited post-secondary program in the maritime sector.
notes: One award a year, so the field is small but so is the pool. You must be an active sea cadet and your program has to sit within the maritime sector, which is the binding constraint for a landlocked Alberta applicant: marine engineering, naval architecture, oceanography, marine biology and the like all count, a general science degree does not. Apply on form NL_LN_55, and attach every supporting document, because the Navy League discards incomplete applications rather than following up. The Navy League also points sea cadets at the Royal Canadian Sea Cadet Education Foundation, which funds separate awards of $1,000 to $5,000, and at a $5,000 Young Citizens Foundation award given to a top sea cadet entering first year. Verified against navyleague.ca and the Navy League's own application form on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Your program has to sit in the maritime sector.

title: Army Cadet League of Canada Awards and Bursaries
audience: Army cadets across Canada heading to post-secondary study
description: The Army Cadet League of Canada runs five national awards and bursaries for individual army cadets, each with its own policy document and online application form.
notes: Five separate awards for individual cadets: the Gerard Buckley Cadet Fund, the 1st Canadian Parachute Battalion Bursary, the Young Citizens Foundation Scholarship Award, the Major Terence Whitty Memorial Bursary and the Colonel Commandants and National Presidents' Scholarship. Each has its own policy document and its own form, most hosted on formsite.com and reachable from the League's awards page. The League publishes no amounts or deadlines on that page, so nothing is claimed here; ask the national office at 613-725-0220 or ed@aclc-lcac.ca, or go through your corps. Do not confuse these with the corps grants on the same page, which fund the unit rather than the cadet. Verified against armycadetleague.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Five separate awards, each with its own form.

title: Jean Lumb Awards
audience: Students of Chinese heritage in grades 9 through 12
description: Awards of $1,000 for students of Chinese heritage anywhere in Canada, given across a dozen categories from academics and athletics to innovation and overcoming adversity.
notes: Unusually open: grades 9 through 12 can apply, not just graduating students, so a Grade 10 student can win and apply again later. Categories have included academics, arts, athletics, community service, defence of the environment, dignity of life, excellence, innovation, innovation in technology, leadership, overcoming adversity, family medicine, and journalism and communication. You may apply to as many categories as you like but can win only one, and each category needs its own application and its own reference letters, written for that category rather than reused. You must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Chinese heritage attending high school in Canada; students on a study permit are not eligible. Heritage is self-certified, with no documentation required. Past winners cannot reapply, unsuccessful applicants can. Winners are notified by August 31. The 29th annual awards are the current cycle; the Foundation does not post the deadline on its home page, so check the application portal or email info@jeanlumbfoundation.ca. Verified against jeanlumbfoundation.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Grades 9 to 12, so you can win early and apply again.

title: Filipino-Canadian National Scholarship Program
audience: Filipino-Canadian students heading to post-secondary study
description: A national program of scholarships for Filipino-Canadian students, each worth at least $1,000, with categories covering academics, creative arts and volunteer work.
notes: Run with the Golden Balangay Foundation and open across Canada. Each scholarship carries a minimum award of $1,000 and typically names at least one recipient per category per year, so the categories matter more than the headline count. You may apply to up to two categories per cycle. You need Filipino heritage plus Canadian citizenship or permanent residence, at least a B average, demonstrated financial need, and you must be attending a Canadian post-secondary institution. The 2026 round closed January 15, 2026 with winners announced February 20, 2026, which puts this on a much earlier calendar than most awards here: a January deadline means starting in the fall of Grade 12. Verified against filcannationalscholarship.com on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: A January deadline, so start in the fall of Grade 12.

title: Diabetes Hope Foundation Scholarship
audience: Final-year high school students living with type 1 diabetes
description: A minimum of 35 scholarships of $3,000 across Canada for students in their final year of high school who live with type 1 diabetes and are heading to post-secondary study.
notes: One of the few national awards written specifically for graduating high school students rather than adapted to fit them. You must be in your final year at a Canadian secondary school or CEGEP, be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, hold a valid SIN, and have been under the care of a Canadian pediatric diabetes team or physician for type 1 diabetes for at least a year before applying. Judged on both merit and need, weighing how you balance diabetes management against school, community involvement and your own health. The Foundation aims for a minimum of 35 awards a year, funding permitting. The 2026 round opened January 5 and closed March 2, so this sits early in the Grade 12 calendar. Applications run only through the portal at dhfscholarship.smapply.io. Note that the Foundation's own 2026 guidelines PDF still says 'fall of 2025' in one line; that is their typo, not a different cycle. Verified against the Diabetes Hope Foundation application guidelines on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Written for graduating students, not adapted to fit them.

title: AbbVie IBD Scholarship
audience: Students diagnosed with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis
description: Fifteen one-time awards of $5,000 from Crohn's and Colitis Canada and AbbVie for Canadian students living with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis.
notes: Explicitly open to students 'enrolled in or awaiting acceptance from' a Canadian university, college or trade school, so a Grade 12 student who has applied but not yet heard back can still enter. Fifteen awards of $5,000, one-time rather than renewable. You must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident with a diagnosis of Crohn's or colitis, and there is no age limit. The package is heavier than most: an online application, a proof-of-diagnosis form signed by your healthcare provider, a consent form, TWO recommendation letters and a 500-word essay on wellness, academic goals and community involvement. Judged by a committee of gastroenterologists, community partners and patient representatives. The 2026 deadline was June 15 at 11:59 p.m. local time; a widely syndicated press release said June 1, but Crohn's and Colitis Canada's own page says June 15. Verified against crohnsandcolitis.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: You can apply while still waiting on acceptances.

title: Vertex Foundation Scholarship
audience: Students affected by cystic fibrosis, including siblings and children
description: A $5,000 award for students in Canada or the United States who have cystic fibrosis, or who are the sibling, child, spouse or caregiver of someone who does.
notes: Wider than it first looks: you do not need to have cystic fibrosis yourself. Siblings, children, spouses and caregivers of a person diagnosed with CF are all eligible, which makes this reachable for a much larger group than most disease-specific awards. Anticipating enrolment as a first-year student in the fall counts, so graduating Grade 12 students qualify. You must be a legal resident of Canada or the US and not on academic probation. Using a Vertex drug is explicitly NOT a factor. The award is paid in Canadian dollars for Canadian residents. The 2026 window ran January 13 to February 24 at 3:00 p.m. CT, with recommendations due February 27 and funds disbursed in August, so this is another early-in-Grade-12 deadline. Administered by Scholarship America. Verified against the Vertex Foundation scholarship FAQ on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Siblings and children of someone with CF qualify too.

title: CHS James Kreppner Memorial Scholarship and Bursary
audience: Canadians with inherited bleeding disorders and their families
description: A $5,000 award from the Canadian Hemophilia Society for Canadians with an inherited bleeding disorder, and for their spouses and children, heading to any post-secondary institution.
notes: Three categories under one program: a scholarship judged on academic merit, a bursary judged on financial need, and a mature student bursary for applicants 30 and over. Open to Canadians with hemophilia A or B, von Willebrand disease, a rare factor deficiency or a platelet function disorder, to carriers, and to anyone who contracted hepatitis C or HIV through a blood transfusion. SPOUSES AND CHILDREN of those people may also apply, which is the detail that widens this well beyond patients themselves. Past recipients cannot win twice. The deadline is April 30 of any given year, which the Society states as a standing annual date rather than a per-cycle one. The organization also operates as Bleeding Disorders Canada, so you will see both names. Verified against hemophilia.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Spouses and children of patients can apply too.

title: COPA Neil J. Armstrong Ab-Initio Scholarship
audience: Aspiring pilots aged 16 to 21 who cannot afford flight training
description: A $14,000 scholarship from the Canadian Owners and Pilots Association covering a Private Pilot Licence for one aspiring pilot aged 16 to 21 a year who could not otherwise afford the training.
notes: One award a year nationally, and at $14,000 it is one of the largest single awards a 16-year-old in Canada can win. The money pays for the Private Pilot Licence only: flight instruction, instructional materials and course costs. It does NOT cover college or university tuition, meals, travel to the airport, clothing, or gear like headsets, flight bags and tablets. Funds go straight to your flight school in milestones as you pass them: $2,500 at first solo, $2,500 each at cross country and solo cross country stages, and $1,500 at licence completion, so you never handle the money. Applicants normally must be COPA members and Canadian residents, though the selection committee can waive membership in special circumstances. You are expected to finish inside about a year. The 2026 round ran December 15 to March 13 at 11:59 p.m. ET, applied for at copa.awardspring.com. Past recipients have come from BC, Ontario, Saskatchewan and Manitoba, so no Alberta winner is on the public list yet. Verified against copanational.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Paid to your flight school in milestones, not to you.

title: Support Our Troops National Scholarship Program
audience: Spouses and dependants of serving Canadian Armed Forces members
description: At least 75 scholarships a year, from $500 to $5,000, for the spouses and dependants of serving Canadian Armed Forces members going to a Canadian college or university.
notes: The largest military-family award program in the country by volume: a minimum of 75 scholarships, and in 2024 it paid out $287,500 across 104 of them. The binding requirement is that the CAF member must be STILL SERVING. You have to submit a current Member's Personnel Record Resume showing that, so families of retired or former members do not qualify here, whatever a general 'military families' list suggests. Spouses and dependants both count. You also need proof of enrolment, a transcript, a reference letter, a list of volunteer work, and a three-part essay of 450 words total on military family life, career goals and the obstacles you face. Graduating Grade 12 students can apply: the 2026 window ran May 1 to July 16, well after acceptance letters land, and the proof of enrolment is allowed to show a future program start date. Recipients are notified by email at the end of September. Questions go to scholarships@cfmws.com. Verified against supportourtroops.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: The serving-member requirement rules out veterans' families.

title: Canada Company Children of the Fallen Scholarship
audience: Children of Canadian Forces members who died on duty since 2002
description: Up to $5,000 a year toward post-secondary education for children of Canadian Forces members who died while serving on an active mission since January 2002.
notes: Narrow by design and worth knowing exists. Eligibility covers children of Regular Force or Reserve Force members who died on duty in an active role on a Canadian Forces mission since January 2002. There is no annual deadline; applications are accepted on a rolling basis, and a program representative contacts every applicant to discuss next steps rather than simply screening them out. Read the Terms of Reference before applying, and expect to authorize the Canadian Armed Forces to confirm eligibility. Funding covers post-secondary and post-graduate study. The eligibility hotline is 1-800-883-6094. A separate charity, the Canadian Hero Fund, covers similar ground for children and spouses and is listed here too, so check both. Verified against canadacompany.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: No deadline; applications are rolling.

title: Canadian Hero Fund Scholarships
audience: Children and spouses of Canadian soldiers killed on active duty
description: Scholarships from the Canadian Hero Fund for the children and spouses of Canadian soldiers killed on active duty, in two streams: one for children and one for spousal retraining.
notes: Two streams: a Children's Scholarship, and a Spousal Scholarship aimed at professional retraining. The Fund does not publish award amounts, award counts or a deadline, so nothing is claimed here on any of the three. Applications for the 2026-2027 academic year were being accepted as of 2026-09-08, with forms downloadable from the site and returned by mail or to info@herofund.ca. Reach them at 1-888-602-3071. Overlaps in purpose with the Canada Company Children of the Fallen Scholarship, also listed here; they are separate charities with separate applications, so apply to both rather than picking one. Verified against herofund.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: A separate charity from Canada Company; apply to both.

title: Children's Aid Foundation of Canada Scholarships
audience: Young people who have been in government care
description: $5,000 for each academic year until your program is finished, for young people who have been in the care of a child protection authority anywhere in Canada.
notes: Eligibility covers anyone who was in temporary or permanent care of the ministry or department responsible for child protection up to their age of majority, OR in permanent care for at least 12 months. You must be under 30, or over 30 with no prior Foundation support. Two things the Foundation says plainly in its own FAQ and that are worth repeating. First, APPLY EVEN IF YOU ARE NOT SURE: you do not need to have applied to schools yet, you fill in the form as best you can and they follow up in the spring. Second, apply even if your marks are not strong, because the decision weighs financial need, persistence and your written answers alongside academic achievement. You reapply every year rather than the award renewing itself. You may need a confirmation of care letter from your child welfare office, though not if you have had Foundation support before. Note that the Foundation is a separate organization from your local Children's Aid Society. The 2026-27 round has closed; the Foundation's page says the 2027-28 application reopens in December 2026. Verified against cafdn.org and the Foundation's scholarship FAQ on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Apply before you have even picked a school.

title: CIM Taking Flight Grants
audience: First Nations, Inuit and Métis students heading into mining
description: Seven grants of $5,000 from the CIM Foundation for First Nations, Inuit and Métis students pursuing a career in mining, and one of the few national awards that takes high school applicants outright.
notes: Formally the Brian and Harold Keevil Endowment Taking Flight Grants. Seven grants of $5,000 a year, open to Indigenous students in high school as well as post-secondary, from across Canada, studying at a Canadian school toward a career in mineral extraction or processing. Recipients are judged on community involvement and demonstrated commitment to the mining industry. The CIM Foundation's wider scholarship list is otherwise almost entirely undergraduate and graduate, so this grant is the door in for a Grade 12 student. The deadline is October 30 and a 2026 submission form is posted, so this one is live and close: confirm with the CIM Foundation before counting on the date. Recipients are announced by December 31. Verified against cim.org and cimfoundation.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: One of few national awards open in Grade 12.

title: Canadian Women in STEM Award
audience: Young women in Canada who have competed in a FIRST robotics program
description: A single $10,000 award from FIRST Robotics Canada for a young woman who has shown leadership and impact through FIRST programs and STEM activities.
notes: The largest of the FIRST Canada national scholarships, and a single award, so the field is competitive. You must have taken part in a FIRST program: FIRST LEGO League, FIRST Tech Challenge or the FIRST Robotics Competition. Not renewable. The 2026 deadline was January 31, which is the earliest of the FIRST slate and lands in the middle of Grade 12, so put it in your calendar in the fall rather than the spring. FIRST Canada also runs separate scholarships for skilled trades, Indigenous students, leadership and problem-solving, all listed here, and partner universities in Ontario add their own on top. Verified against firstroboticscanada.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: A January deadline, the earliest of the FIRST slate.

title: Don Bossi Leadership and Innovation Canadian Scholarship
audience: FIRST robotics students who have led on their team and in their community
description: A single $5,000 award from FIRST Robotics Canada for a student who has shown outstanding leadership and innovation on their team, at school and in their community.
notes: One award, not renewable, and judged on leadership and innovation rather than marks alone. You must have participated in a FIRST program. The 2026 deadline was January 31, the same day as the Canadian Women in STEM Award, so a student eligible for both should prepare one push in January rather than two. Verified against firstroboticscanada.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Shares a January 31 deadline with the Women in STEM award.

title: FIRST Canada Indigenous Scholarship Award
audience: Indigenous students who have taken part in a FIRST robotics program
description: A single $5,000 award from FIRST Robotics Canada for an Indigenous student who has participated in a FIRST program and is going on to post-secondary study in any field.
notes: Unusually unrestricted on the academic side: your post-secondary program can be in ANY field, not only STEM, so participation in FIRST is the qualifying fact rather than what you intend to study. One award, not renewable. The 2026 deadline was February 15, two weeks later than the other two FIRST scholarships. Verified against firstroboticscanada.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Your program can be in any field, not only STEM.

title: FIRST Canada Skilled Trade Scholarship
audience: FIRST robotics students heading into a skilled trade or apprenticeship
description: Two awards of $2,500 from FIRST Robotics Canada for students who competed on a FIRST team and are heading into a skilled trade or apprenticeship rather than a degree.
notes: Aimed squarely at the robotics student who is going into the trades rather than engineering, which most STEM awards quietly exclude. You must have competed on a FIRST Robotics Competition or FIRST Tech Challenge team. Two awards of $2,500, not renewable. The package is a form, a recommendation letter from a high school instructor whose class you actually took, an official high school transcript, and a 500-word essay on your FIRST participation and why you want a trade. Home-schooled applicants should contact the FIRST scholarship committee for substitutes for the letter and transcript. The money is not paid to you: after winning you send FIRST Canada a letter naming the college programme, and it must arrive by the end of the second week of classes. The 2026 deadline was March 15 at 11:59 p.m. ET. Verified against firstroboticscanada.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Built for the robotics student going into a trade.

title: Roly Anderson Memorial Scholarship
audience: FIRST robotics students nominated for hands-on problem solving
description: A $1,000 award from FIRST Robotics Canada for a student who values creative problem solving, likes working with their hands, and leads within their FIRST team.
notes: You cannot apply for this one yourself. It runs on a NOMINATION form, so a mentor or team lead has to put your name forward, which means the useful action is to ask your team mentor rather than to fill in an application. One award of $1,000, not renewable. The 2026 nomination deadline was March 15. Verified against firstroboticscanada.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Nomination only; ask your team mentor to put you forward.

title: Curling Canada Youth Scholarships
audience: Canadian curling student-athletes aged 22 and under
description: One application covers both the For the Love of Curling and Fran Todd All Heart scholarships, with around twenty awards a year for Canadian curling student-athletes.
notes: Two scholarships behind a single application, so there is no reason to pick between them. For the Love of Curling rewards curling performance alongside strong academics and volunteer leadership; the Fran Todd All Heart Scholarship, added in 2025, recognizes student-athletes who give back and share the sport. Curling Canada announced twenty awards in 2026, most at $2,500, with Governor General's Curling Club scholarships at $3,500; the portal itself does not print the amounts, so treat those figures as Curling Canada's own announcement rather than the application terms. Applicants must be 22 or younger as of December 31 of the application year. The window opens May 1 and the 2026 round has closed, with successful candidates notified by August 31. Applications go through the portal at ccfscholarship.ca, which requires creating a profile. Verified against ccfscholarship.ca and Curling Canada's 2026 announcement on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: One application covers both curling scholarships.

title: Scouts Canada Scholarship Program
audience: Registered Scouts Canada members under 26
description: Scouts Canada's national scholarship program for registered members entering or continuing full-time study at a Canadian university or college.
notes: Listed with a caution: Scouts Canada says it is reviewing the program and intends to relaunch a revised version, and has not published the new amount, award count or deadline. Historic awards ran up to $6,000, one per person, not renewable, but that figure belongs to the old program and is not claimed here. Eligibility as previously published: a currently active and registered Scouts Canada member who has not turned 26 by January 1 of the application year, judged on achievement in academics, community and their Scouting group. The application asked for a 200-word statement on what Scouting has meant to you, two reference letters with only one from inside Scouting, a resume, and a current transcript. Email scholarships@scouts.ca for the relaunch date rather than waiting for the page to change. Verified against scouts.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Under review; email scholarships@scouts.ca for the relaunch.

title: Memorial Ribbon Scholarship
audience: Children of Canadian police and peace officers killed in the line of duty
description: Pays up to 80 per cent of tuition and books for up to four years, to a total of $50,000, for the children of Canadian police and peace officers slain in the line of duty.
notes: It covers up to but no more than 80 per cent of tuition and books per year, for no more than four years, capped at $50,000 overall, and it pays for tuition and textbooks only, toward an undergraduate degree or diploma at an approved Canadian post-secondary institution. Any child of a Canadian police or peace officer slain in the line of duty may apply, including a child born outside marriage and an adopted child. Applicants must be between 18 and 26 at the time of applying, though the Society will consider a first-time applicant over 27 case by case, and it also considers support for elementary, middle and high school costs on the same basis. You need evidence of the parent's line-of-duty death; the governing definition sits in the Society's by-laws. Run by the Police and Peace Officers' Memorial Ribbon Society. No deadline is published, so contact the Scholarship Advisory Council rather than waiting for a date to appear. Verified against memorialribbon.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Covers 80 per cent of tuition for four years.

title: Canadian Fallen Firefighters Foundation Education Program
audience: Children and spouses of firefighters who died in the line of duty
description: Scholarships and bursaries from the Canadian Fallen Firefighters Foundation for the children and spouses of firefighters whose line-of-duty deaths the Foundation recognizes.
notes: Two separate streams with two separate forms: the CFFF / Doug Lock Memorial Scholarship, and bursaries capped at $3,000 with a maximum of six awarded a year, including one funded by the Council of Canadian Fire Marshals and Fire Commissioners. You may apply for a scholarship OR a bursary, not both, so read the CFFFEP policy before choosing. Open to children and to the spouse or common-law partner of a firefighter whose line-of-duty death is recognized by the Foundation, which is the gate to check first. The written policy sets the window as March 1 to July 31 for the academic year starting that September, but the Foundation reserves the right to modify it, and its own page said applications were being accepted as of 2026-09-08, so go by the page rather than the policy dates. Forms download from cfff.ca. Verified against cfff.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: You may apply for a scholarship or a bursary, not both.

title: PLCAC Student Award Program
audience: Children of pipeline construction workers
description: An award from the Pipe Line Contractors Association of Canada for the sons, daughters and wards of people whose principal income comes from the pipeline construction industry.
notes: Directly relevant in Alberta, where pipeline construction employs a lot of parents, and it has helped more than 400 students since 1974. Two conditions do the work: your parent or guardian must draw their principal income from the pipeline construction industry, AND that parent must be employed by, or have a history of employment with, a company that is a member of the PLCAC, so check the association's membership directory before you spend time on the form. Your own program can lead to a diploma or degree in ANY field at a recognized Canadian college or university, and post-graduate students are considered too. The PLCAC does not publish the award value, so none is claimed here. The 2026 window runs September 17 to October 19, 2026. Contact plcac@pipeline.ca or 905-847-9383. Verified against pipeline.ca on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Check the member directory first.

title: CABEF Agricultural Scholarships
audience: Students entering first year of an agriculture or agri-food program
description: Seven scholarships of $2,500 from the Canadian Agri-Business Education Foundation for students entering or early in an agriculture or agri-food program at a Canadian college, university or trade school.
notes: Read the regional split before you judge your odds: of the seven awards, only TWO go to Western Canada, which for CABEF means BC, Alberta, the Territories and Yukon combined. Two more go to Central Canada and three to the East. You must be entering first year, or currently in second or third year; students in their FINAL year are not eligible, and neither are graduate or professional programs. You must be at least 16 at the time of applying and enrolled full-time in an agriculture or agri-food related undergraduate program, which includes trade school and apprenticeship routes rather than degrees alone. Past recipients cannot reapply. Judged on leadership plus a written or video answer to a set question about an emerging issue in Canadian agriculture, so a video is a legitimate alternative to an essay here. The 2026 round closed April 30 with winners notified by May 31; winners then send proof of enrolment by September 30 and are paid within 30 days. Verified against cabef.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Only two of the seven awards go to Western Canada.

title: Emmy Duff Scholarship
audience: Students who have been treated for cancer and volunteer in their community
description: A one-time $2,000 award for Canadian students who have been treated for cancer, or are in treatment, and who keep up an ongoing volunteer commitment.
notes: Open to students in any year of study, including first year, so a graduating Grade 12 student heading to a Canadian college or university in the fall can apply. You must live in Canada and be attending a Canadian institution. Two requirements make this different from a standard bursary. You need a letter from your oncologist or current physician confirming that you were treated, or are being treated, for a cancer diagnosis. And you need a demonstrated, ongoing volunteer commitment to causes you care about, which the Foundation weighs rather than treating as a nice-to-have. The written piece is a 300 to 500 word letter on your experience, your goals and why you are applying. A letter of acceptance is requested from finalists only, not up front. Everything goes in as a single PDF by email with the subject line the Foundation specifies. The 2026-27 round closed June 3, 2026. Verified against emmyduffscholarship.org on 2026-09-08.
metaDetail: Needs an oncologist letter and a volunteering record.

title: Future Masterfeeder Scholarship
audience: Canadian students aged 17 to 19 entering agriculture studies
notes: Verified on 2026-09-08 against the Masterfeeds application PDF (FAM_MstrFeederScholarshipApp.pdf) linked from the Future AgMaster Program page. One $1,000 award a year, and the application must be received by April 30. Reachable by a Grade 12 student despite the post-secondary wording: the form asks for the name of the post-secondary school APPLIED TO, and proof of full-time enrolment is required of the recipient rather than the applicant. The age window is the real gate at 17 to 19, and it is narrow enough to check first. Preference goes to students majoring in animal science or biology, though any agriculture program may apply. Requires a 500 to 700 word essay on what you hope to achieve for the future of food production, a current resume with references, and evidence of integrity, volunteerism and leadership. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian signature. Entries go through the online form, by mail, or to futureAg@masterfeeds.com. The winner is notified by August 1 and announced by September 1. Note that Masterfeeds runs a separate all-ages colouring contest called Masterpieces on the same page, which is not this award.
description: Masterfeeds awards one $1,000 scholarship a year to a Canadian student aged 17 to 19 heading into post-secondary agriculture studies, judged on a 500 to 700 word essay about the future of food production. Applications are read anonymously.
metaDetail: One award a year; animal science preferred.

title: Calgary Black Chambers Nutrien Community Scholarship
audience: Black Canadian Grade 12 students entering agriculture or engineering
notes: Verified against the Calgary Black Chambers scholarship page on 2026-09-08. The catchment is wider than the name suggests and is worth reading before you rule yourself out: Airdrie, Diamond Valley, Calgary, Chestermere, Cochrane, High River, Okotoks, Springbank or Strathmore. You must be entering FIRST year, which makes this one of only two Calgary Black Chambers awards a Grade 12 student can apply for; the Business, Legacy, TransAlta STEM and Cavalry FC awards all require second year or beyond. Community involvement is required, with a stated preference for environmental sustainability, and one reference letter. Applications go through the Calgary Foundation's grant interface and close at midnight. The Chambers had not posted dates for the new cycle when this was checked, so the year here is last cycle's carried forward; confirm before you plan around it.
description: One $7,000 award, paid straight to tuition, for a Black Canadian Grade 12 graduate from the Calgary region entering first year of agriculture or engineering. Community involvement counts, with a preference for environmental sustainability.
metaDetail: Nine towns, not just Calgary.

audience: Vulcan County Grade 12 students accepted into agriculture or environmental science

notes: Send acceptance proof, marks, activities and two unrelated references by 4 p.m. Award counts conflict between sources. Dates for the new cycle were not posted when checked; this is last cycle's date carried forward, confirm before planning around it.

title: CUPE Local 709 Post-Secondary Scholarship

notes: Email a typed resume and 500-word career essay. Payment waits for second-semester enrolment. Dates for the new cycle were not posted when checked; this is last cycle's date carried forward, confirm before planning around it. The main award page names a 2026 recipient.

description: Lacombe Ford and Lacombe Performing Arts Centre offer two $500 scholarships for community arts lessons. You must be under 18 during the programming season and live or study in Lacombe County. The award covers tuition paid directly to your instructor or program.
notes: Email the form and a one-minute video; visual artists also send three artwork photos. All videos are posted publicly. Dates for the new cycle were not posted when checked; this is last cycle's date carried forward, confirm before planning around it.

title: Rank-it.ca College Scholarship
