audience: Grade 12 students planning to enter a Canadian or American post-secondary institution within the following calendar year
description: Rank-it.ca offers $500 for an essay about a consumer trend you expect to last. Students planning to enter a Canadian or American post-secondary institution within the following calendar year can apply. The money can cover tuition, books or other education costs.
notes: Write up to 500 words in English or French. Upload a Word, RTF or PDF file using the online form with your contact details before 11:59 p.m. MST. The winner gives Rank-it.ca permission to publish the essay; this does not grant the site exclusive ownership.

title: David Ellis Scholarship
audience: High school students who are children or grandchildren of United Steelworkers members
description: United Steelworkers offers three $1,000 David Ellis Scholarships in each Canadian district to help high school students continue their education. Applicants must be children or grandchildren of a USW member and submit work about young workers' health and safety.
notes: Email a 750-1,000-word essay or a 3-5-minute YouTube video on one of the two posted themes. Include your contact details, school and relative's name and union local. The 2026 cycle closed June 30, 2026. Dates for the next cycle were not posted when checked on September 30, 2026.

title: Kalix Langenau Memorial Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 athletes at W.H. Croxford, George McDougall and Bert Church high schools in Airdrie
description: The Kalix Legacy Foundation gives one $500 scholarship to a Grade 12 athlete at each of Airdrie's three public high schools, in memory of Kalix Langenau. It looks for sportsmanship, teamwork and strong character.
notes: This works by nomination: a classmate, teacher, coach or staff member emails the foundation along with a reference letter from a coach or school staff member. You need an acceptance to a post-secondary program. The 2026 round closed May 16, 2026 and no 2027 date is posted yet, so ask your coach about it in the spring.

title: MD of Taber Annual Bursary
audience: Residents of the Municipal District of Taber enrolled full-time in post-secondary
description: The Municipal District of Taber gives up to four one-time $500 bursaries each year to residents studying full-time at a college, university or recognized post-secondary program. Programs that can lead to work in agriculture get preference.
notes: Applications are only accepted from August 1 to 31, through the online form on the MD page, and you must upload proof of enrolment as a PDF. That means you apply the summer after Grade 12, once you are registered for fall. You must have lived in the MD before enrolling; Taber town residents do not qualify.

title: Mountain View County Citizenship Awards
audience: Grade 12 students who live in rural Mountain View County
description: Mountain View County gives a $1,250 citizenship award to one Grade 12 student at each of the six high schools that serve the county. It recognizes students who contribute to their community.
notes: The awards run through the high schools, so ask your counsellor rather than the county. Judges look at extracurriculars, initiative, attitude toward school and community, leadership, volunteer work and good marks. You must be a rural resident of the county, not a town resident. The county contact is its Community Outreach Coordinator at 403-335-3311 ext 125.
metaDetail: Apply through your high school counsellor.

title: Clearwater County Post-Secondary Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 graduates who live in Clearwater County (outside its towns and villages)
description: Clearwater County gives a $1,000 scholarship to one graduating student at each of West Central, St. Dominic, David Thompson and Caroline high schools. Recipients must be county residents who show citizenship through school and community volunteering.
notes: Every graduating county student is told about it and applies through their high school with a written application and reference letters. Town and village residents do not qualify. The money is paid once you are attending full-time. Home-schooled graduates have a separate $1,000 award, applied for through the county's forms page by August 31.

title: Kneehill County Scholarship Program
audience: Rural Kneehill County residents starting their first year of post-secondary
description: Kneehill County Council gives two $2,000 scholarships each year to rural residents entering their first full-time year at a university, college or trade school.
notes: Councillors choose the winners: the essay counts for half the mark, reference letters for a quarter, and school or community contributions for the last quarter. The 2026 applications are closed and the county has not posted the next date. Past rounds closed around the end of August, so check the page in early summer after Grade 12.

title: Wheatland County Community Benefit Scholarship
audience: High-achieving Wheatland County students going into STEM
description: Wheatland County and the Wheatland Wind Project fund at least one scholarship of up to $2,000 a year for strong students in Wheatland County schools who plan to study science, technology, engineering or math.
notes: Email the application form to parks@wheatlandcounty.ca, mail it, or drop it off at the county office. The county lists July 31 as the deadline each year; the 2027 form has not been posted yet, so confirm the date before you rely on it.

title: Yellowhead County Agricultural Service Board Bursary
audience: Yellowhead County residents enrolled in post-secondary
description: Yellowhead County's Agricultural Service Board gives two $500 bursaries each year to county residents enrolled at a post-secondary institution.
notes: Download the guidelines and application from the county grants page and save the file before filling it in; the county warns that forms completed in the browser can lose your answers. Mail it to Agricultural Services in Edson. The deadline is August 31 every year, so you apply the summer after Grade 12 once you are enrolled.

title: Dale MacMillan Memorial Scholarship for Community Leadership
audience: Sturgeon County residents enrolled in post-secondary who lead in their community
description: Sturgeon County gives two $2,000 awards a year, in memory of community leader Dale MacMillan, to residents enrolled at a recognized post-secondary institution who have shown leadership in the county.
notes: You need a current Sturgeon County address, proof of enrolment, an essay of up to 300 words on your contributions and plans, and up to two reference letters. The Calahoo-Villeneuve Sand and Gravel Advisory Committee picks the winners and may give no award if no application fits. The 2026 round is closed and the next date isn't posted yet.

title: County of Stettler Agricultural Service Board Bursary
audience: High school graduates from the County of Stettler enrolled in post-secondary
description: The County of Stettler's Agricultural Service Board gives one $1,000 bursary a year to a county resident with a high school diploma who has contributed to their community and understands why agriculture matters to rural life.
notes: Send the county proof that you are enrolled in college or university (any year counts), proof of your diploma or eligibility for it, and two references from people who are not related to you. Applications must reach the county office by April 15, and you can only win it once. The April 15 date is from the current form; check that it has not changed before applying.

title: Wheatland County Agricultural Service Board Scholarship
audience: Wheatland County residents studying agriculture or environmental science
description: Wheatland County's Agricultural Service Board gives up to $10,000 a year in scholarships of $500 to $2,500 to county residents in agriculture or environment-related programs.
notes: Email the form to agandenv@wheatlandcounty.ca. Current students and graduates up to three years out can apply, but past winners and people in job-training grant programs cannot. The county has not posted a deadline for the new round; the last one it published was September 15, 2024, so ask the county (403-361-2000) in the summer.

title: Ponoka Ag Society Scholarship
audience: Ponoka-area students aged 17 to 21 heading into agriculture-related studies
description: The Ponoka Agricultural Society gives up to four $750 scholarships a year to young people from the Town or County of Ponoka whose trade, certificate, diploma or degree program relates to agriculture or benefits rural farming communities.
notes: You must be 17 to 21 as of December 1 and live east of the Crestomere School west boundary. Send the form with an essay on how your training will help rural Alberta, plus your current marks, by mail or email. The money is released once you show proof you have paid for your program. The society lists September 1 as its yearly deadline.

title: Parkland County Agricultural Bursary
audience: Parkland County residents enrolled in an agriculture-based post-secondary program
description: Parkland County gives five $500 bursaries a year to residents enrolled in an agriculture-based program at a university, college or other recognized post-secondary school.
notes: Send the form with an essay about your rural background, community and volunteer involvement and your goals, plus proof of enrolment, to Agricultural Services or agriculture@parklandcounty.com. The 2026 window ran July 1 to September 4 and has closed; expect a similar summer window in 2027, the summer after Grade 12.

title: Lacombe County Leadership Scholarship
audience: Lacombe County high school graduates starting full-time at Red Deer Polytechnic
description: Lacombe County funds a $1,850 scholarship at Red Deer Polytechnic for a student entering the first year of any full-time program there.
notes: You must be a current or former Lacombe County resident who finished at a Lacombe County high school within the last three years. You apply through Red Deer Polytechnic's own awards system, not the county, so watch RDP's scholarship dates once you have been admitted. A separate $1,850 version exists for first-year RDP apprentices.

title: Cornerstone Co-op Spirit of Youth Scholarships
audience: High school students living in Cornerstone Co-op's trading area around Vermilion
description: Cornerstone Co-op gives five $1,000 scholarships: two for Buffalo Trail Public Schools students, one for East Central Alberta Catholic Schools and two in memory of Liane Plante for St. Paul Education students. Home-educated students apply in the Buffalo Trail stream.
notes: Marks count for 40% and community involvement for 60%. Apply online through the form for your school division or mail a paper form to the Vermilion office, with an official transcript. Ties go to students who support the co-op or have worked there. Questions go to marketing@cornerstone.crs.

items.text: An online form for your school division, or a paper form by mail
An official transcript
An essay on your community involvement

title: Robert E. Walter Memorial Scholarship
audience: Residents of Mackenzie Municipal Services Agency member municipalities planning a local government career
description: The Mackenzie Municipal Services Agency gives one $2,000 scholarship a year to a student from its member municipalities in the Peace region who is studying toward a job in local government.
notes: Members include Berwyn, Falher, Grimshaw, High Prairie, Manning, Nampa, Rainbow Lake, the Town of Spirit River, Clear Hills County, Northern Sunrise County and the MDs of Fairview, Peace and Spirit River. You must agree to work in the North Peace or Mackenzie region for at least a year after graduating. Email the form to info@mmsa.ca by March 31.

title: Big Lakes County Return of Service Bursary
audience: Big Lakes County residents 18 or older who will work in the county or northern Alberta after graduating
description: Big Lakes County pays $3,500 a year, matched by another $3,500 from the provincial Northern Alberta Development Bursary, for up to two years to two students entering a one- or two-year program or the last two years of a degree. Larger streams exist for medicine, dentistry, nurse practitioner, pharmacy and large-animal vet students.
notes: In return you must work full-time in your field in Big Lakes County or northern Alberta for one year per year of funding. You must be 18 or older, live in the county (towns included), have lived in Alberta for 12 months and have applied to a provincially funded program. Apply January 2 to April 30 and reapply each year. A $750 trades stream has no matching money.

title: MD of Wainwright Education Bursary
audience: MD of Wainwright residents accepted to any accredited post-secondary program
description: The Municipal District of Wainwright gives $1,000 education bursaries to residents accepted to or attending any program at an accredited college, university or trade school.
notes: Residents of the MD and the villages of Irma, Edgerton and Chauvin can apply; Town of Wainwright residents cannot. Students in agriculture or environmental programs should apply for the MD's separate ASB bursary instead. The fillable form is on the MD page and no deadline is posted, so email asbprograms@mdwainwright.ca or call 780-842-4454 to confirm the date.

title: MD of Wainwright Agricultural Service Board Bursary
audience: MD of Wainwright residents going into agriculture or environmental programs
description: The Municipal District of Wainwright's Agricultural Service Board gives $1,000 bursaries to residents accepted to or attending an agricultural or environmental program at an accredited post-secondary school.
notes: The same residency rule as the education bursary applies: the MD plus Irma, Edgerton and Chauvin, but not the Town of Wainwright. The board picks winners through an anonymous review. The fillable form is on the MD page and no deadline is posted, so confirm it with asbprograms@mdwainwright.ca.

title: County of Northern Lights Student Bursary
audience: County of Northern Lights residents going into post-secondary, technical or apprenticeship training
description: The County of Northern Lights, around Manning, gives two $2,500 bursaries a year to residents of any age heading into post-secondary studies or technical or apprenticeship training. Winners are chosen on financial need and references.
notes: Recipients can get up to $2,500 more through the provincial Northern Alberta Development partnership if they sign the return-of-service agreement on page 5 of the form, which means living and working in the northern program area for at least ten months after graduating. That matching money needs you to be 18 or older and not in an apprenticeship. The form is due July 15 each year.

title: Youth Climate Action Bursary
audience: Calgary high school graduates and Calgary post-secondary students active in the youth climate movement
description: The Calgary Climate Hub gives four to eight bursaries of $500 to $1,000 a year to young people involved in climate action, such as climate strikes, school eco-clubs or community climate projects.
notes: This round is for the 2026/27 school year: you qualify if you will study at a Calgary post-secondary school, or if you graduated from a Calgary high school and are studying elsewhere. That means current Grade 12 students apply in next year's round, the September after graduating. Email a 200 to 500-word description of your climate involvement, your school and program, and links to any related projects, using the address on the Climate Hub page.

title: Brandon Langhjelm Memorial Essay Contest
audience: Canadian residents aged 15 to 25
description: The Justice Centre for Constitutional Freedoms runs a yearly essay contest in memory of lawyer Brandon Langhjelm, with prizes of $3,000, $2,000 and $1,000 for essays on Canadian freedom issues.
notes: The 2026 topics are social media restrictions for youth, or safety and privacy in AI chatbots. Essays run 1,200 to 1,500 words and are uploaded through the online form by 11:59 p.m. on September 27, 2026. Strong entries engage with thinkers and theories and end with practical policy proposals. You must be 15 to 25 on the deadline.

items.text: An entry form on the contest site
An essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words on one of two topics

metaDetail: Topics are youth social media limits or AI chatbot privacy.

title: Headway's Book Lovers Scholarship
audience: Students 16 and older in their final year of high school or in post-secondary, in Canada, the US, the UK or Australia
description: Book-summary app Headway gives one $1,500 scholarship a year for the best vision of a non-fiction book that could become a timeless handbook for humanity.
notes: Write up to 500 words or record a two-minute video, and add short paragraphs on your leadership and goals, a transcript showing at least a 3.0 GPA, and a recommendation letter from a teacher or community supervisor. It closes at 3 p.m. Central on September 15, 2026, and only one student wins worldwide, so treat it as a long shot.

items.text: A Google Form
Two short paragraphs, on your leadership and your goals
A current transcript
An essay of up to 500 words, or a video of up to 2 minutes, on a non-fiction book
One recommendation letter from a teacher or supervisor

title: Chick-fil-A Community Scholars
audience: High school seniors and college students living in Canada or the US with community service or leadership
description: Chick-fil-A gives up to 13 scholarships of up to $25,000 to students who lead in their communities, with a year-long leadership development program for the $25,000 winners. Canadian residents can apply.
notes: Apply on the Scholarship America portal by 3 p.m. Central on November 3, 2026, for study starting in 2027-28. You need at least a 3.0 GPA, community service, extracurriculars or leadership in the last 12 months, your transcript, and the first two pages of your parents’ T-1 tax return. At least one online recommendation must arrive within three business days of the deadline.

items.text: A transcript, official or unofficial
The first two pages of a parent's T1 tax return, with SIN and bank details blacked out
At least one online recommendation, up to three, due within three business days after the deadline
No essay. You must be 18 by July 15, 2027.

title: TD Scholarship for Indigenous Peoples
audience: First Nations, Métis and Inuit students applying to a full-time post-secondary program of two years or more
description: TD and AFOA Canada give 25 Indigenous students a year up to $60,000 over four years: up to $10,000 a year toward tuition plus $5,000 a year for living costs.
notes: Applications open in fall 2026 through AFOA Canada, for funding that starts in September 2027, so this round is the one for current Grade 12 students. You must be a member or citizen of a First Nation, Métis or Inuit community, a citizen or permanent resident, and have applied to a full-time program of at least two years. Winners must complete a paid four-month term at TD each year. The 2025 round ran October 1 to November 5 and no 2026 dates are posted yet; AFOA answers questions at td-scholarships@afoa.ca.

title: Jake Weitz Memorial Scholarship
audience: Canadian students starting a mechanics program at a Canadian college or university
description: A registered Canadian charity based in Didsbury, Alberta that pays $1,000 to students entering the mechanical trades. It awarded 13 scholarships in 2026 and 10 in 2025.
notes: You apply for the program you are starting, not the one you are in: the form asks for proof of acceptance or enrolment in an accredited Canadian college or university mechanics program, so a Grade 12 applies in the winter before starting. Eligible paths include automotive service, heavy duty equipment, agricultural equipment and aviation maintenance technician. You need high school English, math, physics or science plus any related CTS courses. A 30 second to one minute video explaining your interest in mechanics is strongly recommended. Applications go through a Google form or a PDF emailed to the foundation by March 1, with winners notified by April 15. You can only receive this award once in your lifetime.

title: Rick Blight Leadership in Action Scholarship for Athletes
audience: Canadian student athletes aged 16 to 21
description: Three scholarships from Men's Health Foundation in memory of Rick Blight, for Canadian student athletes who show leadership in their sport and look after their own mental wellbeing or their team's. Two awards of $2,000 and one of $1,000.
notes: Closes at 11:59 p.m. on September 15, 2026. You send in the questionnaire from the downloadable PDF, a high school or college transcript, a signed reference letter from a teacher or community leader, and a three to five minute video or audio recording about your involvement in sport and your volunteering. Everything goes to the foundation by email. The award has given out more than $55,000 since 2012, and current high school students qualify.

items.text: A questionnaire, emailed with the rest
Transcripts
A signed reference letter from a teacher or community leader
A 3 to 5 minute video or audio story about your sport, volunteering and mental wellness

metaDetail: Two awards of $2,000 and one of $1,000.

title: James Lee Foundation Scholarship
audience: Canadian residents over 16 with a creative portfolio aimed at advertising
description: The James Lee Foundation awards a minimum of $5,000 to emerging creative talent across Canada who want to work in advertising. Writers, art directors, film makers, recording artists, illustrators and digital artists all qualify.
notes: Submissions run August 1 to September 15, 2026, and judging is finished by October 15. You upload a link to a portfolio of up to 10 pieces plus a statement of at most 1,000 characters on how the money would help your creative path. You must be a Canadian resident over 16 and not already working professionally in the field, so a Grade 12 student building a portfolio is exactly who this is for.

title: Niagara Region Right to Life Scholarship
audience: Grade 11 and 12 students attending a Canadian high school
description: An essay contest run by Niagara Region Right to Life, open to grade 11 and 12 students across Canada. Three prizes are awarded each year: $2,000, $1,500 and $1,000.
notes: You submit a personal profile, a letter of recommendation and a 1,500 word essay by email, using the address printed on the official poster and brochure, by Friday October 16, 2026. Winners are announced by December 18, 2026. The 2026/2027 topic asks whether artificial intelligence is a force for good or a technology that undermines human dignity, and whether it changes how human beings are defined, reproduced and die, naming IVF, surrogacy, gene editing and embryo screening. The sponsor is an advocacy organisation and the essay is judged on how well you engage its questions, so read the brochure topic in full before you start. Students educated in Canada outside a high school may also enter.

items.text: An essay on the set topic (for 2026-27: AI and human dignity)

metaDetail: Open to Grade 11 as well as Grade 12.

title: VAPPA Student Bursary
audience: Vulcan County and Town of Vulcan graduates entering agriculture, energy, medical or emergency services
description: The Vulcan Area Petroleum and Agriculture Partnership Association, made up of landowners, government and energy companies with holdings around Vulcan, pays $1,000 bursaries to local graduates heading into agriculture, oil and gas, medical or emergency services careers.
notes: You must have earned your high school diploma while living in the Town of Vulcan or Vulcan County, and be registered at a post-secondary institution. Send the application with your final Grade 12 transcript, proof of acceptance or enrolment, and an essay of at least 1,000 words on the career you are chasing and why you deserve the award, by May 15. Missing documents can follow later, but the money is not released until after classes start and you have shown proof of enrolment. You may reapply in later years of study, though first-time applicants are considered first.

title: Brazeau County Agricultural Service Board Bursary
audience: Brazeau County residents in a post-secondary agriculture or environment program
description: Brazeau County’s Agricultural Service Board gives up to two $500 bursaries a year to county residents studying agriculture or the environment.
notes: Open to students living in Brazeau County who are enrolled in a BSc in Agriculture or Environment, a college diploma in either, or another degree or diploma directly tied to agriculture. Enrolment comes first, so a Grade 12 applies for the year they are starting. The county does not publish a closing date on its education page, so phone the county office before you plan around a date. Brazeau County also jointly funds the Tuition Assistance Bursary with the Town of Drayton Valley, which is a separate program.

title: Woodlands County Agriculture Bursary
audience: Woodlands County students in a full time Alberta agriculture or environmental science program
description: One $500 bursary a year from Woodlands County for a local student taking agriculture or environmental science at an Alberta post-secondary institution.
notes: You, or your parents, must live in Woodlands County or own property there. You need to be enrolled full time in an agriculture or environmental science program at an Alberta post-secondary institution, so a Grade 12 applies for the fall they are starting. Send the form with your high school transcript, proof of post-secondary enrolment and a cover letter making your case, to the county office in Fort Assiniboine by October 15.

title: Woodlands County Post-Secondary Bursary
audience: Woodlands County students entering full time post-secondary study
description: Woodlands County pays $2,000 for a first year of post-secondary study and $1,000 for a second, $3,000 in total, to students from the county.
notes: You qualify as a resident, or if your parents own property in the county and you lived there within the past five years. You must be full time at a recognised accredited institution and pass at least three courses a semester to collect that portion. The useful part for a graduating student: the county policy says that taking up to three school years off before starting post-secondary does not cost you the bursary. Applications close October 15.

title: Woodlands County Apprenticeship Bursary
audience: Woodlands County apprentices in a provincially recognised trade program
description: Up to $1,500 for a first year of apprenticeship training and $1,500 for a second, $3,000 in total, for apprentices from Woodlands County.
notes: Applications are taken all year rather than on one closing date. You need proof of enrolment in a provincially recognised apprenticeship program and two reference letters, and you must pass the classroom portion before the money is released against an official transcript. There is no age limit, you can only receive it once, and you have to declare that you are not drawing wages or a subsidy from an employer while you are at school. Residency works the same as the county post-secondary bursary.

title: Saddle Hills County Student Bursary
audience: Saddle Hills County residents entering post-secondary, trades or Class 1 driver training
description: Saddle Hills County helps local students moving into post-secondary study, the trades, or commercial Class 1 driver training.
notes: You must have lived in Saddle Hills County for at least a year, with a year in Alberta immediately before that, and be enrolled in a recognised program. The county also asks that you intend to live and work in northern Alberta after you finish and have reasonable job prospects there, so say so plainly in your essay. Send an essay of at least 200 words on your field of study and two reference letters with the online form by June 1. The county does not publish the award value, so ask before you count on a figure.

title: Saddle Hills County Veterinary Education Bursary
audience: Students in a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine or veterinary technologist program
description: The Saddle Hills County Agricultural Service Board supports students training as veterinarians or veterinary technologists, with priority to the Central Peace region.
notes: Of the two routes this covers, the veterinary technologist diploma is the one you can enter straight from Grade 12; the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine needs university first, so it is a later step rather than a first-year option. Applications go in through the county website by July 15, and the county does not publish the value.

title: Lamont County Centennial Scholarship
audience: Lamont County rural residents graduating this year or within the last two years
description: Lamont County awards two $1,000 scholarships a year to students from the rural county who are heading to post-secondary study.
notes: You must live in the county itself rather than in one of its towns or villages, and either be on track to graduate or have graduated within the last two years, with an application already in to a post-secondary institution. The county says marks are not the main test: it is looking for a demonstrated commitment to the community. Applications close June 30. Lamont County also keeps a useful page of outside awards open to its students.

title: Peace River Agricultural Society Bursary
audience: Peace Country residents aged 25 and under, with agriculture courses preferred
description: Three $500 bursaries a year from the Peace River Agricultural Society for young people in the Peace Country taking an educational course or pursuing sport, with agriculture given priority.
notes: Three intake dates each year: March 30, July 31 and November 30. You must be 25 or younger on the date you apply and live in the Peace Country, which the society defines as Grande Prairie, the County of Grande Prairie No. 1, Peace River, the MD of Peace, the MD of Greenview, the MD of Northern Lights, Clear Hills County, Saddle Hills County, Grimshaw or the MD of Smoky River. Agriculture-focused courses get priority. Winners complete at least 50 volunteer hours with an approved agricultural non-profit before the money is paid out. Send a one page letter with proof of registration and your costs.

title: Beaver County Agricultural Service Board Scholarship
audience: Beaver County residents in a post-secondary agriculture program of two years or more
description: Beaver County’s Agricultural Service Board sponsors a yearly scholarship for county students studying something tied to the agriculture industry.
notes: You must be a current resident of Beaver County and enrolled in a post-secondary agriculture-related program that runs two years or longer, so a Grade 12 applies for the program they are starting. The value moves: council sets a pot each year and splits it equally between eligible applicants, which means a single eligible applicant can receive the whole budget. You can only win it once for the same program. Applications go to the county’s agricultural fieldman by September 1.

title: Ed Stelmach Community Foundation Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in Lamont, Two Hills, Fort Saskatchewan, Tofield, Viking, Vegreville and New Myrnam
description: The foundation started by former premier Ed Stelmach awards three $2,750 scholarships a year to Grade 12 students from a set list of communities northeast of Edmonton.
notes: Open to students finishing Grade 12 at a public or Catholic high school in Lamont, Two Hills, Fort Saskatchewan, New Myrnam, Tofield, Viking or Vegreville. You need at least 80 percent in Social Studies, acceptance at a post-secondary institution, a 500 word essay covering your goals, your community involvement, hardship you have come through and your financial need, and a reference letter from someone in your community. Applications are mailed and have to arrive by May 1.

title: Greenview Post-Secondary Scholarship
audience: MD of Greenview residents, or students whose parents live there, entering post-secondary study
description: The Municipal District of Greenview budgets money every year to help local students with post-secondary costs, including a $2,500 scholarship for students in a degree program.
notes: Policy 8008 counts you as a resident if you live in Greenview, normally live there, or your parents live there, so a student who moves away to study still qualifies. Applications close June 30 each year, and you can apply again every year you stay enrolled. Council sets aside $25,000 a year for the degree stream. The policy runs a second stream for trade, diploma, certificate and apprenticeship programs, but the value of that one is not stated in the policy document, so confirm the figure with Greenview rather than planning around a number. If you accept the scholarship and then do not attend, the money goes back to the municipality.

title: Emma Armstrong Memorial Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in Strathmore, Drumheller or Bassano
notes: Community participation, leadership, character, teamwork and athletics all count. You need a letter and two references. The handbook warns the amount may change in later years.
description: Two $1,000 awards remember Emma Armstrong of Hussar, who played everything from curling to water skiing and usually ended up leading. They go to Grade 12 students at Strathmore, Drumheller, Bassano or Wheatland Crossing who start post-secondary within three years.
metaDetail: Two awards, and you have three years to start.

title: Pioneer Gas Co-op Achievement Award
audience: Children of Pioneer Gas Co-op members starting post-secondary
notes: The membership has to be a year old, so check with whoever holds it before you count on this one. The deadline falls the October after you graduate, not in the spring.
description: Pioneer Gas Co-op gives $500 to the child of a member in good standing who is starting a degree, diploma or apprenticeship. You need at least 75 percent in your core subjects.
metaDetail: Needs a parent's Co-op membership.

title: Dr. Walter Shydlowski Health Care Scholarship
audience: Bassano hospital district residents entering health care
notes: Eligibility runs on the old hospital district boundary rather than the town limits, so ask the school office whether your address counts.
description: A $300 award for a student who lives in the Bassano General and Auxiliary Hospital and Nursing Home district and is continuing into any health care field. Marks, community service and financial need are all weighed.
metaDetail: Runs on the hospital district boundary.

title: Brooks and District Chamber of Commerce Business Scholarship
audience: County of Newell graduates entering business
notes: Open to grads of Bassano, Brooks Composite, Duchess, Ecole Rousseau, Rosemary and St. Joseph's Collegiate. The July deadline is later than most, so it is worth a second pass after graduation.
description: The Brooks and District Chamber of Commerce gives three $500 awards to County of Newell graduates registered in a business diploma, applied degree or bachelor's degree. You need a 75 percent average.
metaDetail: Three awards, and the deadline is in July.

title: Brooks Kiwanis Club Armstrong Trust Scholarship
audience: County of Newell grads with financial need
notes: You have to apply for a student loan as part of it, and finalists may be interviewed.
description: The Brooks and District Kiwanis Club awards this one mainly on financial need, with academics and school and community contributions also weighed. The amount varies with what the trust can pay and what you need.
metaDetail: A student loan application is part of it.

title: Brooks and District Kiwanis Club Vocational Scholarship
audience: County of Newell grads entering technical training
notes: The application asks for Grade 12 math and English plus whatever else your program needs for entry, and a description of your school and community activities.
description: One $500 award a year for a public high school graduate in the County of Newell heading to technical training at NAIT, SAIT, a vocational training centre or the equivalent.
metaDetail: Grade 12 math and English are required.

title: Greater Athabasca Community Foundation Scholarship
audience: Athabasca area graduates, including homeschool grads
notes: You need an essay, two references and Canadian citizenship or permanent residency. The money comes after you send your first semester transcript.
description: The Greater Athabasca Community Foundation gives $250 to a graduate of Edwin Parr Composite or Boyle School, or a homeschooled graduate living in the area, who has led something in the community.
metaDetail: Homeschool graduates qualify too.

title: Green Leaf Fuel Excellence in Community Service Scholarship
audience: Boyle and Edwin Parr grads with a service record
notes: A teacher or principal has to endorse the application, and April 1 makes it one of the earliest local deadlines.
description: Green Leaf Fuel gives $500 to an Edwin Parr Composite or Boyle School graduate who documents what they have contributed to the community and what they plan to study next.
metaDetail: Needs a teacher or principal endorsement.

title: North Corridor Co-operative Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students whose family holds a Co-op membership
notes: The application asks for an essay and your marks, and payment follows the end of your first year.
description: North Corridor Co-operative funds four $500 scholarships for Grade 12 students whose parent or guardian is a member. You have a year after graduating to begin further study in Canada.
metaDetail: Four awards, one family membership needed.

title: Century 21 Mary Poirier Scholarship
audience: Bonnyville area grads who led something in the community
notes: You submit a one minute video about your goals plus a reference from outside your family. The page heading says May 28 while the deadline line says June 1, so treat May 28 as the safe date.
description: A $500 award for a student from Bonnyville Centralized High School, Ecole Notre Dame High School or Ecole des Beaux Lacs who has shown community leadership.
metaDetail: Needs a one minute video.

title: Lookmanjee Sportsman Mobile Park Scholarship
audience: Graduates living at Sportsman Mobile Home Park
notes: The eligible group is tiny, which makes the odds better than the amount suggests. You need a reference letter, a letter from your principal and a transcript.
description: A $2,000 award for a student who is a tenant at Sportsman Mobile Home Park in their graduating year. The essay covers your goals and your financial situation.
metaDetail: Only park tenants can apply.

title: Bonnyville Agriculture Society Scholarship
audience: Students registered in an agriculture business program
notes: Two reference letters and the full application form are required. The June 30 date lands well after graduation, so it is easy to forget.
description: The Bonnyville Agriculture Society gives $1,000 to a student registered in an agriculture business program, weighing marks, 4-H or Society involvement and community work.
metaDetail: 4-H involvement helps here.

title: Ramzi Halabi Memorial Scholarship
audience: Graduating students heading into business or planning one
notes: The whole application is a 500 word essay about yourself, your career goals and why business interests you.
description: Nick's Lounge funds this $500 award for a graduating student going into business or entrepreneurship. Students taking something else who hope to start their own business are told to apply anyway.
metaDetail: A 500 word essay is the application.

title: Royal Canadian Legion Mirror Poppy Sales Bursary
audience: Children of Armed Forces members and grandchildren of veterans
notes: A letter is required and the form comes from the school career centre.
description: Poppy sales in Mirror pay for a $500 bursary for a graduating Grade 12 student who is the child of a Canadian Armed Forces member or the grandchild of a veteran, and who is going on to post-secondary.
metaDetail: Open to grandchildren of veterans.

title: Lucy Clifton Bedinfield-Wehrfritz Scholarship
audience: Claresholm and Fort Macleod students in arts or trades
notes: You need at least 90 percent attendance in your final year, and a willingness to work to the best of your ability counts more than a top average. The family has committed to ten years of funding.
description: Lucy Bedinfield-Wehrfritz supported her local schools for decades and died in 2022 at 94. Her family funds up to six $2,000 awards a year, three at Willow Creek Composite and three at F.P. Walshe, for students entering artistic or trades careers.
metaDetail: Needs 90 percent attendance in Grade 12.

title: Neal Knoot Memorial Scholarship
audience: Students entering forestry or natural resources
notes: You can apply to have it matched by the Northern Alberta Development Council, but that money comes with a return-service obligation of one month working in the north per $500, or you pay it back.
description: The Lesser Slave Forest Education Society funds two $500 scholarships for students heading into forestry, forest products manufacturing, natural resources or environmental science, or any health and safety program.
metaDetail: Matching funds carry a northern work obligation.

title: MJ Munn-Kristoff Forest Resources Scholarship
audience: Students entering forestry or environmental science
notes: It shares an application and a deadline with the Society's Neal Knoot award, so one form puts you in for both.
description: A $500 award from the Lesser Slave Forest Education Society for a high school graduate studying forestry, forest products manufacturing, natural resources or environmental science.
metaDetail: One form covers both Society awards.

title: BPO Elks Memorial Scholarship
audience: High Prairie area students entering post-secondary
notes: You send a transcript and an essay, and there is an interview. The Elks page the school links to returns a 404, so ask the school or the lodge for the current form.
description: The High Prairie Elks give $1,000 to a local student entering post-secondary who combines academic results with volunteering and citizenship.
metaDetail: There is an interview stage.

title: Elliott and Rosche Memorial Bursary
audience: Big Lakes County students in biology, earth or water sciences
notes: The county boundary is the only geographic test, so students from Kinuso, Faust, Joussard and High Prairie all qualify.
description: The Lesser Slave Watershed Council gives $1,000 to a Big Lakes County student studying biology, earth sciences or anything water focused.
metaDetail: Open across Big Lakes County.

title: Ruth Pratt Memorial Bursary
audience: Students entering agriculture programs
notes: The Society's own bursary page returns a 404, so ask the Society or your school office for the form rather than relying on the link.
description: The High Prairie Agricultural Society gives $1,000 to a student pursuing post-secondary studies in agriculture. The application is a single form.
metaDetail: The Society's own link is dead.

title: Tolko High Prairie Scholarship
audience: High Prairie area graduates entering post-secondary
notes: Children of Tolko employees and students entering forestry or related studies get preference. The application is posted in Google Classroom rather than on a public page.
description: Tolko funds two $1,000 scholarships for High Prairie area graduates going on to post-secondary. Any program qualifies, and you send proof of enrolment with the form.
metaDetail: The form lives in Google Classroom.

title: Lacombe Legion Scholarship
audience: Descendants of long-serving Lacombe Legion members
notes: The service requirement is the whole test, so check the family record before writing this off. The application comes from the Legion office rather than the school.
description: The Lacombe Legion gives $2,000 to a child, grandchild or great-grandchild of a past or current branch member who has at least ten years of continuous service with the Royal Canadian Legion.
metaDetail: Ten years of Legion service in the family.

title: M.D. of Bonnyville Municipal Scholarship for Nursing
audience: M.D. of Bonnyville residents in nursing programs
notes: Every funded year costs you a year of full-time work afterwards in the M.D., Cold Lake, Bonnyville or Glendon. You write a 300 to 500 word essay on practising in rural Alberta and send a reference and proof of enrolment. Late applications are not accepted.
description: The Municipal District of Bonnyville pays $7,000 a year to one resident enrolled full time as a registered nurse or nurse practitioner student. It is a return-of-service award aimed at keeping health workers in the area.
metaDetail: One year of local work per funded year.

title: M.D. of Bonnyville Municipal Scholarship for Veterinary Medicine
audience: M.D. of Bonnyville residents in veterinary medicine
notes: Each funded year commits you to a year working in the M.D., Cold Lake, Bonnyville or Glendon. First-time recipients are preferred over repeat applicants.
description: One resident enrolled full time in a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine program gets $10,500 a year from the M.D. of Bonnyville, on the same return-of-service terms as its nursing and medical awards.
metaDetail: Return of service is required.

title: M.D. of Bonnyville Municipal Scholarship for Medicine
audience: M.D. of Bonnyville residents in medical school
notes: The essay asks about your interest in rural medicine and what you have contributed to the community, from volunteering to farming. Each funded year is repaid with a year of local practice.
description: The largest of the M.D. of Bonnyville's three municipal scholarships, $14,000 a year for one resident enrolled full time in a Medical Doctor program.
metaDetail: The essay asks about rural practice.

title: Bow Island and District Health Foundation Scholarship
audience: Bow Island area students entering health care
notes: Nursing, pharmacy, pre-med and kinesiology are all named as examples. You are notified at the start of your program but paid after you show evidence that you finished the course or year.
description: The Bow Island and District Health Foundation funds $500 scholarships in three categories: a high school student entering health care, a student from the service area in second year or later of a health program, and an Alberta Health Services employee upgrading.
metaDetail: Paid after you finish the year.

title: Friends of Canadian Simmental Foundation Scholarships
audience: Students involved in beef cattle, in any program
notes: The set is four general $3,000 scholarships plus the $3,000 First Year Scholarship and the $3,000 Trevor Vance Memorial, both for first-year students only. You can win each named award once, and no more than two Foundation awards in your life.
description: The Foundation hands out $18,000 a year to students involved in beef cattle who are working toward any degree, diploma or certificate. One application form covers all six awards, including two reserved for first-year students.
metaDetail: One form enters you for six awards.

title: G.L.D.C. Gas Co-op Post-Secondary Scholarship
audience: G.L.D.C. Gas Co-op members and their children
notes: Community involvement and fit with co-op values carry the decision. You can only receive it once, and winners are asked to allow their name and photo on the co-op's website and Facebook page.
description: The co-op awards two $1,000 scholarships a year to members in good standing, or their children, who are entering first year at a recognized university, college or trade school. One of the two is named the Jack Siebenga Memorial Scholarship.
metaDetail: Winners are asked to be named publicly.

title: CCWA Helen Dueck Memorial Nursing Scholarship
audience: Coaldale area graduates entering nursing or health care
notes: You need English 30-1, Biology 30, Chemistry 30 or Science 30, and Math 30-1 or Math 31. Send a cover letter, a resume and either proof of acceptance or the date you expect to hear.
description: Helen Dueck nursed in Coaldale and volunteered as a health care practitioner in several countries after she retired. The Coaldale Community Wellness Association gives $1,000 in her name to a graduate entering health care, with nursing preferred.
metaDetail: Specific Grade 12 courses are required.

title: CCWA Jake Janzen Memorial Community Service Scholarship
audience: Coaldale area graduates with a volunteer record
notes: How the application is put together is part of the judging, so the cover letter and resume are worth the time.
description: The Coaldale Community Wellness Association gives $1,000 to a graduate with substantial volunteering behind them who plans to keep serving the community. Any post-secondary program qualifies.
metaDetail: Any program qualifies.

title: CCWA George Wall Memorial Agricultural Scholarship
audience: Coaldale area graduates entering agriculture
notes: Your cover letter has to set out your extracurricular experience in agriculture, so 4-H, rodeo or farm work all belong in it.
description: George Wall farmed irrigated and dry land near Coaldale and Readymade and sat on the Coaldale Hospital Association board. This $1,000 award goes to a graduate entering agricultural studies.
metaDetail: Farm and 4-H experience belongs in the letter.

title: St. Paul Legion Scholarship
audience: Children of active Legion members in the St. Paul area
notes: You confirm the family connection and send proof of enrolment. The October deadline means you apply after you have started, not before.
description: The St. Paul Legion gives $500 to a graduating child of an active member from the St. Paul, Myrnam, Elk Point or Heinsburg area who is entering post-secondary.
metaDetail: The deadline falls after you start.

title: St. Paul Poppy Area Scholarship
audience: Grandchildren of veterans in the St. Paul poppy area
notes: The winner is drawn from the eligible submissions rather than judged, so a complete application is the whole job.
description: Funded by poppy campaign money, this $500 award goes to a graduating grandchild of a veteran from the St. Paul, Myrnam, Elk Point or Heinsburg poppy area who is entering post-secondary.
metaDetail: The winner is drawn, not judged.

title: Coronation and Consort Victim Services Scholarship
audience: Consort area students continuing to post-secondary
notes: The school's list gives the April 30 date but no amount. The older application form asked for an essay or video about your volunteer service plus two references, so expect something similar.
description: Victim Services in Coronation and Consort offers a scholarship to a local student going on to post-secondary, listed among the awards Consort School students can apply for.
metaDetail: The amount is not published.

title: Veteran and District Lions Club Scholarship
audience: Consort School grads who finished Grade 9 in Veteran
notes: Marks, community involvement and financial need are all weighed, and the school provides a reference. You have to be registered for post-secondary in the year you apply.
description: Two $500 scholarships a year for Consort School graduates who completed Grade 9 at Veteran School and still live in the Veteran area, bounded by the County of Paintearth, Special Area 2 and the Loyalist road.
metaDetail: Two awards, tied to Veteran School.

title: Gaye Ross Memorial Nursing Scholarship
audience: Drumheller area students in RN or RPN programs
notes: Students already in an RN or RPN program can apply, not just those entering, and the September deadline suits both.
description: A $1,500 scholarship for someone living in Drumheller or the surrounding area who has been accepted into a registered nursing or registered psychiatric nursing program.
metaDetail: Open to students already in the program.

title: Hanna Masonic Lodge Student Bursary
audience: Grade 12 students in Hanna, Youngstown, Cessford or Delia
localArea: Hanna, Youngstown, Cessford or Delia students
notes: You do not need any Masonic connection. Extracurriculars, character and financial need are what the Lodge weighs.
description: The Hanna Masonic Lodge gives $500 to a Grade 12 student from J.C. Charyk Hanna, Youngstown, Cessford or Delia who has been accepted into post-secondary.
metaDetail: No Masonic connection needed.

title: Garry Hannigan Memorial Scholarship Fund
audience: Albertans up to age 18 living with epilepsy
notes: This one pays for activities rather than tuition, so a season of hockey, a music program or a camp fee all fit. Applications are accepted from January 1 to March 31 each year.
description: The Edmonton Epilepsy Association gives up to $500 to help youth up to age 18 take part in sports or recreation that will help them develop as individuals.
metaDetail: It pays for activities, not tuition.

title: Edmonton Epilepsy Continuing Education Scholarship
audience: Alberta post-secondary students living with epilepsy
notes: The 2026 round is closed. The next one opens January 5, 2027 and closes March 31. The Association does not publish the amount or the detailed criteria, so ask before the window opens.
description: The Edmonton Epilepsy Association manages this scholarship for students with epilepsy who are continuing their education.
metaDetail: The next window opens January 5, 2027.

title: Sam Bull Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta First Nation students in law or politics
notes: You send a copy of your status card, a certified transcript and a statement of 100 to 200 words on your objectives. Proof of acceptance is needed before the money is released.
description: The Alberta Indian Investment Corporation gives $1,000 to a status First Nation student from Alberta studying law or political science, weighing marks, career plans and what the studies will bring back to First Nation community development.
metaDetail: Needs a status card and a certified transcript.

title: Senator James Gladstone Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta status First Nation students in business or economics
notes: Selection weighs your marks, your career plans and what your studies will contribute to First Nation business and economic development. Same paperwork and date as the Corporation's law award.
description: Named for Canada's first Indigenous senator, this award goes to a status First Nation student from Alberta in business, finance or economics. University students receive $1,000 and college or technical students $750.
metaDetail: College students receive $750.

title: David M. Bayne Legacy Bursary
audience: Hospitality students tied to Banff or Lake Louise
notes: New Canadians, Albertans and local youth get special consideration. You need a budget, references, a transcript and evidence of acceptance, plus banking details and a photo if you win.
description: Four $5,000 bursaries for post-secondary students in tourism, hospitality or culinary programs who face barriers to advancing their careers and have a personal or professional tie to Banff or Lake Louise.
metaDetail: Four bursaries, and new Canadians are prioritized.

title: SPECEF General Scholarship
audience: Canadian students heading into the energy industry
notes: You need an SPE student membership, satisfactory grades and volunteer involvement. Diploma, degree, graduate and non-engineering students all qualify, but students in their final undergraduate year do not.
description: The Society of Petroleum Engineers Canadian Educational Foundation funds multiple scholarships for full-time students at any Canadian institution who intend to enter the energy industry after graduating.
metaDetail: Final-year undergraduates are excluded.

title: Ben Sandison Writer's Craft and English Scholarship
audience: Students accepted into writing or English programs
notes: You submit a 500 word essay and a recommendation from a writing or English teacher. The fund states no geographic restriction, and Alberta schools link to it.
description: One of three memorial scholarships in Ben Sandison's name, $1,000 for a student accepted into a Writer's Craft, English or related post-secondary program.
metaDetail: A 500 word essay and a teacher reference.

title: Ben Sandison Hockey and Fitness Scholarship
audience: Students accepted into hockey or fitness programs
notes: You list your athletic accomplishments and include a recommendation from a coach or gym teacher.
description: A $1,000 scholarship for a student accepted into a hockey, fitness or related program at a post-secondary institution.
metaDetail: Needs a coach's recommendation.

title: Ben Sandison Drumming and Music Scholarship
audience: Students accepted into drumming or music programs
notes: Along with your music experience you send an audition video of up to three minutes and a recommendation from a music instructor.
description: A $1,000 scholarship for a student accepted into a drum, music or related post-secondary program.
metaDetail: Needs a three minute audition video.

title: Michael R. Allers Memorial Scholarship
audience: Drayton Valley area students entering education studies
notes: It sits in the Foundation's youth group of scholarships, all of which close June 1 and apply through the same site.
description: The Drayton Valley Community Foundation gives $1,000 to a student from its area who is studying to become a teacher.
metaDetail: One of the Foundation's June 1 awards.

title: Bredal Energy Fund Scholarship
audience: Drayton Valley area students entering oil and gas careers
notes: Priority goes to students and families living in Drayton Valley and Brazeau County. You can apply in your graduating year or one year after it.
description: Two $1,500 scholarships a year for students from the Drayton Valley Community Foundation area who want a career supporting the oil and gas industry, at a university, college or trade school.
metaDetail: You can apply a year after graduating.

title: Community Foundation Emergency Services Scholarship
audience: Drayton Valley and Brazeau County emergency services students
localArea: Drayton Valley and Brazeau County students
notes: There is no age restriction, so this is open to people coming back to school later. You need to be in good standing with your school and community and include a letter of support.
description: A $500 scholarship for a Drayton Valley or Brazeau County resident enrolled in an accredited emergency services program, covering firefighting and fire sciences, emergency medical services, emergency management and law enforcement.
metaDetail: No age limit on this one.

title: Alberta Beach and District Agricultural Society Scholarship Fund
audience: Alberta Beach area students in two-year programs or longer
notes: It is paid in two pieces, $1,250 in first year and $750 in second, each released after your enrolment is verified.
description: One $2,000 scholarship a year for a student enrolled in a program of at least two years at a recognized institution. Marks, citizenship, volunteering and leadership are all weighed, and you write an essay.
metaDetail: Paid across two years of study.

title: Crown Mentorship Foundation Alliance Program Bursary
audience: Black post-secondary students in Calgary and Edmonton
notes: The money follows the Deloitte Mentorship Shadow Day, so the bursary comes with the program rather than instead of it. International students can apply.
description: The Crown Mentorship Foundation gives a $2,000 bursary to Black students living and studying in Calgary, Edmonton or the surrounding areas, alongside mentorship and professional development.
metaDetail: Comes with a mentorship day.

title: Future in Agriculture Bursary
audience: Athabasca County students in agriculture programs
notes: You, a parent or a guardian has to live in or own property in the county. First-year students get priority, and mature students are welcome. The county hopes you bring the knowledge back.
description: Athabasca County's Agricultural Service Board funds one $1,500 bursary a year for a student in full-time agriculture or related studies at an Alberta university, college or trade school.
metaDetail: Mature students qualify too.

title: Kinette Club of Vulcan Bursary
audience: Vulcan area students starting full-time post-secondary
notes: You must be a Canadian citizen or landed immigrant, registered full time for September, and a first-time recipient. The form the school hosts does not state the amount or the year of the April 15 date.
description: The Kinette Club of Vulcan helps local students heading to a recognized university, college or technical institution, judging applicants on the qualities of good citizenship.
metaDetail: The amount is not published.

title: Grimshaw Regional Healthcare Attraction and Retention Scholarship
audience: Grimshaw area students in health care programs
notes: You show proof of residency, send a professional reference and write an essay about your commitment to rural northern health care. Your family living there counts if you have moved away to study.
description: Four $3,000 scholarships a year for students from Grimshaw, Berwyn, the M.D. of Peace No. 135 or the County of Northern Lights who are accepted into a health care or medical program, at any level including prerequisite courses.
metaDetail: Prerequisite courses count as eligible study.

title: Bonnyville Oilmen's Registered Apprenticeship Program Scholarship
audience: Bonnyville area grads in a Red Seal apprenticeship
notes: You have to be graduating from Off Campus, Notre Dame High, Bonnyville Centralized or Ecole des Beaux-Lacs inside the society's boundaries. The application needs an employer evaluation, references and an essay.
description: The Bonnyville Oilmen's Society gives one $1,000 scholarship a year to a graduating student enrolled in one of Alberta's Red Seal interprovincial apprenticeship programs.
metaDetail: Needs an employer evaluation.

title: Bonnyville Oilmen's Post-secondary Scholarship
amount: $1,000 a year for up to two years
audience: Bonnyville area graduates
notes: The essay covers your career plans, your activities and your volunteering, and the instructions tell you to leave academic achievements out of it. You need to be graduating from one of the four local schools.
description: The Society picks two students a year for $1,000, and pays a second $1,000 the following year if they send proof that they are continuing.
metaDetail: The essay must leave out your marks.

title: Clayton Bellamy Scholarship Fund for Music and the Arts
audience: Graduating students entering fine arts programs
notes: You need at least 65 percent, admission and registration in fine arts, performance experience and references from your principal and a teacher. Students who plan to teach get preference, and financial need breaks any remaining tie.
description: The Clayton Bellamy Foundation for the Arts gives $2,500 and a certificate to a graduating student with academic results, artistic talent and a habit of sharing that talent with the community.
metaDetail: Performance experience is required.

title: Friends of Canadian Simmental Foundation Advancing Education Bursary
audience: Simmental association members 25 and under
notes: It funds learning that is not a degree, which makes it unusual. The board reviews applications twice a year, in spring and fall, and caps the total at $5,000 a year. You have a year to spend it and must send receipts and a report.
description: This bursary pays up to $1,000 toward agricultural training, conferences and educational events for Canadian Simmental Association or Young Canadian Simmental Association members aged 25 or younger.
metaDetail: It funds courses and conferences, not tuition.

title: Dr. R.B. Demerchant Animal Health Bursary
audience: Caroline and West Central High School grads in animal health
notes: Two-year programs receive $1,000 paid as $500 a year, while the shorter Olds program receives $500. 4-H or school activities and financial need are weighed. The school announces it at the awards ceremony whether or not anyone wins it.
description: One student a year from Caroline School or West Central High School gets this bursary for animal health studies, whether an animal health technology diploma, the University of Alberta companion and performance animal health degree, or the Olds veterinary technical assistant program.
metaDetail: The amount depends on program length.

title: Seed Smart Scholarship
audience: Students in agriculture-related programs
notes: You send transcripts, an essay of 300 to 500 words and two references.
description: Alberta Seed Processors funds two $1,000 scholarships a year for students in agriculture-related studies, weighing academic and non-academic accomplishments, volunteering and rural leadership.
metaDetail: Two awards each year.

title: Cochrane Immigrant Services Scholarship
audience: Newcomer Grade 12 students in Cochrane
notes: You have to be 21 or under as of August 31. The school's directory lists August 31 or November 30 as the dates and warns that details can change, so confirm with the committee.
description: Two $250 scholarships for Grade 12 students who are newcomers to Canada with permanent resident status and are willing to volunteer with the Cochrane Immigrant Service Committee.
metaDetail: Comes with volunteering at the committee.

title: Freehorse Family Wellness Society Post-Secondary Funding Program
audience: First Nations students without band funding
notes: There are three intakes: June 15 for fall and winter, October 15 for the winter term and March 15 for spring and summer. You need 12 months of Canadian residency, and NWT registrants must be ineligible for territorial funding.
description: The Freehorse Family Wellness Society funds tuition, books, supplies and living support for First Nations students, including members of Alberta First Nations that have no funding available, the Alberta General List of the Michel Band, and Northwest Territories registrants living in Alberta.
metaDetail: Three intakes across the year.

title: Momentum Indigenous Scholarship
audience: Indigenous students near Strathcona's Alberta and Saskatchewan operations
notes: There is no age limit and past recipients can apply again. Selection weighs your commitment to learning and what you give back to your community. The 2026 round ran April 1 to June 16 and has closed. Strathcona had not posted 2027 dates when this was checked in September 2026, so the date shown is last cycle's deadline rolled forward.
description: Strathcona Resources awards ten $5,000 scholarships to Indigenous students from communities near its operations in Alberta and Saskatchewan, for post-secondary study or skilled trades training.
metaDetail: Ten awards, and no age limit.

title: APTA Student Bursary
audience: Piano students of Alberta Piano Teachers Association members
notes: Both you and your teacher write a letter, and the money goes to the teacher rather than to you. The Association does not publish an amount.
description: The Alberta Piano Teachers Association helps students of its members keep taking lessons when money is the obstacle. Interest and motivation matter more than how advanced you are.
metaDetail: Paid to your teacher, not to you.

title: Consort Agro Services Green Certificate Awards
audience: Altario and Consort grads of the Green Certificate program
notes: Both the number of awards and the amounts vary year to year, so the form states neither. Finishing the Green Certificate is the whole eligibility test.
description: Consort Agro Services backs graduates of the Green Certificate agriculture apprenticeship at Altario or Consort High School who are entering full-time study at an accredited institution.
metaDetail: Tied to the Green Certificate program.

title: Consort and District Chamber of Commerce Scholarship
audience: Prairie Land graduates from the Consort area
notes: The five year window means this is still open long after you graduate. An entrepreneurial streak is preferred, and the application covers your community involvement and proof of enrolment.
description: One $500 scholarship for a student living inside the Consort and District Chamber of Commerce boundaries who finished Grade 12 at a Prairie Land School Division school within the past five years and is enrolled in post-secondary.
metaDetail: Open up to five years after Grade 12.

title: Gail Watt Annual Scholarship in Human Services
audience: Flagstaff County students entering human services
notes: There is no age restriction, so former students returning to school qualify. The essay is what gets judged, and payment follows proof of admission. Applications go to the FFCS office in Killam.
description: A $500 scholarship for current and former students of Daysland, Sedgewick and Forestburg schools who are studying human services or community development.
metaDetail: No age limit, and former students count.

title: Cumberland Community Club Scholarship
audience: Delburne area students aged 18 to 21
notes: The money is handed over in September once you show proof of registration. Forms come from Delburne School or from the club by email.
description: The Cumberland Community Club gives $1,000 to a student aged 18 to 21 attending an Alberta institution. Applications submitted by May 31 are considered for the following school year.
metaDetail: Paid in September on proof of registration.

title: Hanna Knights of Columbus Bursary
audience: Hanna, Delia and Youngstown graduates
notes: J.C. Charyk students can apply every year, Delia students in even years and Youngstown students in odd years. Students in second through fourth year of post-secondary can also apply.
description: The Hanna Council of the Knights of Columbus picks two students a year for $500 bursaries. You need a 65 percent average and proof of post-secondary enrolment.
metaDetail: Delia and Youngstown alternate years.

title: Bottomley-Stuart-Blair and Hiltbrand Brothers Bursary
audience: Hanna area students with financial need
notes: Financial need is the main test rather than marks, which makes it worth applying for even with an average transcript. The form asks you to answer as fully as you can, and the amount is not published.
description: Royal Canadian Legion Branch 25 in Hanna administers this educational bursary for students from Hanna, Youngstown, Delia or Cessford who have been accepted into post-secondary.
metaDetail: Financial need outweighs marks.

title: Starland County Leaders of Tomorrow Scholarship
audience: Starland County residents entering post-secondary
notes: You pick one stream only. You cannot already hold a post-secondary credential or have won under this program before.
description: Starland County funds $1,000 scholarships in three streams: academic, agricultural and trades. You live inside the county boundaries and enrol at a recognized institution.
metaDetail: Pick one of three streams.

title: Islay Health Centre Auxiliary Bursary
audience: Vermilion River county students in health
notes: Residents of the towns of Vermilion, Marwayne and Kitscoty are excluded, so the award is aimed squarely at the rural county. You send proof of acceptance plus a personal and an educational reference.
description: The Islay Health Centre Auxiliary gives up to $1,000 a year to someone accepted into a health related post-secondary course who lives in the County of Vermilion River.
metaDetail: Three towns are excluded from the county.

title: Eckville Legion Branch 156 Bursary
audience: Descendants of Canadian Forces members near Eckville
notes: Community involvement and financial need are both weighed, and families of local branch members get consideration. The form asks for the service number of the family member who served. The amount is not published.
description: Legion Branch 156 in Eckville supports children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren of people who served honourably in the Canadian Forces, in an apprenticeship, college or university program.
metaDetail: Apprenticeships count alongside degrees.

title: Storwell Self Storage Foster Children Bursary Fund
audience: Former foster youth 24 and under entering full-time study
notes: You have to be 24 or younger and able to verify your care history. Kinship care, alternative living arrangements and Children's Aid Society involvement can all qualify. Enrolment has to start by the next semester.
description: Storwell funds a bursary for young people who have been in foster care in Canada or the United States and are starting full-time studies at a recognized institution.
metaDetail: Kinship care counts as foster care.

title: Jasper Park Community League Scholarship
audience: Jasper Park neighbourhood residents in Edmonton
notes: You need two consecutive years living there with address verification, and at least ten hours of league volunteering or another clear record of community service. Past recipients are considered only when two new applicants have not been funded.
description: The Jasper Park Community League in west Edmonton gives up to $1,000, normally as two awards, to residents of the neighbourhood between 87 and 92 Avenue and 149 and 156 Street who are entering or continuing post-secondary.
metaDetail: Ten hours of league volunteering.

title: NIEEF Indigenous Scholarships
audience: Indigenous students in business or community development
notes: You need a current Cando student membership, and students at Cando accredited institutions get priority. The application takes your marks or GPA, an essay, two academic references and a resume.
description: Cando awards six $3,000 scholarships to Indigenous students enrolled full time in business administration, economics, finance, management, natural resources or community economic development.
metaDetail: Needs a Cando student membership.

title: Mike W. Achtymichuk Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta middle, junior and high school music students
notes: This pays for extracurricular music learning rather than tuition, and the money goes straight to whoever provides it. You have to use it by June 1 after you win. The application needs a letter, evidence of need and support from a teacher or conductor.
description: Created by Joyce Howdle and Olga Achtymichuk, this $1,000 award helps an Alberta student in middle, junior or high school take their music further, through MusiCamp Alberta, private lessons or similar activities.
metaDetail: For lessons and camps, not tuition.

title: Fairview Health Professional Enhancement Committee Scholarship
audience: Fairview area students entering health programs
notes: High school students, students already in a program and adults considering a return can all apply, in person or online programs alike. The essay asks about your career plans and your commitment to working in the rural north. You may reapply each year.
description: Up to four $500 scholarships a year for people from Fairview, Hines Creek, the M.D. of Fairview No. 136 or Clear Hills County who are entering a medical, allied health, veterinary or animal health program, or the prerequisite training for one.
metaDetail: Online programs qualify too.

title: Mikisew Cree First Nation Student Services Sponsorship
audience: Mikisew Cree members in post-secondary study
notes: There are three intakes: July 30 for September, November 15 for January and April 1 for spring and summer. Apply through Student Services rather than a public form.
description: Mikisew Cree First Nation sponsors members attending university, college or other higher education through its Student Services department. How long you are funded depends on your program.
metaDetail: Three intakes across the year.

title: ACFN Education Grant
audience: Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation members in post-secondary
notes: You have to apply to Athabasca Tribal Council post-secondary funding first. Full-time students are preferred, continuing students come first and recent high school graduates next. Intakes close July 31, November 30 and March 31.
description: The Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation funds tuition and books for members accepted into accredited post-secondary programs, with living support in exceptional cases.
metaDetail: Apply to the Tribal Council first.

title: Fort McKay First Nation Post-Secondary Student Support Program
audience: Fort McKay First Nation members
notes: You cannot have outstanding debts to the Nation or your institution, and orientation is required. Intakes close July 1 for September, November 1 for January and April 1 for May or August.
description: Fort McKay First Nation covers tuition, books, technology, tutoring, supplies and qualifying living expenses for members in approved full-time programs, including upgrading.
metaDetail: Covers tutoring and technology too.

title: ManCap Foundation Education Grants
audience: Alberta grads entering post-secondary with a business in mind
notes: The Foundation states plainly that academic excellence is not a prerequisite and financial need is a criterion. You need an acceptance letter, two letters of recommendation and answers to their questions. Recipients are announced September 30.
description: The ManCap Foundation gives $5,000 grants, named for Alberta entrepreneurs, to Alberta high school graduates entering first year at a designated Alberta institution in preparation for starting a business.
metaDetail: Marks are explicitly not a requirement.

title: Evelyn Henry Reconciliation Scholarship
audience: Women in Alberta or Saskatchewan studying reconciliation
notes: Start a month or two before the April 1 date, because your recommendation has to clear a chapter first. You need two years of Alberta or Saskatchewan residency, a reference letter and an official transcript. The number and size of awards changes each year.
description: P.E.O. Alberta-Saskatchewan set up this fund in 2017 for a female student taking courses in Indigenous studies who plans to use that education to further reconciliation between Indigenous and non-Indigenous peoples in Canada.
metaDetail: A local chapter must recommend you.

title: Alex Schaap Memorial Scholarship
audience: Palliser School Division grads entering technology training
notes: The application is deliberately open-ended: you are asked to be creative and resourceful in showing why you qualify. Two references are required, and you need to be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident living in Alberta.
description: A $1,000 scholarship each year for a Palliser School Division graduate entering full-time first-year technology training at an accredited institution.
metaDetail: A creative application is invited.

title: Marit McKenzie Scholarship
audience: Palliser Regional grads entering fine arts
notes: You can answer with a short essay, a story, a video or a photography submission rather than a standard form.
description: A $1,000 scholarship for a Palliser Regional Schools graduate entering a full-time first-year fine arts degree or diploma at an accredited Alberta institution.
metaDetail: You can apply with a video or photos.

title: Tom Baldwin Memorial Scholarship
audience: Peace River constituency graduates
notes: The five year window means graduates who took time off still qualify. Applications go back through the school division with supporting documents.
