description: A $1,000 scholarship for an Alberta resident in the Peace River constituency who graduated within the past five years from the Peace River, Holy Family, Northwest Francophone, Fort Vermilion or Northland school divisions, and is in full-time study. The winner must agree to work in northern Alberta for at least two years and apply to the Northern Alberta Development Council bursary program.
metaDetail: Open five years after you graduate.

title: Early Childhood Scholarship
audience: Fairview area grads entering early childhood programs
notes: Experience working with young children counts alongside your marks and effort. The amount is small, so treat it as a top-up rather than a plan.
description: A $100 scholarship for a graduate of Fairview High, Hines Creek Composite, Worsley Central or St. Thomas More accepted into an accredited early childhood education degree or diploma.
metaDetail: Experience with children counts.

title: Tom and Alice Walker Memorial Bursary
audience: Fairview and Hines Creek area graduates with financial need
notes: The amount is not published and depends on what the fund earns. Applications go through the school division.
description: A bursary for a graduate of Worsley Central, Hines Creek Composite, Fairview High or St. Thomas More who has financial need, studies diligently and shows good citizenship, and is enrolled at an accredited Canadian institution.
metaDetail: The amount depends on the fund.

title: Whitelaw History Book Scholarship
audience: Fairview area grads from the Whitelaw districts
notes: It goes to the highest combined average across five subjects, and the school submits the candidate's name and marks to the division rather than you applying directly.
description: Proceeds from a local history book fund up to $500 a year for a graduate of Fairview High, St. Thomas More or Hines Creek Composite who lives in one of the rural districts the book covers and is continuing post-secondary.
metaDetail: Awarded on your five subject average.

title: West Meadowlark Memorial Scholarship
audience: West Meadowlark community league members in Edmonton
notes: You or your immediate family need to be league members and West Meadowlark residents for two consecutive years, and the league asks for five volunteer hours.
description: The West Meadowlark Community League funds two $500 scholarships for Grade 12 graduates who move straight into a post-secondary program lasting at least a year.
metaDetail: Two awards, tied to league membership.

title: Livingstone MacLeod Association Bursary Fund
audience: Livingstone Range graduates in trades or agriculture
notes: You write an essay and supply two references. The award moves around the division, so it is not tied to one school.
description: One $2,000 bursary a year within the Livingstone Range School Division for a graduate who needs support to take up eligible trades or agriculture studies.
metaDetail: Open across the whole division.

title: James Miller Bursary
audience: Northern Lights grads entering a welding apprenticeship
notes: Welding is the whole criterion, which makes the field narrow and the odds correspondingly better if it is your trade.
description: A $500 bursary for a Northern Lights Public Schools student in their graduating year who is entering a welding apprenticeship at a post-secondary institution.
metaDetail: Welding apprentices only.

title: Matthewson and Co Bursary Program
audience: Students from prairie communities under 5,000 people
notes: There is no age limit, so this is open to adults returning to school. The application runs through the 4-H Alberta website.
description: Two $500 bursaries for people from an Alberta, Saskatchewan or Manitoba community of fewer than 5,000 residents who have finished high school and are entering Canadian post-secondary or apprenticeship training.
metaDetail: Applications go through 4-H Alberta.

title: Bott Sisters Memorial Scholarship
audience: Caroline area farm students entering post-secondary
notes: Agriculture, culinary and fine arts studies are preferred, an unusual combination that widens who can realistically apply. Graduates from the previous year can still apply.
description: A $2,500 scholarship for a graduate of David Thompson, West Central, Caroline or Visions West Outreach who is active on a family farm, volunteers in the community and is enrolled for the coming year.
metaDetail: Farm work plus volunteering.

title: Next Step Legacy RAP Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 athletes entering a trade through RAP
notes: There are eight awards, one per zone, and the final value depends on the funds and who applies. Needing both RAP and school sports narrows the field considerably.
description: Awards of $1,000 to $2,000 for Grade 12 students heading into a trade who took part in the Registered Apprenticeship Program at some point in high school and played school sports.
metaDetail: Needs both RAP and school sports.

title: Burnt Lee Recreation Area Scholarship
audience: Students from the Burnt Lee area near Peace River
notes: The area is defined by township and range, the north half of Township 82 Range 1 W6 and all of Township 83 Ranges 1 and 2 W6, so check a county map if you are unsure. Effort and citizenship come first and financial need second.
description: A $400 scholarship for a first or second year post-secondary student who graduated from the Peace River, Holy Family Catholic or Grande Prairie Catholic divisions and has lived three years in the Burnt Lee area.
metaDetail: Second-year students qualify too.

title: Canadian Forest Products Scholarship
audience: Fairview area Grade 12 students continuing their education
notes: The essay is capped at 200 words, and you need two references, one from the school and one on your personal character, plus certified grades. Your principal submits it.
description: Canfor funds a scholarship for Grade 12 students at Fairview High, Worsley Central, Hines Creek Composite or St. Thomas More, judged on school and community involvement and what you plan to study.
metaDetail: The essay is capped at 200 words.

title: G3 Grow Beyond Scholarship
audience: Canadian high school graduates outside Quebec
notes: Four of the awards go to western Canadian students, which is unusually good odds for Alberta. The 2026 round closed in April, so watch for the next one to open in winter. You must be at your province's age of majority.
description: A grain company award for a graduating student entering a first-year Canadian degree or diploma, decided on a video about agricultural innovation and on community involvement.
metaDetail: Four of the awards are reserved for western Canada.

title: Petro Canada Fund Scholarship
audience: Drayton Valley and Brazeau County students in energy programs
localArea: Drayton Valley and Brazeau County students
notes: Applications are due June 1 each year. You have to be enrolled before the money is released. Because priority rather than residency is the rule, students from outside the county can still apply.
description: A community foundation award for a student entering studies that support an oil and gas career, with priority for Drayton Valley and Brazeau County families and for financial disadvantage.
metaDetail: Priority, not a hard rule, for local families.

title: Community Scholarship Trust Society Scholarship
audience: Drayton Valley area graduates within two years of high school
notes: You can apply up to two years after graduation, which covers a gap year. An Alberta high school diploma and proof of enrolment are both required. Outreach and home-schooled students are named explicitly.
description: An award for a former Frank Maddock, Breton, Holy Trinity, Drayton Valley Outreach or Home School Association student who is enrolled full-time in post-secondary study.
metaDetail: A gap year does not disqualify you.

title: Calgary Italian Sportswomen's Dinner Association Scholarship
audience: Female Grade 12 students of Italian descent in Calgary
notes: Five thousand dollars is large for a city award with this narrow a field. You must be registered for post-secondary in September. Sport achievement is weighed with the rest, not on its own.
description: A $5,000 award for a Calgary Grade 12 student of Italian descent with at least a 75 percent average and achievement in sport alongside academics, leadership and community activity.
metaDetail: Unusually large for an award this specific.

title: Calgary Italian Cultural Centre Scholarship
audience: Calgary area Grade 12 graduates of Italian descent
notes: The county catchment means rural students around Calgary qualify too. Applications are due at the end of September. The centre publishes the program in Italian and English, so read whichever version you find first carefully.
description: A cultural centre award for a graduate of Italian descent from Calgary, Foothills, Mountain View County or Rocky View County who is entering post-secondary within a year of graduating.
metaDetail: The catchment reaches well past the city limits.

title: ATA Battle River Local 32 Scholarship
audience: Children of Battle River teachers entering post-secondary
notes: Part-time teaching parents count, and so do retired ones and those on leave who keep paying the ATA leave fee. You have 18 months after Grade 12 to use it, and you apply before your program starts.
description: A teachers' local award for the child of a current, retired or on-leave Battle River teacher who is starting post-secondary study.
metaDetail: Retired and part-time teaching parents both count.

title: Clearwater Endowment Fund and SLS Recreation Park Society Scholarship
audience: Cochrane and Springbank area graduates
notes: The scoring is published as a 100-point rubric, so you can see where the marks come from before you write anything. Two awards at this size in one small catchment are good odds.
description: Two awards of $2,500 for graduating Cochrane area or Springbank students entering their first year of full-time post-secondary study, selected on a 100-point assessment.
metaDetail: The scoring rubric is published up front.

title: Foothills Natural Gas Co-op Achievement Award
audience: Foothills area students entering post-secondary
notes: The co-op posts the award but the linked application form did not load when we checked, so phone or email the office for a current copy rather than assuming the award has ended.
description: A co-op award of $500 for a student showing a clear commitment to entering post-secondary education, selected once a year.
metaDetail: Call the office; the online form did not load.

title: Pete Ketcham Memorial Scholarship
audience: Students from West Fraser operating communities
notes: The company hands out several each year across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom and Europe, so the field is wide but so is the number of awards. Living in a mill town is the qualifying fact.
description: Several annual $1,500 awards for post-secondary students from areas where West Fraser operates, including its Alberta mill communities.
metaDetail: Several awarded a year, not just one.

title: Obsidian Energy Energy Excellence Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in Obsidian Energy operating areas
notes: There is an interview, which is unusual at this level and worth preparing for. Your school division has to be one that serves an operating area, so ask your counsellor whether yours is on the list before you apply.
description: Three awards of $3,000 for Grade 12 students in school divisions serving Obsidian Energy operating areas who have at least an 80 percent average and acceptance into oil and gas related study.
metaDetail: An interview is part of the selection.

title: Bancroft Student Bursary
audience: Drumheller area students entering post-secondary
notes: The club's page states no residency restriction even though the bursary is administered in Drumheller, so students from nearby towns should ask rather than assume they are out. Character weighs as heavily as marks.
description: A Rotary bursary of $1,000 for a student who meets post-secondary entrance requirements and shows strong leadership, honesty and integrity.
metaDetail: Character weighs as heavily as marks here.

title: Edmonton Gymkhana Association Scholarship
audience: Students in horse sport entering post-secondary
notes: Five places means most serious applicants place somewhere. You need a tuition receipt for current studies, two dated references and an essay of at least 300 words. The September deadline suits students already enrolled.
description: Five ranked awards from $1,200 down to $400 for students accepted at an accredited post-secondary institution, decided on an essay covering goals and horse-related experience plus two references.
metaDetail: Five ranked places, from $1,200 down to $400.

title: Lance Yearley Scholarship
audience: Children of Quality Control Council members
notes: Union membership in your family is the gate here, so check your parent's local before anything else. Academics, extracurriculars and the written submission are all assessed. The July deadline is later than most graduation awards.
description: An award of up to $2,500 for the dependent child of a Quality Control Council member in good standing who is entering an accredited first-year diploma or degree program.
metaDetail: A parent's union membership is the gate.

title: Rugged and Real Scholarship
audience: Lesser Slave River area students
notes: Mature learners qualify alongside recent graduates, so there is no age cutoff to worry about. Three awards in a municipal district this small are good odds.
description: Up to three awards of $1,000 for students living within the Municipal District of Lesser Slave River who will attend post-secondary in the coming year.
metaDetail: Mature learners qualify alongside new graduates.

title: ACFN High School Graduation Incentive
audience: Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation members completing high school
notes: Where you live does not matter, only membership, so members outside the community qualify. There is no competition and no deadline: you apply after you graduate and send the diploma.
description: A one-time $1,000 incentive for a recognized Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation member who completes an Alberta high school diploma, paid on proof of the diploma.
metaDetail: Not a contest; graduate and claim it.

title: Fort McKay Alcor Aboriginal Trades Scholarship
audience: Graduating Indigenous students entering the trades
notes: The five named trades are the whole field, so check that your program is one of them. Two awards a year in the Wood Buffalo region makes the odds reasonable for students who qualify.
description: Two annual awards of $1,000 for graduating Indigenous students accepted into an accredited trade school for plumbing, refrigeration, electrical, millwright or carpentry.
metaDetail: Five named trades, two awards a year.

title: Future Generations Foundation Individual Funding
audience: First Nations post-secondary, trades and cultural learners
notes: Twenty thousand a year puts this among the largest awards a First Nations student in Alberta can apply for, and cultural learning counts as a stream alongside academic study. You must turn 18 during the calendar year. The 2026 round closed in June.
description: Funding of up to $20,000 a year for First Nations students in college or university, training and trades, or cultural learning, requiring First Nation membership or status and a valid social insurance number.
metaDetail: Cultural learning is a funded stream, not a footnote.

title: Small Town, Big Dreams Scholarship
audience: Young women from Drayton Valley and Brazeau County
localArea: Drayton Valley and Brazeau County students
notes: Grades are explicitly not the deciding factor, which is unusual. Applications are due June 1. Studying away from home is a requirement, so a student staying local does not qualify.
description: A $1,500 award for a female graduate aged 17 to 20 from Drayton Valley or Brazeau County who is studying away from home, weighing financial circumstances rather than grades.
metaDetail: Grades are explicitly not the deciding factor.

title: ATB BIPOC Business Administration Entrance Scholarship
audience: Incoming RDP Business Administration students who are Black, Indigenous or people of colour
notes: An entrance award, so you apply as you start rather than partway through. ATB funds a parallel award reserved for Indigenous students, and it is worth checking which fits you better.
description: A scholarship of $1,250 for an incoming full-time Red Deer Polytechnic Business Administration student who is Black, Indigenous or a person of colour, considering grades and financial need.

title: ATB Indigenous Business Administration Entrance Scholarship
audience: Incoming Indigenous RDP Business Administration students
notes: Reserved for Indigenous students entering the program, which makes the field much smaller than the general entrance scholarships. Apply in your first term.
description: A scholarship of $1,250 for an incoming full-time Indigenous Red Deer Polytechnic Business Administration student, considering grades and financial need.

title: ATB Financial Entrance Scholarship in Business Administration
audience: Incoming first-year RDP Business Administration students
notes: For students just starting the diploma. ATB runs a separate continuing scholarship for the jump into second year, so you can be considered twice over two years.
description: A scholarship of $1,000 for an incoming full-time first-year Red Deer Polytechnic Business Administration student, considering financial circumstances, grades and community service.

title: B.A. Bruce Snider Scholarship for Indigenous Students
audience: Incoming first-year Indigenous RDP students with financial need
notes: Six awards at $2,500 makes this the most generous entrance award for Indigenous students at the school. Cultural leadership is weighed alongside need.
description: Six scholarships of $2,500 for incoming full-time first-year Indigenous Red Deer Polytechnic students, considering financial circumstances and leadership supporting Indigenous culture.

title: Black Knight Inn University Transfer Scholarship
audience: Incoming RDP Commerce, Education, Science and Nursing students
notes: Four program streams share two awards, so check that yours is one of the named ones before applying.
description: Two scholarships of $750 for incoming full-time first-year Red Deer Polytechnic students in Commerce, Education, Science or Nursing, considering grades and financial circumstances.

title: Booth Family MusiCamp Scholarship
audience: MusiCamp Alberta registrants who need help attending
notes: This covers camp attendance rather than tuition, and the application is a straight case for why the money matters to you, your family and your musical development.
description: A scholarship of roughly $437 for a MusiCamp Alberta registrant at Red Deer Polytechnic, awarded on an explanation of how the funding would make attendance possible.
metaDetail: It pays for camp, not tuition.

title: Border Paving Entrance Bursary
audience: Incoming RDP students in any credit program with financial need
notes: Need is the only criterion and every credit program qualifies, which makes this the most broadly open of the $2,000 entrance awards at the school.
description: A bursary of $2,000 for an incoming full-time first-year student in any Red Deer Polytechnic credit program, selected on financial circumstances alone.

title: Border Paving Scholarship for Business
audience: Incoming RDP Bachelor of Business Administration students
notes: Two awards at $2,000 for students entering the business degree, judged on need as well as marks.
description: Two scholarships of $2,000 for incoming full-time first-year Red Deer Polytechnic Bachelor of Business Administration students, considering financial circumstances and grades.

title: Cochrane and Area Humane Society Scholarship
audience: Cochrane and Stoney Nakoda students in animal or human care
notes: Volunteering at the shelter is the qualifying work, so start well before your application year. Human care programs count too, not only veterinary ones.
description: A $1,000 scholarship for a Stoney Nakoda or Cochrane area high school student accepted into post-secondary human or animal care, health, medicine or education, requiring meaningful volunteer service with the society.
metaDetail: Shelter volunteering is the qualifying work.

title: Consort Lions Club Scholarship
audience: Consort and Altario students entering trades or short programs
notes: You need at least two high school years at Altario or Consort. Degree students are not the target here: shorter credentials and the trades are, which is the opposite of most academic awards.
description: A Lions Club award of $500 for a student entering a one-year certificate, two-year diploma or apprenticeship in Canada, with preference for technical and apprenticeship study.
metaDetail: Built for short programs, not degrees.

title: Pioneer Homestead Bursary
audience: Prairie Land graduates from Special Areas 2, 3 and 4
notes: Residence in one of the three Special Areas is a hard requirement and rules out most of the province. Financial need is weighed alongside the 70 percent average.
description: A bursary of $1,005 from the estate of Ruth Rushfeldt Curry for a Prairie Land graduate living in Special Areas 2, 3 or 4 who is entering first-year post-secondary with at least a 70 percent average in the named senior subjects.
metaDetail: Only the three Special Areas qualify.

title: KCSFE Academic Excellence Scholarship
audience: Red Deer and northern Alberta students with strong grades
notes: International students qualify, which is rare. Applications run through a Google Form and the closing date is published in the separate annual guidelines document rather than on the award page, so open that first.
description: A scholarship paying $1,000 to high school students and $2,000 to college and university students who live, or whose parents live, in Red Deer or farther north in Alberta.
metaDetail: International students qualify here.

title: KCSFE Volunteerism and Community Leadership Scholarship
audience: Red Deer and northern Alberta students who volunteer
notes: Grade 10 and 11 students can apply, so you do not have to wait for your graduating year. The closing date is in the annual guidelines document, not on the award page.
description: A scholarship paying $750 to high school students and $1,500 to college and university students in Red Deer and northern Alberta, awarded for volunteering and community leadership.
metaDetail: Open from Grade 10, not just Grade 12.

title: KCSFE Bursary
audience: Red Deer and northern Alberta students with financial need
notes: The three tiers mean this one award follows you from high school through a master's degree. International students qualify. The closing date is in the annual guidelines document.
description: A bursary paying $1,000 to high school students, $2,000 to undergraduates and $2,500 to graduate students who live, or whose parents live, in Red Deer or farther north in Alberta.
metaDetail: Three tiers, from high school to graduate study.

title: Fred and Muriel Lebold Scholarship
audience: IBEW Local 92 members and their families
notes: Any field of study qualifies and three awards are given, so a union family with more than one student can do well here. You need to be in good standing or enrolled for the coming semester.
description: Three awards of $3,000 for Local 92 members and their immediate family who are in their final year of high school or enrolled in post-secondary study, in any field.
metaDetail: Any field, three awards, union families only.

title: Ken Foster Memorial Scholarship
audience: Transit union members, their children and grandchildren
notes: Eight thousand dollars is among the largest amounts on this site. Grandchildren of members qualify, which widens the family net considerably, but anyone who has already attended college is excluded. The 2026 round closed March 31.
description: Five scholarships of $8,000 and a sixth of $2,000 from the Amalgamated Transit Union for members, their children, stepchildren and grandchildren entering an accredited college or a technical or vocational school for the first time.
metaDetail: Grandchildren of members qualify too.

title: Fairview Health Complex Foundation Scholarship
audience: Fairview and Hines Creek graduates in health care
notes: Any health care field counts, from nursing to lab technology. The application is short: a form plus a personal note of about a page. The November deadline is unusually late, so it catches students already in first term.
description: A $1,000 scholarship for a graduate of Fairview High School, St Thomas More or Hines Creek High School entering first-year study in any health care field.
metaDetail: A form and a one page note, nothing more.

title: North Peace Winter Games Legacy Scholarship
audience: North Peace graduates in arts, culture or sport programs
notes: The five year window means earlier graduates can still apply. Your program should point toward northern employment, which the application asks you to explain.
description: Awards of $500 for Alberta residents in North Peace communities who graduated locally within the past five years and are entering full-time study related to arts, culture or sport.
metaDetail: Graduates from the last five years qualify.

title: Grant Notley Memorial Scholarship
audience: Students from Grant Notley's former constituency
notes: The essay topic is fixed: how you hope to contribute to improving the quality of life in Alberta, in 500 to 1,000 words. Students whose parents live in the old constituency qualify even if they attend school elsewhere.
description: One $500 scholarship a year for a student at a high school in the Spirit River and Fairview constituency Grant Notley represented, or one of the named Berwyn, Grimshaw and Bonanza routes, decided on an essay and on Social Studies and English marks.
metaDetail: One fixed essay topic decides it.

title: Knowlton Family Rural Alberta HBA Award
audience: Rural Alberta students entering Western University
notes: This is the largest award on this site for a rural Alberta student. You need to enrol in Business 1220E, show interest in Ivey, and have competitive extracurricular experience. Renewal in second year needs a 70 percent average.
description: An award worth up to $30,000 over four years for a first-year Western University student from Alberta outside Calgary and Edmonton, paying $5,000 in each of years one and two and $10,000 in years three and four if the student continues into the Ivey Business School HBA program.
metaDetail: Up to $30,000 across four years.

title: Northern Lakes College Dual Credit Bursary
audience: Students who took a Northern Lakes College dual credit course
notes: Taking one dual credit course in high school is the whole qualification, which makes this close to automatic money for students who already did it. You have to continue at Northern Lakes to collect.
description: A $500 bursary for a student who completed a Northern Lakes College dual credit course in the previous academic year and then enrols in post-secondary studies at the college.
metaDetail: One dual credit course qualifies you.

title: Entwistle Scholarship at Guelph
audience: Black students and students of colour entering Guelph
notes: You have to be heading to Guelph, so this only helps an Alberta student moving to Ontario. Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons all qualify.
description: A $1,000 scholarship for a Black student or student of colour entering undergraduate studies in the University of Guelph College of Social and Applied Human Sciences, with preference for International Development Studies.
metaDetail: Only for students heading to Guelph.

title: Adam Richard Leinweber Entrance Scholarship
audience: Students entering physics at the University of Calgary
notes: Ten thousand dollars for one entering physics major is among the largest entrance awards at the university. Declaring Physics rather than general Science is what puts you in the running.
description: A $10,000 entrance scholarship for a first-year University of Calgary Science student majoring in Physics, awarded on academic achievement.
metaDetail: Declaring physics is what qualifies you.

title: 4-H Alberta Provincial Scholarships
audience: Past and present Alberta 4-H members going on to post-secondary
notes: One online application puts you in the running for every provincial scholarship on the list, and you can win one of them per year. Regional, district and club scholarships are extra and can be won in the same year as a provincial one, but several want an essay or reference letters sent by mail, so read each one's criteria before May. The application opens March 1 and closes May 1 at noon.
description: About seventy named scholarships run through one 4-H Alberta application, from $500 to $2,750 each, most of them for agriculture, veterinary, human ecology or agri-business programs and many limited to members from one county, district or region. Most ask for at least three years of 4-H membership and weigh community involvement and 4-H achievement.
metaDetail: One application covers about seventy awards.

title: Edmonton Music and Speech Arts Festival Scholarships
audience: Young musicians and speech arts performers entering the Edmonton festival
notes: There is no separate application: you enter festival classes, and scholarships go to the highest marks across a group of similar classes, at the adjudicator's decision. The 2026 festival's entry deadline was February 5; the 2027 date here is last year's rolled forward, so check the festival's site in January. Register in both the provincial syllabus and the local addenda.
description: The Edmonton Music and Speech Arts Festival, formerly the Edmonton Kiwanis Music Festival, awards dozens of named scholarships from $25 to $750 each spring in piano, voice, strings, speech arts and other disciplines, mostly within age brackets such as 13 to 15 or 13 to 18.
metaDetail: Won through festival marks, not an application.

title: Bourse André-Boudreau
audience: Francophone Alberta students in technology, innovation or leadership

Proof of enrolment for the coming academic year is required before payment, and only successful applicants are contacted, by July 31.
description: A $1,750 bursary from the Fondation franco-albertaine for francophone students living in Alberta whose studies or project involve new technologies, innovation and leadership.
metaDetail: For technology, innovation or leadership.

title: ACFA Rivière-la-Paix Bursaries for École Héritage and École des Quatre-Vents
audience: Grade 12 students at École Héritage and École des Quatre-Vents
localArea: École Héritage and École des Quatre-Vents students
notes: The Fondation franco-albertaine holds the fund, but the page sends you to the ACFA of Rivière-la-Paix and to the two schools for how to apply, so ask your school counsellor for the form and the date.
description: Three bursaries a year for Grade 12 students at École Héritage in Falher and École des Quatre-Vents in Peace River: the Saint-Isidore, des Compagnons and Alfred P. Canuel bursaries. The ACFA of Rivière-la-Paix ran them for years before moving them to the Fondation franco-albertaine in 2012; École des Quatre-Vents graduates have been eligible since 2020.
metaDetail: Three bursaries for two francophone schools.

title: Baseball Alberta Scholarships and Bursaries
audience: Baseball Alberta players heading to college or university
notes: Baseball Alberta names each year's recipients but does not post an amount, a form or a date, so ask your association or Baseball Alberta directly how nominations work before the season ends.
description: Five annual awards for Baseball Alberta players: the Carl Linden Bursary for a player who came up through the grassroots programs and showed heart and hustle overcoming obstacles; the Bob White Memorial and Doris Taylor scholarships for players with strong marks, community service and athletic ability; the Edmonton International Baseball Foundation's Ron Hayter Bursary for players working toward a degree; and the Mille Warwick McAuley / Betty Carvith Dunn Bursary for female players pursuing a university or college degree.
metaDetail: Five awards, recipients named every year.

title: Norris-Bowen Scholarship
audience: Students who self-identify with a disability, in any further education in East Central Alberta
notes: Applications for 2026 closed May 4, 2026. The 2027 date here is that deadline rolled forward a year, so confirm it on the association's page in the spring. Questions go to 780-672-0257.
description: Created by Muriel Rieger in memory of Franklin Waldo Norris and Jesse Bowen, the Camrose Association for Community Living awards $500 to a person who self-identifies with a disability and will take further education of any type in the East Central Alberta region.
metaDetail: Any kind of further education counts.

title: Gillespie Family Bursary
audience: Students with financial need studying disability services or a related field
notes: Applications for 2026 closed May 4, 2026. The 2027 date here is that deadline rolled forward a year, so confirm it on the association's page in the spring. Questions go to 780-672-0257.
description: Set up by Don Gillespie in memory of his wife Lois and now run by the Gillespie family with the Camrose Association for Community Living, this $1,800 bursary goes to a student in financial need who is studying in the disabilities field or a related area.
metaDetail: Financial need is required.

title: CAFCL Human Services Scholarship
audience: Students in disability studies, special education, psychology, sociology or nursing
notes: Applications for 2026 closed May 4, 2026. The 2027 date here is that deadline rolled forward a year, so confirm it on the association's page in the spring. Questions go to 780-672-0257.
description: The Camrose Association for Community Living awards $2,500 to a student in the disabilities field or a related area such as disability studies, special education, psychology, sociology or nursing.
metaDetail: Disability studies and related fields.

title: Calgary Calabrese Academic Scholarship
audience: Calgary-area graduates of Calabrese descent in academic post-secondary programs
notes: The 2026 application is closed and the society has not posted the next one, so this listing will not count down. Winners must attend the society's banquet in January, and proof of post-secondary registration is needed before payment.
description: The Calgary Calabrese Cultural and Heritage Society funds academic scholarships for students in the sciences, humanities, business and the arts. You must have family roots in Calabria, Italy, on either side, have finished Grade 12 at a high school in Calgary or the surrounding area in the year the form names, be enrolled in post-secondary, and be in good academic standing.
metaDetail: Family roots in Calabria are required.

title: Calgary Calabrese Technical Scholarship
audience: Calgary-area graduates of Calabrese descent in trades and technical training

description: The technical side of the Calgary Calabrese Cultural and Heritage Society's program, for students training in hands-on fields such as automotive, health care, construction and culinary work. The same rules apply: Calabrian family roots, Grade 12 finished in Calgary or the surrounding area, and post-secondary enrolment.
metaDetail: For trades, health care, culinary and more.

title: AMRIZE Education Endowment Scholarship

description: A Banff Canmore Community Foundation scholarship for students going on to post-secondary studies, focused on residents of Exshaw and Lac des Arcs.
metaDetail: Exshaw and Lac des Arcs residents first.

title: Marika Laub Memorial Scholarship
audience: Bow Valley residents chasing big goals
notes: Applications for this cycle are closed and the foundation has not set 2027 dates. It keeps a mailing list on the same page that emails you when applications open.
description: A Banff Canmore Community Foundation scholarship that supports Bow Valley individuals striving to achieve big dreams and to live inspirationally.
metaDetail: For Bow Valley residents.

title: Pembina West Co-op Scholarship Fund
audience: Grade 12 graduates in Pembina West Co-op communities
notes: Applications for 2026 closed June 10, 2026; the 2027 date here is rolled forward, so check the co-op's page in the spring. The co-op posts the form as a download and also takes applications online.
description: Pembina West Co-op awards two $1,000 scholarships a year to Grade 12 graduates in its communities who reflect the co-op's values of community, integrity and respect. You need two references from educators or community leaders who are not family, and a one to two page essay on your community involvement and goals. Students connected to the co-op through work or membership get preference, and you must be enrolled full time in a certificate, diploma or degree at an accredited Canadian college or university.
metaDetail: Two a year; co-op connection preferred.

title: Pembina West Co-op Youth Employment Initiative
audience: Grade 10 to 12 students working at Pembina West Co-op
notes: There is no application: the money builds up as you work. Ask Pembina West Co-op's human resources department to confirm how your hours are counted.
description: Students who work at Pembina West Co-op bank $0.50 for every hour worked toward a scholarship. It is open from Grade 10 to 12 to students working at least 520 hours a year between September and August, who are still employed there in their graduating year. The money can be claimed within one academic year after graduation with proof of full-time enrolment in a certificate, diploma or degree at an accredited Canadian college or university.
metaDetail: Banked from your paid hours.

title: GCAA High School Student Awards
audience: Alberta high school students aged 14 and up who volunteer with German cultural groups
notes: The 2026 deadline was March 31, 2026; the 2027 date here is rolled forward. Apply by mail, email or hand delivery to the GCAA at the German Cultural Club, and include signed, dated time sheets for your volunteer hours.
description: Up to six $250 awards a year from the German Canadian Association of Alberta for Alberta high school students aged 14 or older who have volunteered at least 15 hours with a German club in good standing with the association, or at a major event promoting German language and culture such as Heritage Days, German Days or Oktoberfest. The money is for curricular or extracurricular activities.
metaDetail: Fifteen volunteer hours at a German event.

title: GCAA Undergraduate and Diploma Scholarships
audience: First and second year Alberta post-secondary students who volunteer with German cultural groups
notes: The 2026 deadline was March 31, 2026; the 2027 date here is rolled forward. Apply by mail, email or hand delivery to the GCAA at the German Cultural Club, and include signed, dated time sheets for your volunteer hours.
description: Up to two $2,500 scholarships a year for Alberta residents who are Canadian citizens or permanent residents, entering the first or second year of full-time studies at a public university, college or technical institute in Alberta, with at least 25 hours of volunteering for a German organization or event and a history of volunteer work. Academic excellence is the main consideration; you need a non-family reference, transcripts and proof of enrolment.
metaDetail: Twenty-five volunteer hours required.

title: An Elnora Lorraine (Sandham) Riddle Nursing Entrance Scholarship
audience: Rural Alberta students entering first-year Nursing at the University of Alberta
notes: Selection is on your admission average. The award page listed a deadline of 01/10/2026, which the University of Alberta's award system writes month first; the 2027 date here is that one rolled forward, so check the page when you apply for admission.
description: Endowed by Dr. James Dean Sandham, this University of Alberta entrance scholarship goes to a rural Alberta resident entering the first year of an undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Nursing, on the basis of superior academic achievement.
metaDetail: For rural Albertans entering Nursing.

title: Joudrey Bursary
audience: Birch Hills County residents entering university, college or a trade
notes: Applications open January 1 and close April 30 each year; the policy also mentions a May 31 form date, so apply by the earlier one. Send it to reception@birchhillscounty.com, in person at the county office in Wanham, or by mail. You need a 150-word essay on how the award will affect your access to education, confirmation from your school that you are on track to graduate, and your acceptance letter.
description: Birch Hills County Council awards this bursary each year to residents entering a university, community college or technical or trades program, with preference to students heading into social services, health care or mental health. Home-schooled students qualify with proof of diploma equivalency, and you cannot have received it before.
metaDetail: Council awards it in full each year.

title: Trevor H. Shirtliff Difference Maker Scholarship

description: Canadian School Counsellor Magazine awards this scholarship, in memory of its founder, three times a year to students their counsellor nominates for working to improve life for themselves, their peers and their community. Selection weighs academic achievement, integrity, leadership and creativity, and it suits students in their final year of high school.
metaDetail: Counsellor nomination only.

metaDetail: Two awards a year.

title: ICAE Youth Essay Competition

description: The Igbo Cultural Association of Edmonton's essay competition, held with its Biafra Heroes Memorial Celebration, asks for 500 to 1,000 words on a topic set by level; in 2026 high school students wrote on the role of youth in preserving cultural memory in the diaspora. Winners are recognized at the celebration and receive educational awards from the Biafra Heroes Memorial Scholarship Fund.
metaDetail: An essay of 500 to 1,000 words.

title: Charlie Fielding Memorial Bursary

description: A Royal Canadian Legion Branch #25 bursary for former students of J.C. Charyk Hanna School, Berry Creek Community School, Youngstown School or Delia School who have been accepted into the Canadian Armed Forces, the RCMP, a municipal police service, a paramedic program or professional firefighter training. Community service and financial need are considered.

description: The Edmonton Epilepsy Association's life enhancement scholarships, up to $500 each, help young people up to age 18 take part in arts and cultural activities that build their development as individuals.
metaDetail: Open all year; for arts activities.

title: Gino Castellan Memorial Foundation Scholarship
audience: Graduating student-athletes who played high school sports in Central Alberta
notes: The 2026 poster asked for the class of 2026 by April 30, 2026; the 2027 date here is rolled forward. Everything goes in one PDF by email to ginocastellanmemorial@gmail.com, and a reference letter from a coach is required.
description: Four scholarships of $750 a year for graduating student-athletes who played high school sports in Central Alberta, have been accepted to a post-secondary institution, and show leadership in and out of sport, good citizenship and commitment to growing in their sport. You send a one to two page letter on how sport has shaped you and how you have given back, a list of your high school sports, a community involvement summary and proof of acceptance.
metaDetail: Four awards; a coach reference is required.

title: MADD Red Deer & District Mary Williams Award
audience: Red Deer area graduates affected by impaired driving, or active advocates against it
notes: The application form does not give a date, so ask MADD Red Deer & District or your counsellor for the current one. Proof of the injury and its link to an impaired driving crash is required, and advocacy applicants need written confirmation from a counsellor and from administration or another credible source.
description: One $500 award for a student graduating from high school this calendar year and going on to an accredited post-secondary institution, who lives within MADD Red Deer & District boundaries and was severely injured, or had a parent, guardian or sibling killed or severely injured, in an impaired driving crash. Students who have been active advocates against impaired driving, such as founding or belonging for two years to a SADD chapter, can also apply.
metaDetail: One award a year.

title: Provost & District Chamber of Commerce Scholarship
audience: Graduates of Provost Public, Saint Thomas Aquinas and Hughenden Public schools
notes: Applications for the class of 2026 closed April 10, 2026; the 2027 date here is rolled forward. The money is released once post-secondary registration is verified, and you need two letters of reference.
description: The Provost & District Chamber of Commerce gives $250 each year to one graduate at each of Provost Public School, Saint Thomas Aquinas and Hughenden Public School who plans to study business management, community development, the trades or agriculture, volunteers and is involved in the community.
metaDetail: One award at each of three schools.

title: Crossfield Agricultural Society Student Bursary
audience: High school graduates going on to post-secondary, with 4-H members welcome

description: The Crossfield Agricultural Society's bursary for that year's high school graduates heading to post-secondary in the fall. You write at least 150 words on yourself, your education, why you chose your field and what you hope to achieve, and highlight volunteering, clubs, community activities and any barriers you face in the move to post-secondary. The form asks about 4-H membership, and proof of acceptance and registration is required.
metaDetail: A 150-word essay and proof of acceptance.

title: The Jack Siebenga Memorial Scholarship
audience: GLDC Gas Co-op members and their children entering first year of post-secondary

description: G.L.D.C. Gas Co-op awards two $1,000 scholarships a year, one named for Jack Siebenga, to gas customers in good standing in its franchise area, or their children, who are entering the first year of a university, college or trade school. Community involvement, academic commitment and interest in rural development or energy are preferred, and each student can win only once.
metaDetail: Two a year; co-op members and families.

title: KCSFE Arts and Sports Scholarship

notes: Apply online through the Google Form linked on the page after reading the year's guidelines, which set the deadline; paper applications are not accepted. You can win KCSFE awards up to five times in total: twice in high school, twice in university or college, and once in graduate school.
description: The Korean Canadian Scholarship Foundation of Edmonton awards $1,000 to high school students and $2,000 to university or college students, chosen 80% on artistic or athletic ability or potential and 20% on academics. It is open to all backgrounds, including permanent residents and international students, who are full-time in Grade 10 to 12 or an undergraduate program (majoring in arts or sports at that level) and live, or have parents who live, in Edmonton or elsewhere in Alberta from Red Deer north.

title: Trevor Vance Memorial Scholarship

You do not need to be in an agriculture program.

title: Stringam Law Scholarship

title: ATA Local 3 Scholarship

metaDetail: Listed by Iron Ridge Secondary Campus in Blackfalds; for future teachers.

title: Rosalind Elks Scholarship

metaDetail: Two awards, paid in two parts.

title: Town of Didsbury High School Scholarship
audience: Graduating high school students who live in the Town of Didsbury
notes: The 2026 deadline was April 27 at 3:30 p.m., at the Didsbury High School office or by email; the 2027 date here is rolled forward. Letters from relatives, school staff or classmates are not accepted, and you have until September 2028 to show full-time enrolment and claim the money.
description: A $2,000 award from the Town of Didsbury for residents in their final year of high school who are in good academic standing and show community and school spirit, extracurricular involvement, leadership and a record of volunteering in Didsbury. Questions go to the scholarship coordinator at scholarships@sperd.ca.
description: St. Paul Education's own booklet of about fifty local awards, from $200 to $1,500. It includes four County of St. Paul scholarships of $1,000 each for academic, agriculture, health care and trades students, the Sobeys and Empire and Maria Samoil-Marchak scholarships ($1,500), Tim Hortons, Lakeland Family Eyecare, Saik Insurance, St. Paul Fish & Game, Lions Club, Greg Flondra, Ruth Bateyko, E.H. Bjornstad and Steve Kuziw awards ($1,000), the JMD Accounting Scholarship for future CPAs, and local sports awards from minor hockey, karate and football.

title: Aspen View Public Schools Grade 12 Academic Award
audience: Grade 12 graduates of Aspen View Public Schools
notes: No application: the school sends the list of qualifying students to the division, and the cheque comes with a letter from your trustee at the school's awards ceremony. The rules come from the division's June 2021 procedure, reprinted in Boyle School's current awards package.
description: Every Aspen View Public Schools Grade 12 student with an average of 80% or more gets $300, and 90% or more gets $500. The average uses your best Grade 12 marks across at least 25 credits, including five in English, taken at a division school; Special Projects and Work Experience do not count, and you must finish your diploma by June.
metaDetail: Automatic at 80% or 90%.

title: Pembina Hills Grade 12 Citizenship Award
audience: Grade 12 students at Pembina Hills high schools
notes: Apply online or on paper; the division says to check your school handbook or ask your principal for the deadline. Each school's selection committee picks its winners, and a trustee presents the award at the school's ceremony.
description: Pembina Hills School Division gives nine $500 citizenship awards to Grade 12 students each year: two at Barrhead Composite, two at R.F. Staples, two for Vista Virtual School primary students, and one each at Barrhead Outreach, Swan Hills School and Westlock Outreach. Your application shows how you meet at least three criteria such as responsibility, helping others, honesty, kindness and dependability.
metaDetail: Nine awards across six schools.

title: Ellen E. Thompson Scholarship
audience: Grasslands Public Schools graduates with financial need
notes: Applications go to the Grasslands central office by June 1, and winners hear by June 30. The form is in the Bassano School scholarship handbook; other Grasslands high schools can tell you where to get it.
description: Two $3,000 scholarships each year for Grasslands Public Schools graduates going to a recognized post-secondary school. Financial need is the main test, judged the way Alberta student aid does it: your family's last two tax returns, the number of dependent children and how many are already in post-secondary.

title: John Wass Smidstrup Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 graduates of County of Newell high schools
notes: No application: the award goes on marks and is given in the fall after graduation.
description: Two $1,000 scholarships each year, one to a male and one to a female graduate of a County of Newell high school, for the highest average (blended marks for diploma courses) across five subjects from the award's list. Both winners must be going on to a recognized post-secondary school.
metaDetail: Awarded on your best five subjects.

title: James Nesbitt Sr. Memorial Scholarship for Journalism
audience: Grasslands Public Schools graduates studying journalism, communications or English
notes: Due June 1. The Bassano School handbook lists it with the Grasslands division awards.
description: One $500 scholarship each year for a Grasslands Public Schools graduate going into journalism, communications or English, with at least a 70% average in Grade 12 courses.

title: Glen Keeley Memorial Scholarship
audience: Students who attended school in Claresholm, Stavely or Nanton
notes: The school lists the deadline only as mid to end of July, so the date here is an estimate; confirm it with Willow Creek Composite High School.
description: Four $2,000 scholarships for Canadian citizens living in Alberta who attended school in Claresholm, Stavely or Nanton for at least a year and are registered at any post-secondary school, including technical and trade schools. You need good standing in Grade 12 or your last post-secondary year, plus leadership, community spirit and extracurricular involvement.
metaDetail: Four awards; one year in Claresholm, Stavely or Nanton.

title: Carmangay Lions Club Legacy Scholarship
audience: Graduates living in the Carmangay area
notes: Due September 15, after graduation. Willow Creek Composite High School lists it with its fall scholarships.
description: A $500 scholarship for a student who lives in the Carmangay area when they finish high school and is registered at a post-secondary school. You describe your community service, volunteering and leadership.
metaDetail: Applied for in the fall after graduation.

title: The King's University Admission Scholarships
audience: High school graduates admitted to The King's University in Edmonton
notes: No separate application: you are considered when you apply for admission on high school marks. The money is paid half in the fall and half in the winter, applied to tuition, and you need at least 12 credits a term.
description: Every new student admitted to The King's University on high school marks is considered automatically: a final Grade 12 average of 80% to 89% earns the $2,000 Honours Scholarship and 90% or more earns the $3,000 Academic Distinction Scholarship. The Leder School of Business adds $3,000 and $2,000 to the two incoming business students with the highest entrance marks.
metaDetail: Automatic at 80%; $3,000 at 90%.

title: The King's University Competitive Awards for Incoming Students
audience: Grade 12 students starting at The King's University
notes: Applications for King's competitive awards open February 1, 2027 and close March 26, 2027; music awards that need a performance video are due before March 31. The awards page filters by program and year of study and gives each award's criteria.
description: About forty King's awards take applications from incoming high school students, usually needing an 80% entrance average for scholarships or financial need for bursaries. They include the Boessenkool Scholarship (twelve at $2,000 for commerce), the Cook/Mahaffy Bursary ($4,000), Computronix computing science awards ($1,000 to $3,000), environmental studies awards from $500 to $2,000, the King's Awareness Scholarship ($2,000, renewable, for students from a Canadian high school that has not sent anyone to King's in two years), music scholarships that ask for a video, and several awards that ask for a statement of Christian commitment.
metaDetail: One window: February 1 to March 26.

title: GLC Solutions Women in Business Scholarship
audience: Women entering or in the Bachelor of Commerce at The King's University
notes: Apply in King's competitive awards window, February 1 to March 26, 2027.
description: One $4,000 scholarship each year from GLC Solutions for a full-time female student, incoming or returning, in the four-year Bachelor of Commerce at The King's University. You need an 80% high school entrance average or a 3.30 GPA, and a written statement of Christian commitment, career intent and volunteer experience; marks and the statement are weighed together.
metaDetail: Needs an 80% entrance average.

title: GLC Solutions Women in Technology Scholarship
audience: Women entering or in Computing Science at The King's University
notes: Apply in King's competitive awards window, February 1 to March 26, 2027.
description: One $4,000 scholarship each year from GLC Solutions for a full-time female student, incoming or returning, in the four-year Bachelor of Science with a major in Computing Science at The King's University. You need an 80% high school entrance average or a 3.30 GPA, and a written statement of Christian commitment, career intent and volunteer experience.
metaDetail: Needs an 80% entrance average.

title: Keyano College Program Entrance Scholarships
audience: Students entering first year full time at Keyano College
notes: No application: the Office of the Registrar picks recipients from entering students' marks, and entrance scholarships are paid half in the fall and half in the winter.
description: Keyano's Registrar awards entrance scholarships on marks to new full-time students: Keyano College Entrance Scholarships ($1,200), four Syncrude Canada scholarships ($1,750 each) for the top entrants to the Bachelor of Education, Bachelor of Science, Business Administration and Bachelor of Science in Nursing, and three $500 Lamb family scholarships for entrants to nursing, the Bachelor of Commerce and Business Administration.
metaDetail: Chosen by the Registrar on your marks.

title: Canadian Baptist Theological Seminary and College Scholarships
audience: Students admitted to CBT's college or seminary programs in Cochrane
notes: Apply once a year through the Populi student system before the school year starts, or before the Winter semester if you start in January. Most awards need admission to a program and at least two courses that semester, and returning students need a 2.3 GPA.
description: Canadian Baptist Theological Seminary & College funds more than twenty scholarships through one yearly application, most paid per credit hour: from $50 a credit for named scholarships up to $250 a credit for the Barnabas Scholarship (new students nominated by a CNBC or SBC church) and for ministry leaders on staff at a CNBC church. Others cover dependents of CNBC, CBT and IMB staff, spouses of CBT students, former missionary volunteers, and students planning missions, pastoral, children's or religious education ministry.
metaDetail: Most students get at least one; one yearly form.

targetInstitutions: Canadian Baptist Theological Seminary and College

title: Northwestern Polytechnic Awards
audience: Students entering or attending Northwestern Polytechnic in Grande Prairie
notes: The awards listing filters by type (bursaries, entrance, Indigenous, leadership, fine arts, year-end) and by program, and each award says whether you apply or are selected. Several NWP awards also have their own listings here.
description: Northwestern Polytechnic's awards listing holds about 350 awards, with more than $350,000 a year in scholarships and bursaries: entrance awards such as the Alberta Blue Cross awards for students with 80% in English 30 and four other 30-level courses, bursaries for financial need, and program awards for power engineering, automotive, millwright, animal health technology, education and athletics, from a few hundred dollars to $2,000.
metaDetail: About 350 awards in one searchable list.
